Minutes after Warren Zaire-Emery entered the fray and was tasked with dealing with him, the Barcelona superstar blazed past the PSG substitute and prodded the ball past Safonov at his near post. Zaire-Emery's misery would then turn to relief only two minutes later when Vintinha hit an audacious effort from the edge of Barca's box, and the ball nestled into the back of the net past the sprawling Joan Garcia.

After Fabian Ruiz's clincher, it was another statement win for the holders but also highlighted their imperfections. PSG's night was blotted by an injuries to three of their best players - Ousmane Dembele, Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

‌



At the Etihad, City took an early lead against AEK Athens through Elliot Anderson, who had a tap-in after Enzo Fernandez's free-kick hit the crossbar. Enzo Maresca's side doubled their lead when Phil Foden played a neat one-two with Rico Lewis and fired home.

AEK threatened a comeback shortly after the break when Stavros Pilios scored, but Cherki made it 3-1 just five minutes later. It then turned into the Foden show, as the City star grabbed a hat-trick in a 5-1 battering.

‌



Who'll win the Champions League? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 3 Images Phil Foden grabbed a hat-trick as Manchester City won 5-1 (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

‌



It was less straightforward for Liverpool, who came from 2-0 down to beat Villarreal. An error from Virgil van Dijk allowed the La Liga side to go in front with four minutes on the clock before Sergi Cardona quickly made it two.

But a brace from Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo's header flipped the game on its head. Florian Wirtz then grabbed a much-needed goal to make it 4-2 before a consolation effort from the visitors. It ended 4-3, as Liverpool followed PSG by making it three wins from three games in the Champions League.

‌



In the early kick-offs, Borussia Dortmund survived a scare to claim a 2-1 win away to Sabah. Fenerbahce, meanwhile, failed to convert their fast start and threw away a two-goal lead against Slavia Prague, who picked up their first point of the campaign as the league table starts to take shape.

Later on, Napoli and Bodo/Glimt played out a seven-goal thriller, with the Italians coming out on top to win 4-3. Roma were also big winners against Slovan Bratislava, hammering them 4-0.

‌



PSV also snatched a narrow 1-0 victory at Porto thanks to Guus Til's goal. And in Germany, the points were shared as Stuttgart drew 1-1 with Atletico Madrid, who played the final half-hour with 10 men.

Sports.content:
Michael Carrick rules five stars out of Como clash as Man Utd boss issues injury update

Lisandro Martinez and Marcus Rashford were among the players to miss Manchester United's final training session before facing Como in the Champions League on Wednesday

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is missing a huge chunk of his squad (Image: Matt McNulty/Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has provided an update on five Manchester United players who've all been ruled out of Wednesday's clash with Como. Lisandro Martinez, Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw, Ayden Heaven and Marcus Rashford all missed the Red Devils' final training session at Carrington before flying out to Italy.

Carrick was already without Patrick Dorgu, Benjamin Sesko and Manuel Ugarte due to long-term injuries, while Leny Yoro is suspended following his red card against Atletico Madrid last time out in the Champions League. "Licha is not too bad but he's not with us. We'll have to see if he's ready for the weekend," Carrick told reporters. "Kobbie were looking at another 10 days or so. Luke a little bit longer than that.

"A little bit of injury and illness in the camp. Ayden is ill and Marcus is still feeling a hip issue we're trying to overcome."

Sports.title: Frenkie de Jong's 'dream' transfer remark, wife dropping hint and Man Utd U-turn
Sports.content:
Frenkie de Jong's 'dream' transfer remark, wife dropping hint and Man Utd U-turn

How Erik ten Hag's hopes of bringing Frenkie de Jong to Manchester United failed to materialise

View 2 Images Erik ten Hag was desperate to sign Frenkie de Jong for Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

The early months of Erik ten Hag's Manchester United reign were littered with talk of Frenkie de Jong joining the club. Having worked together at Ajax between 2017 and 2019 - and given United's need for midfield reinforcement - it was easy to see why Ten Hag wanted to sign the Barcelona and Netherlands star.

‌



‌



With Barca eager to get him off the wage bill amid a round of cost-cutting at the Nou Camp, it seemed a case of when, not if, he would arrive at Old Trafford. But despite extensive talks, arranged by Ten Hag himself, United couldn't get a deal for De Jong over the line.

‌



Having rebuilt his relationship with Barca, he has gone on to become a lynchpin for the Catalans, with almost 300 appearances to his name. Meanwhile, Ten Hag has been left wondering what might have been had he joined United in 2022.

‌



Here's a look back on United's pursuit of De Jong and why it never became a reality…

Erik ten Hag blasts Cristiano Ronaldo and reveals real reason for Man Utd bust-up READ MORE :

Erik ten Hag slams Man Utd for breaking promises and 'embarrassing' Scott McTominay transfer READ MORE :

Dream transfer

Thanks to Johan Cruyff - the Barca great as a player and manager - the Nou Camp club carries a mystique for Dutch footballers. That certainly applied to De Jong, who called his 2019 move from Ajax a dream come true.

Upon his arrival, he said: "I'm very excited about signing for Barca. I was very happy when I took the decision. I celebrated with my family, but not too much because we're still halfway through the season with Ajax.

‌



"But I'm very happy. I've always dreamed about playing for Barca since I was little. I like the players and the club. It's the team of my dreams. I want to be an important player for Barcelona and win many trophies."

View 2 Images De Jong's determination to stay at Barcelona has paid off (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Wife's hint

Three years into his spell in Spain, that dream threatened to turn into a nightmare as the club looked to cut costs by getting their highest earner off the wage bill. There was even talk of Barca taking legal action against De Jong after he declined to take a pay cut.

‌



With United and Chelsea interested in signing him, many players would have happily headed for the exit door but De Jong was determined to stay and live out his dream. That feeling was shared by his then-girlfriend, now wife, Mikky Kiemeney, who made it clear where she saw their future.

With speculation peaking, she posted a video on Instagram of the couple in their car and wakesurfing and wrote: "Meanwhile... living our best life." She captioned another clip: "Found another gem in Catalunya." More than four years on from the saga, she continues to share pictures of her and her family enjoying life in the city.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

United U-turn

Despite that, it seems De Jong did at least consider joining United, holding talks with Ten Hag, chief executive Richard Arnold and football director John Murtough before opting to stay put.

‌



In his recent interview with The Athletic, Ten Hag insisted he did everything he could to make it happen, saying: "Everyone's thinking the manager is doing the negotiations, that I'm involved in financial issues, but I was never.

"Of course, I did my best. I set up meetings with him, where it was Richard and John involved as well, to pursue him to come over. He could have been very important building the team, not only that year but for the future. But we didn't make it."

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd star makes Michael Carrick U-turn and names ideal Old Trafford replacement
Sports.content:
Ex-Man Utd star makes Michael Carrick U-turn and names ideal Old Trafford replacement

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick is a man under the cosh and Dwight Yorke, who had backed the ex-player, believes giving him the Old Trafford job may have been the wrong call

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is a man under pressure with one win in seven games to start the Premier League season (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Former Manchester United star Dwight Yorke admits he will "hold his hands up" and concede that appointing Michael Carrick perhaps wasn't the right call - despite backing him initially.

‌



‌



The ex-Middlesbrough boss came in to steady the ship in January and enjoyed a stunning interim period, which saw United rise up to third place in the Premier League and return to the Champions League. Those exploits landed him the job on a permanent basis.

‌



However, he's found things much tougher this season and Carrick has now presided over the worst start in 40 years with United winning one of their seven league games thus far and being dumped out of the Carabao Cup.

‌



The pressure is very much on the United boss, who had the backing of several former players last season. United's desire to stick by a manager is clear following several poor calls by the hierarchy, but Yorke is no longer convinced he's the man for the job.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He told Keys & Gray Unleashed: "That (sacking managers) is the current trend, isn’t it? It’s been the trend for the last five years: you get the manager, you say you’re going to back them and then at some point you end up getting rid of them,’ the former Trinidad and Tobago international went on. Obviously that is something that’s been in the DNA certainly for the past five years.

"Putting my hands up, I was one that said give Carrick the chance, but then I look back at it now, see what we’re doing, and I’m not sure if that was the right decision."

‌



"These guys are brilliant guys when you meet them and you know them like I have done. They’re brilliant. I’m not sure they’re made for managerial jobs when the pressure is on. Like anything else, when the going is good then it’s fantastic. When it’s not so good, I’m not so sure. I’ve seen it with Ole [Gunnar Solskjaer] and I’ve seen it with Carrick."

View 2 Images Dwight Yorke is no longer convinced by Michael Carrick (Image: Matthew Peters/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



United have tried several different types of managers over the past decade. They've gone after proven big names, up and coming talents and ex-players - none of whom have worked out.

Antonio Conte is being linked with the job but Yorke admits he's consider going after Eddie Howe, who left Newcastle in the summer after several successful years.

Article continues below

He said: "Who is out there? Howe would be one of those guys who stand out out there at the moment. He’s not in a job, looking for a job. But if you expand it out there even more, who else is out there? There is nobody else and that’s why Carrick will survive for a little bit longer. There are no top managerial candidates out there who can come in and really excite the people and the fans at Manchester United."

Sports.title: Erik ten Hag blasts Cristiano Ronaldo and reveals real reason for Man Utd bust-up
Sports.content:
Erik ten Hag blasts Cristiano Ronaldo and reveals real reason for Man Utd bust-up

Cristiano Ronaldo quit Manchester United after a bust-up with Erik ten Hag, and the club's former manager has now blasted him four years on from their public row

View 2 Images Erik ten Hag has spoken out on what went wrong with Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United (Image: ANP, ANP via Getty Images)

Cristiano Ronaldo let Manchester United down by not being fit enough during the final months of his second stint at Old Trafford, according to Erik ten Hag. The club's former manager claims that he pulled out of training sessions and did not work for the team or sufficiently prepare to run during matches.

‌



‌



Ronaldo left United by mutual consent in November 2022, months after Ten Hag took charge. He said at the time that his manager did not respect him.

‌



Four years later, the Dutchman has shared his version of events. He recalls challenging Ronaldo about his lack of professionalism.

‌



Ten Hag has told The Athletic: "I confronted him with this. Many times I say, 'Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can't bring yourself in the box, you can't score'.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"He was not capable to do this. It's the wrong idea to put this to me that I expected him to do the pressing, that he's exhausted. But he couldn't. He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was because he didn't prepare himself. Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team.

"He was telling the players, 'Save your legs at the training'. I understand it when you are top fit; you have sessions, you can save the legs. But first you have to train yourself to get into the right fitness levels."

‌



Ronaldo said in an interview with Piers Morgan Uncensored days before his departure was eventually announced: "I don't have respect for him (Ten Hag) because he doesn't show respect for me."

He added on the same subject: "If you don't have respect for me, I'm never gonna have respect for you. Not only the manager, but the other two or three guys who are around the club.

‌



View 2 Images Ten Hag and Ronaldo rarely saw eye to eye (Image: Matthew Ashton - AMA, Getty Images)

"I felt betrayed. I don't care; people should listen to the truth. Yes, I felt betrayed. I feel that some people didn't want me here, not only this year but last season too."

‌



Ten Hag has also addressed fresh criticism from Fred, who opened up on the Charla Podcast, saying: "Ten Hag was tactically very good, but with the group he was a piece of c***. He argued with everyone. He argued with me, with Cristiano [Ronaldo], with Casemiro, with [Marcus] Rashford... he wouldn't put me in to play; sometimes it got stressful.

"Only his Dutch players played. A clique-ridden coach. But, tactically, one of the best I've ever worked with. He wanted the team to run, but Cristiano [was] older. He took Cristiano out, and then there was a falling out."

Article continues below

Ten Hag said: "I'm not mad at Fred. You fight with your players when they are showing inefficient and unprepared standards. But it's always with respect. You want to push them; you want to get the best out of them."

Green made a go-ahead 3, Duren added a three-point play and Duncan Robinson connected on a 3 to put the Pistons ahead 107-99 with 5:10 to go.

Sports.title: Hat-trick hero Foden shines as Man City thrash AEK Athens
Sports.content:
Phil Foden bagged a hat-trick as dominant Manchester City cruised to a 5-1 win over AEK Athens to claim their second Champions League victory of the campaign.

Foden had waited 10 months for a goal before four arrived in back-to-back outings, adding to his strike against Ipswich at the weekend with three tidy finishes, the first two from Rico Lewis assists.

Man City had far too much quality for their Greek visitors despite leaving Erling Haaland in the stands, with Enzo Maresca allowing 17-year-old Floyd Samba to deputise in his place. Maresca proved his point in doing so: City have many other means of scoring beyond Haaland.

Elliot Anderson was also on target in a dominant first half that included 10 efforts on Alberto Brignoli's goal, with Allan striking the crossbar and Rayan Cherki going close.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Anton Toloui provides insight on three things we learnt from Manchester City's dominant Champions League performance against AEK Athens

Man City on a roll This was Man City’s 10th win in 12 matches in all competitions this season (L2) – of sides in Europe’s big-five leagues, only Barcelona have won more (11).

AEK failed to land a shot on target until Stavros Pilios pulled a goal back early in the second period. But their hope was short-lived. Cherki scored City's third five minutes later to kill any suggestion of a comeback and Foden issued another timely reminder of his class by completing a statement hat-trick.

The last time Foden scored three times in the same game was April 2024. It's felt like a lifetime since the City Academy graduate, a known favourite of Pep Guardiola, was anywhere near his dazzling best. His latest display was somewhere close to perfect.

The key moments from the Etihad

12: GOAL! Anderson steers home the rebound from Enzo Fernandez' free-kick for his first club goal.

23: CROSSBAR! Allan crashes a fierce effort off the woodwork as City threaten again.

34: GOAL! Foden combines neatly with Lewis and stabs beyond Alberto Brignoli.

52: GOAL! Pilios gives AEK a lifeline with a well-taken strike across Gianluigi Donnarumma.

57: GOAL! Cherki finds the bottom corner to kill any AEK momentum.

65: GOAL! Lewis tees up Foden and he guides the ball into the top corner with a wonderful finish.

76: GOAL! Ryan McAidoo offers Foden the chance to complete his hat-trick with an easy tap-in.

Image: Elliot Anderson scores his first goal in Man City colours

Maresca backs Foden to return to top form

Man City boss Enzo Maresca:

On Foden: "I've said since day one, I consider him one of the best English players. For different reasons, in the last two years, he was not good enough. But I know how good he is. We are trying to help him because we are sure he's going to help us."

On the performance: "It was not easy, especially after the PSG game. We had two games that we certainly needed to win, and we did our job.

"I'm also happy because some of the players have not been playing many minutes, but they were ready. This is important. It is the best feeling for any manager when you make many changes but the performance is still good."

Foden insists his best is yet to come

Man City forward Phil Foden to TNT Sports:

"I enjoyed that a lot. We showed determination again; it wasn't pretty at times, giving sloppy passes away, but I thought we stuck at the game plan, we kept going, and in the end we broke them down.

"I've still got a long way [before I'm back at my best], but I'm going in the right direction and scoring along the way. It definitely helps.

"I just want to keep working hard and trying to be the best I can for the manager and for the team."

Nikolic: We gave City too much respect

AEK Athens boss Marko Nikolic:

"We didn't want to sit back and try to survive, like I said before the game. We wanted to be dangerous with the ball.

"But of course the quality in the finishing phase from City was brutal. These guys were much better in the final third than us. They punished every mistake. A deserved victory for City.

"AEK is only playing Champions League group phase for the second time in 20 years; we're trying to compete. Maybe we showed too much respect for our opponent."

Sports.title: Ngumoha stars as Liverpool come back to win thriller against Villarreal
Sports.content:
Liverpool came from two goals down to defeat Villarreal 4-3 at Anfield and make it three wins from three in this season’s Champions League.

Two goals from Alexis Mac Allister and one apiece from Ronald Araujo and Florian Wirtz completed the turnaround, with Rio Ngumoha superb. All of it came after Virgil van Dijk's poor header allowed Georges Mikautadze to score in the fourth minute.

It was the earliest that Liverpool had fallen behind at Anfield in a major European tie for a quarter of a century but worse was to come when Sergi Cardona raced through to finish off a slick move for the Spanish side's second, a deserved lead at that stage.

But Mac Allister's header from Kostas Tsimikas' corner pulled one back and the lively Ngumoha then fashioned an equaliser when Araujo ghosted in at the far post with Cardona sleeping. It was hardly deserved but Liverpool were rampant after the break.

Image: Liverpool's Ronald Araujo scored a first-half equaliser

The introduction of Wirtz undoubtedly helped but it was Ngumoha whose dancing feet opened up the Villarreal defence to set up Mac Allister for his second. Wirtz then made it four himself with a left-footed finish beyond Peter Gulacsi. His relief was palpable.

Image: Substitute Florian Wirtz put Liverpool 4-2 up

Andoni Iraola will likely feel the same after Tani Oluwaseyi set up a nervous finish. Liverpool have conceded three goals in each of their last two Champions League games but won them both. It has not been entirely convincing but it is a third victory in a row.

Analysis: Ngumoha lights up Anfield

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Vinny O'Connor provides insight on three things we learnt from Liverpool's comeback victory against Villarreal.

They played Rio by Duran Duran upon the final whistle at Anfield, so obvious was it that the winger had been the best player on the pitch. Mac Allister scored two, Wirtz had his big moment but for all the expensive signings on show, Rio Ngumoha was the standout.

Ngumoha finished with two assists and seven successful dribbles. There were times when three Villarreal players were trying to stop him but it never deterred him and you always sensed that the teenager had the trickery and the talent to find a way through.

Image: Rio Ngumoha's touch map for Liverpool in their 4-3 Champions League win over Villarreal

It was a privilege to watch him play and impossible not to imagine what is ahead for him. "On the ball, this kid has so much quality," said Daniel Sturridge on Amazon Prime. "It is stuff you can't teach. What he does with the ball at his feet, it is God-given ability."

There is more to learn, of course. He was partially culpable for Villarreal's second goal, failing to track a runner. But that was hardly a story on a night when Ngumoha lit up Anfield. Others are under scrutiny at Liverpool. He is just having the time of his life.

4 - GOAL! Mikautadze seized on Van Dijk's poor header to score

Iraola: Ngumoha difficult to stop

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following his side's sensational Champions League comeback against Villarreal, Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola heaped praise on young winger Rio Ngumoha, after his dazzling display.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola speaking in the press conference:

"I think he was coming from a very good game the other day, he had a good second half against Brentford. Today he didn't have an easy game also because they were demanding him defensively and their left-back was attacking a lot.

"There was a moment offensively where he was very difficult to stop. If we can put Rio in situations one against one, he makes plays, he produces things, today the assist for Alexis is a lovely play. He could go down for a penalty but he decides to continue which is a great decision.

"Also endurance wise he is able to play more and more minutes. We were pushing him a little bit. He was tired but I think he has done a good effort and I'm very happy for him.

"I am happy with his attitude because he is eager to improve things that we think he needs to improve. He is eager to add more things to his game.

"He has been on the right lately, he is feeling more comfortable now, shooting on his left, he can add this to his game. He is only 18, still not the full package and it is not always going to be like this, there will be ups and downs in the process."

Perez: Ngumoha had a great game

Villarreal head coach Inigo Perez speaking in the press conference:

"The key moment was when they equalised to make it 2-2 just before half-time. We had a fantastic first half. But the mentality and emotion drops, theirs grows and it affects you, particularly at Anfield. But we still managed to stay in the game until the end.

"Rio Ngumoha had a great game but many other players played well. There were emotions, there were goals. When you play at Anfield these things can happen. When a goal is scored here, you can feel the reaction.

"But I don't think we were close to being hammered. I believe if we are able to correct simple details - but elite details - we would be able to win on these big stages."

Sports.title: 'Appalling' batting and 'wickets in clumps' leave England with ODI setback
Sports.content:
England captain Harry Brook admits his side were 'too careful' against Pakistan’s spinners after collapsing to a disappointing 87-run defeat in their ODI tri-series opener.

Arafat Minhas starred with bat and ball in Rawalpindi for the hosts, who recovered from 133-5 to post 302-9 from their 50 overs before skittling England for 215 to claim their second win of the tournament.

Pakistan's all-rounder fired 59 off 58 deliveries and was part of a strong lower middle-order fightback, with Hasan Nawaz top-scoring with a 74-ball 79 and Faheem Ashraf adding 39 off 26 deliveries in the closing overs.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Pakistan’s innings against England in the ODI tri-series, where the hosts recovered from a slow start

Tom Banton and Ben Duckett shifted the momentum in England's favour with a 91-run opening stand, only for Arafat to bamboozle the visitors with a career-best 6-40 and help Pakistan wrap up victory with more than 11 overs to spare.

"We thought they [Pakistan] were slightly under par," Brook said after their defeat. "It got dewy, as we thought it would do and we were pretty happy at halfway.

"We thought [Tom] Banton, Ducky [Ben Duckett] set the tone to nearly get a 100 partnership and then it was a case of losing too many wickets in clumps. We couldn't really string the partnerships together and we ended up on the wrong side.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ben Duckett and Tom Banton were both dismissed quickly after putting on a 91-run opening stand

"We've spoken a lot about rotation of strike through the middle but I think we were a little too careful against the spinners especially, so we can probably put them under a little bit more pressure in stages.

"We've got to tonight to talk about it and tomorrow and bounce back better on Thursday."

England were well placed at 165-3 - despite Arafat removing Banton (57) and Brook (five) - when Naseem Shah bowled Joe Root for 33, with the tourists still in a good position until losing their last five wickets for 18 runs in a chaotic five-over spell.

Jordan Cox was trapped lbw by Arafat before Pakistan's spinner removed Jamie Overton in his next over, with the manner of the dismissal criticised by former England bowler Stuart Broad on commentary.

"That's appalling batting," Broad told Sky Sports, having seen England slip to 205-7. "With Will Jacks at the other end, you're saying England have a chance, you play for your partner.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stuart Broad called out Jamie Overton for his 'appalling batting' after his dismissal

"You say you have a weakness against spin, that's certainly not what you do - he's just chipped it down long-on's throat. A poor wicket for England to lose."

Arafat closed out victory by being involved in all three final wickets, coming in the space of four balls, dismissing Jacks and Adil Rashid in successive deliveries before running out Gus Atkinson.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gus Atkinson was run out in chaotic fashion to complete England's defeat to Pakistan

He became the third Pakistan all-rounder - after Abdul Razzaq and Shahid Afridi - to grab a five-wicket haul and score a half-century in an ODI, with the 21-year-old proud of his man-of-the-match display.

"Hasan [Nawaz] and I discussed that we need to bat deep," Arafat said. "I took charge after Hasan got out and I tried to bat until the end of the innings, which helped in taking the score beyond 300."

On his bowling, Arafat added: "I kept my plans simple. I think variations are very important for a spinner, as they help in deceiving the opposition batters."

Image: Arafat Minhas took 6-40 from his 8.4 overs

Pakistan take plaudits as England need to 'learn from mistakes'

Victory for Pakistan is their second successive win in the ODI tri-series, following their 37-run win over Sri Lanka in the tournament opener, keeping them top of the standings and leaving them well-placed to qualify for the final on October 31.

"A bit of credit to Pakistan, who in both innings fought back," former England captain Nasser Hussain told Sky Sports. "They were 81-4 and 133-5 and yet managed to get over 300.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Overton's brilliant yorker cleans up Hasan Nawaz during England's tri-series games against Pakistan

"England were going well and everyone was thinking they were going to win this game, but there was a bit of fight and a bit of character from Pakistan - with bat and ball."

England - missing several key players - have won all three ODI series this year after losing six of seven bilateral series before that, with Hussain expecting them to take lessons from their convincing defeat.

"He [Sam Curran] looks a bit short of a gallop at the moment, both with the ball and with the bat," Hussain added. "He didn't have rhythm, but that will come. Adil Rashid will get better the more he bowls - he's obviously coming back from injury.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain and Stuart Broad discuss England’s ODI opening options, following another half-century for Tom Banton

"They are missing Jos Butler - England's greatest ever white-ball player. They're missing Jofra Archer and they're also missing Jacob Bethell.

"They've been on a good track, so don't get too up when you win and don't get too down when you haven't chased 300 - just learn from the mistakes that you made today."

Sports.title: Barcelona handed first defeat of season by PSG in classic
Sports.content:
Barcelona were handed their first defeat of the season as they lost 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germain in a Champions League classic.

In a game that saw a total of 40 attempts on goal, it was the reigning European champions who were able to outgun the visitors in a contender for match of the season.

The pair traded goals, with Desire Doue's strike and Lucas Hernandez's header each being cancelled out courtesy of youngster Xavi Espart and the irrepressible Lamine Yamal.

Seconds after Barca's number 10 levelled things for a second time, Vitinha restored PSG's lead as Barcelona ran out of gas. Fabian Ruiz put the icing on the cake five minutes later with a tap-in as Hansi Flick side tasted defeat for the first time in 12 games this season.

There were some sour notes on an otherwise exhilarating evening. Ballon d'Or holder Ousmane Dembele came off with a suspected hamstring injury inside the opening 20 minutes. Team-mate Khvicha Kvaratskhelia was also helped off in the second half after picking up a knock.

Dani Olmo was also withdrawn in the first half for Barcelona, who are already struggling with an injury crisis. It adds another blow for the LaLiga leaders, who visit Real Madrid in the first El Clasico of the season on Sunday.

Key moments from a classic at the Parc des Princes...

2: POST! Kvaratskhelia smashes the woodwork in less than 120 seconds.

5: SAVE! Garcia denies Dembele and Doue in quick succession.

10: CHANCE FOR GORDON! Ball drops to Englishman in good position, but he fails to make the most of it.

14: JUST WIDE! Olmo misses target in Barcelona's first meaningful attempt.

19: INJURY! Ballon d'Or holder Dembele comes off with suspected hamstring issue.

Image: Ousmane Dembele came off with a suspected hamstring injury inside 20 minutes

25: HUGE MISS! Substitute Torres denied by Garcia from close range.

27: INJURY! Olmo replaced as Barca's injury list grows.

29: CHANCES GALORE! PSG squander three brilliant attempts in a matter of seconds.

38: GOAL! Doue finally puts PSG ahead after Lamine Yamal mistake.

Image: PSG's Desire Doue celebrates opening the scoring

40: SAVE! Nearly immediate response from Barca as Fermin is thwarted by Safanov.

51: SAVE! Hakimi denied as PSG miss more chances.

55: GOAL! PSG punished as Espart equalises.

Image: Barcelona youngster Xavi Espart equalised early in the second half

59: INJURY! Kvaratskhelia is helped off the pitch on the hour.

Image: PSG's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia was helped off the pitch after picking up an injury just before the hour mark

71: POST! Torres misses again as he strikes the post from close range!

72: GOAL! A set-piece does the job as Hernandez's header restores PSG's lead.

Image: Lucas Hernandez made it 2-1 with a bullet header

79: GOAL! Lamine Yamal smashes Barca level from a tight angle.

Image: Lamine Yamal squeezes in equaliser to make it 2-2

81: GOAL! Vitinha hits back immediately from edge of the box.

Image: Vitinha celebrates in front of PSG fans after restoring lead

86: GOAL! Ruiz seals the deal as Barca run out of steam.

Image: Fabian Ruiz celebrates scoring PSG's fourth goal

Gordon: We need to try and become PSG

Barcelona forward Anthony Gordon speaking with TNT Sports:

"I think it was quite predictable that it was going to be high-scoring and a good spectacle for people to watch. I was hoping we would come out on the right side of that, but unfortunately we didn't.

"They deserved it. They were the better team and had the better moments with real quality. Athletically, they were able to sustain the pressure and intensity for longer than we were. They've been the team to beat for two years and tonight they gave a great example as to why.

Image: Barcelona's Anthony Gordon said his side can take positives from the defeat

"I think we can take great positives because we played well. It was a competitive spectacle. We've still got work to do and that's a good position to be in. They've been the team to beat for two years. We need to do enough work, analyse the game and try and become that."

Football at its most entertaining

Analysis from Sky Sports' Callum Bishop:

"I covered PSG's 5-4 win over Bayern Munich last season. It was a breathless game and one of the greatest I had ever witnessed.

"While tonight might not quite have been at that level, it was in a very similar bracket. Two of the best teams in the world with full belief in themselves and only one intention: outscore the other.

"No one could've blamed Barcelona if they came to the French capital and decided they were going to shut up shop and try to stop the potent PSG attack.

"Their approach was the complete opposite. They had faith that their attack was as lethal. In the end, they fell short, but they can hold their heads high.

"As a neutral, these are the types of games you dream of watching. It makes you feel things only free-flowing football can.

"If you want a demonstration of what two heavyweight giants playing each other should look like, it is this. Blow for blow, haymaker for haymaker.

"A joy to watch."

Sports.title: Portsmouth strike late to frustrate Wolves
Sports.content:
Terry Devlin denied Wolves victory just as the hosts' inspired substitutions again looked to prove decisive as Portsmouth drew 1-1 at Molineux in the Championship.

Four days after Tawanda Chirewa came off the bench to score the winner at Burnley, substitute Jordan James' strike looked like it would prove the difference for Wolves.

But right-back Devlin popped up with a superbly taken equaliser to give Pompey an unlikely share of the spoils.

The scoreline was harsh on Wolves as Chirewa hit the bar and was denied another goal, while Mateus Mane and Fer Lopez missed chances in a dominant second-half performance. Portsmouth failed to hit the target until Devlin struck in the 86th minute.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto and Portsmouth head coach John Mousinho exchanged heated words after the full-time whistle of their Championship clash at Molineux

In a forgettable first half, Andre had the only Wolves chance. The Brazil midfielder lofted a bouncing shot just wide from 25 yards after Devlin beat Marshall Munetsi to head away Mane's cross.

Portsmouth's only chance of the opening half came in the 36th minute. Wolves failed to deal with Adrian Segecic's deep free-kick and after Nasser Djiga missed the header and Ebou Adams' angled effort was blocked, Rocco Shein's low shot was a few feet wide.

Wolves made a double change at half-time to spark some life into the game - Chirewa, Friday's matchwinner at Burnley, and James replaced Sean Neave and Munetsi - and it worked, with a much-improved display.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jordan James scored the first goal of the night

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Terry Devlin's fine finish helped Portsmouth make it 1-1

Chirewa, who scored the winner within 21 seconds of his arrival at Turf Moor, quickly rattled the bar with a tight-angled, rising shot after turning inside his man.

Mane dragged a low, angled drive well wide, then Lopez volleyed wide from Rafiki Said's inviting cross as Wolves continued to probe for the breakthrough.

That came in the 62nd minute from James, who slammed home a fierce low first-time drive after starting the move with a one-two with Lopez, beating Nicolas Schmid at his near post.

Pompey missed a good chance to equalise when Adams headed over substitute Marezi's corner from five yards while substitute Tommy Doyle's teasing cross just missed the sliding Chirewa as Wolves sniffed a second goal.

But Devlin struck when he chested down and volleyed right into the corner of the net after Marezi's free-kick had been headed clear.

Chirewa's low shot was clawed around a post by Schmid as Wolves desperately pushed for a winner at the death and both benches had to be pulled apart at the final whistle as tensions briefly boiled over before order was quickly restored.

The managers

Wolves' Cesar Peixoto:

"I think the players, because of the last games, were a little more anxious and played more secure. They didn't find the right courage to play in the first 45 minutes.

"At half-time I told them to play with more courage, with more mobility. We made two substitutions and I think we were better.

"In the last few minutes we conceded a goal from their first shot on goal. I think it is an unfair result but we have to do better in the first 45 minutes.

"I said at half-time, go and run, play free, play with courage and be brave in the game. But in the last few minutes we dropped deep because the players wanted so much to win the game to take off this pressure."

Portsmouth's John Mousinho:

"I thought it was about right. Wolves had more possession and shots and the onus is on them as a club coming down from the Premier League to do that.

"But overall we did a really good job of restricting that and when you take everything into consideration I thought we deserved it."

Mousinho played down the angry scenes between the two benches at the final whistle.

He added: "I shook their manager's hand and he said I talk too much and I said that's what I do as a head coach.

"It was handbags and I walked off - it's fine, no worries."

Sports.title: Doué and Vitinha burn bright as brittle Barcelona come unstuck against PSG
Sports.content:
Fire, noise, fury, a sense of empty energy. And across town, a football match too. Do any of these randomly pitched autumnal Champions League fixtures mean anything? Probably not when you’re Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona, and the only game in town is risk-free TV income and a semi-guaranteed place in the knockout stuff.

But this was still a dazzling occasion at the Parc des Princes, where the champions of France and Spain played out a light, open, frictionless, exhibition-style game of football. PSG finished 4-2 winners, having been pegged back to 2-2 midway through the second half. But this was also a game where the score almost did not seem to matter, and where the only really hard message was the frailty of the Barcelona backline and PSG’s thrilling attacking energy in these midweek A-games.

“Debris! Debris! DEBRIS!” the insanely loud PA announcer screamed into his mic before kick-off, in what appeared to be a poor-taste tribute to the current state of the nation’s capital, although it may also have been “du bruit”.

In the hours leading up to this game France’s interior minister had specifically ruled out postponing the whole thing due to the ongoing state of civil unrest, the kind of statement that is no doubt intended to sound reassuring, but which also generates its own kind of whiplash.

Paris is burning. Paris is always burning. No, but Paris really is burning this time. The main site of the violence of the last few days is three miles east of the Parc, which lurks by the ring road in one of Paris’s slightly négligé inner quarters, rising up like a vast concrete alien doughnut in between the townhouses.

On matchday it required a degree of cognitive dissonance to take in these two opposing spectacles. On one hand the piles of charred bikes and the mass looting which has, in reassuringly Parisian style, seemed to focus on elite high-fashion brands. Chanel will rue the day.

In the middle of which Paris also hosted this glittering treat of a football match, stuffed with so many throwaway little delicacies, like an elite artisan patisserie. Before kick-off there were leaping tongues of flame, a laser show spectacular, and a vast tifo at one end showing a ghoulish PSG serial killer type attacking the Barcelona badge with his blood-soaked chainsaw. The message here seemed to be: we are confident. We believe in our process. And we will hack you to death.

View image in fullscreen Désiré Doué strikes to give PSG the lead in the first half. Photograph: Julien de Rosa/AFP/Getty Images

From the start this was a high-grade, disarmingly open game. For Hansi Flick’s Barcelona it represented a genuine test of method. Here we have an elite team that plays with a studied disregard for some of the tenets of positional defensive play. We will press forward and trust what lies behind. We will also give up on the basic idea of marking pretty much from the kick-off, as it turned out.

With one minute gone PSG should have scored. A quick diagonal passing move from right to left put Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in space. His shot pinged off a post and back to an offside Ousmane Dembélé, who shinned wide of an open goal.

There was a fury to PSG in those opening minutes, the front players finding angles and free channels. Pedri and Marc Bernal in central midfield took a while to settle for Barça. Bernal is pure La Masia, a baby-faced 19-year-old Catalan, misleadingly so, as he also has the physique of a rugby union flanker. And Pedri is of course the kind of footballer who glides through these occasions, so casual you half expect to look down and notice he’s playing in flip-flops and holding a Calippo.

Before long Barcelona were making chances of their own, Dani Olmo setting off on a couple of surging deep runs, Anthony Gordon almost getting on the end of a cutback.

João Cancelo was booked with 16 minutes gone for a lunge on Désiré Doué, a disastrous state of affairs for any full-back faced with this nightmare of feints and fast-twitch feet. And two minutes later Dembélé was off, injured chasing the ball, replaced by Ferran Torres. Maybe he should play a bit more, get match fit.

View image in fullscreen Xavi Espart scores his first Champions League goal to equalise for Barcelona at 1-1. Photograph: David Ramos/Uefa/Getty Images

Still the game just zinged from end to end. Raphinha had a close-range shot blocked by Matvey Safonov after a nice pass from Gordon. PSG had three shots blocked or saved in the space of six seconds on 28 minutes, Joan García saving brilliantly low down.

And on 38 minutes PSG deservedly took the lead. The goal was in keeping with the game, expertly hi-tech but also strangely easy and open. Lamine Yamal essayed an ambitious chipped clearance. João Neves took the ball back. It fell to Doué, and he had time to jink inside, feel the space around him, and shoot low inside the post.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

PSG were bossing this by now, Kvaratskhelia running up and down the gears on the left, such a beautifully inventive presence, socks crumpled down around his ankles, all mooching straggly menace, as though the base player from Shed Seven has reinvented himself as a state of the art elite European inside forward.

By the break Barcelona were hanging on, overrun in midfield. And the second half was more of the same: mobile, relentless, high-grade product, lovely attacking interchanges, occasional large spaces in the Barcelona backline.

Doué forced another fine close-range save, played in by Vitinha. On 55 minutes Barcelona equalised, Xavi Espart galloping through the left side of the PSG defence and smashing a shot into the net off the hands of Safonov. The PA announcer gave the goal to Lamine Yamal, because, well, great branding. But it was Espart’s first in Europe, the second of his career. He’s 19, hyper-versatile, another dreamy Catalan youth-teamer.

Barça brought on Rodri, absent from the starting XI, Flick admitted afterwards, solely with the weekend’s clásico in mind. For a while order was restored, Rodri strolling around like the only grownup on the pitch.

View image in fullscreen Vitinha fires in from the edge of the box as PSG retake the lead late on. Photograph: Dave Winter/Shutterstock

But PSG always have tools to hurt you. Doué sliced open the right side again and crossed for Fabián Ruiz to hit the post from six yards out. From the corner Lucas Hernandez had the space to leap and produce a wonderful finish, thumped off the meaty part of the forehead high into the top corner.

Seven minutes later it was 2-2. This was a strange goal, scored by Lamine Yamal after a wonderful run in from the right and a lofted near-post finish that in the moment either looked like a mistake from Safonov or a moment of pure invention.

Two minutes after that it was 3-2 to PSG as the game kept on running to its own speed, this time a controlled first-time shot from Vitinha, seizing on a bouncing ball near the edge of the box. Ruiz added a fourth four minutes from the end.

The game against Lyon at the weekend will mitigate against the usual round of rotations, and injuries did begin to bite a little here. But PSG still finished like a machine built for these occasions, operating always with strength in reserve, and quite clearly the most potent midweek team in Europe once again.

Sports.title: Mac Allister double sparks Liverpool’s thrilling comeback win over Villarreal
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola and Iñigo Pérez parked a long and close friendship in the buildup to their first competitive confrontation as coaches. The old Athletic Bilbao teammates will have a humdinger of a Champions League contest to dissect once communications are restored. Liverpool, ignited by Rio Ngumoha, recovered from two goals down against Villarreal to maintain their 100% record plus their gathering momentum.

Alexis Mac Allister struck twice, Florian Wirtz capped recent improvement with his first goal of the season while Liverpool were dreadful for the opening 30 minutes, transformed after the break and fretting in stoppage time after Tani Oluwaseyi had volleyed in a third for Villarreal. The game flipped on Sergi Cardona’s mistake and Ronald Araújo’s equaliser with the final touch of the first half. “We weren’t able to handle the emotion tonight,” conceded Villarreal coach Pérez.

But the lasting impression was of Ngumoha seizing responsibility in the absence of big names and driving Liverpool on at the age of 18. The winger was electric, the difference maker, and from the right-wing role that he is still adapting to. He supplied the cross for Araújo’s all-important leveller and unravelled the Villarreal defence for Mac Allister’s second, Liverpool’s third on a rollercoaster of a night and performance.

“Rio didn’t have it easy tonight,” said Iraola. “They demanded a lot of him defensively with their left-back attacking but he was very difficult to stop. If you can put him in one-v-ones he can make space and produce things, like the lovely assist for Alexis, and endurance-wise he is able to play more and more minutes. He is eager to improve and if he can add things to his game he’ll become the full package.”

The regular phone calls between Iraola and Pérez had ceased in the days leading up to the fixture. Had they continued the Liverpool head coach might have told his opposite number to bring a coat and not wear a short-sleeved polo shirt on a day of incessant rain. Iraola rested Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola. A fourth game in 10 days explained the omissions of Wirtz and Barcola, who had featured heavily in the previous three, while Isak’s workload was being carefully managed after his recent thigh injury.

Liverpool’s much-changed team fell behind quickly. An error-strewn start by Virgil van Dijk was responsible, and also in keeping with a ponderous opening half hour from the hosts. Villarreal passed their way around Anfield with style and precious little resistance.

The Liverpool captain presented Georges Mikautadze with an immediate opportunity when he misjudged a long clearance by Renato Veiga. Van Dijk’s poor touch almost released the Georgia international striker through on goal but Jérémy Jacquet closed off that route. Van Dijk’s second slip followed moments later, and this time there was no reprieve. The defender attempted to head another Veiga long ball back into the safe arms of Alisson. He found Mikautadze instead and Villarreal’s No 9 pounced expertly, controlling well before rolling the ball under the Liverpool keeper. There were apologies all round from Van Dijk.

View image in fullscreen Alexis Mac Allister heads home to score Liverpool’s opening goal. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Ed Sykes/Apl/Sportsphoto

Villarreal doubled their lead with a goal that encapsulated the start made by both teams – the visitors passing their way through Liverpool’s midfield and picking holes in their high defensive line, with the home side slow to react. Pape Gueye, Alberto Moleiro and Nathan Saliba combined to send their rampaging left-back, Cardona, through on goal. Played onside by Kostas Tsimikas, the full-back beat Alisson with a finish a striker would have been proud of.

Cardona’s defending was much less impressive as Liverpool clawed their way back into the contest. The recovery commenced when Mac Allister rose superbly to meet a Tsimikas corner and flicked an unstoppable header into the unguarded side of Peter Gulacsi’s goal.

Villarreal’s comfort vanished entirely when Ngumoha clipped a cross towards the far post following another Tsimikas corner. Cardona checked his surroundings, then inexplicably let the ball bounce behind him, and right into the spot where Araújo was lurking. The on-loan defender headed home for the second successive week in the Champions League and celebrated with a mass pile-on with fans in the Anfield Road Stand.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Araújo was withdrawn at the interval because Iraola felt Liverpool would match up better to Villarreal with Ryan Gravenberch at right-back and Wirtz restored to the forward line. And so it proved. Liverpool improved vastly after the restart with Ngumoha and Wirtz a constant, marauding threat.

View image in fullscreen Ronald Araújo heads home Liverpool’s second goal in first-half stoppage time. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters

Ngumoha took the acclaim of the Kop after creating Mac Allister’s second of the night with a sparkling run down the right. It was some one-two that brought Liverpool the lead. Mac Allister floated a pass out to the winger, whose first touch brought the ball under control and took him away from Cardona in the same movement. He then left the substitute Juan Foyth in his wake before pulling back a pass from the byline for the incoming midfielder to smash a shot in off the underside of Gulacsi’s crossbar.

Wirtz completed the comeback after Tsimikas and Cody Gakpo had combined to create space for the playmaker inside the area. The Germany international drilled a clinical left-footed finish inside the Villarreal keeper’s far corner. Oluwaseyi created a nervous finale when converting a cross from the former Newcastle forward Ayoze Pérez but Liverpool held firm. “We started too relaxed and we were too relaxed at 4-2,” Iraola said. “But against a really good Villarreal team I give value and importance to this win.”

Sports.title: Football regulator has ‘absolute power’ to force Manchester City sale if verdict upheld
Sports.content:
The Independent Football Regulator (IFR) will have “absolute power” to force Manchester City’s owners to sell if they are ultimately found to have run the club improperly, the watchdog’s chair has said.

Manchester City have been found guilty of circumventing Premier League rules by an independent commission, which found they set up “sham” commercial arrangements to inflate revenues or reduce costs by over £900m over a nine-season period.

They were also found to have made “concerted efforts” to “stop and frustrate” the Premier League’s investigation into those arrangements. City have lodged an appeal, claiming the verdict “contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe”.

David Kogan, the chair of the IFR, told podcast The Rest Is Football it was premature to talk about any action his organisation might take while the appeal was ongoing. Kogan did confirm, though, that the IFR had “absolute power” to force a sale by the club’s ownership, if that was felt to be appropriate.

“We have the power to ask an owner to step away from a club if we believe that they run a club in a way that is neither fit, fair or done with propriety,” Kogan said. Asked if an owner could refuse to divest, Kogan replied: “No, no, no. We’ve got absolute power to do so.”

On the possibility of the IFR investigating City, Kogan said: “I am not going to get pushed into making any judgement on this until we’ve seen all of those questions being answered. Then we will have to decide whether we’re going to mount our own investigation and come to a conclusion on that and what we’re going to do. And pre-empting that would be a colossal mistake.”

Manchester City are majority-owned by Abu Dhabi United Group (Adug), an investment vehicle owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, a member of the Abu Dhabi royal family.

Kogan has already pledged to resign if there is any political interference in any investigation the IFR may undertake into City, amid concerns it could create a diplomatic issue between the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates.

Sports.title: Carrick insists Manchester United board back him after Ten Hag points to ‘toxic culture’
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick believes Manchester United’s board continue to back him, although the manager admits he must start winning matches to keep his job. Carrick also denied there is a toxic culture at the club, after Erik ten Hag’s claim there had been when he was manager.

Carrick’s side travel to Como on Wednesday for their third Champions League game, aiming for a third victory of the season in all competitions. Sunday’s 1-1 draw at Leeds left United 13th in the Premier League, having won only once.

Their only other success was last month’s 4-0 home win against Sabah, of Azerbaijan, in the Champions League. Carrick was asked on Tuesday if he feels backed by the executive.

“Yeah – why wouldn’t I?” said the 45-year-old. “I’m in this position, I have a really good relationship with everybody at the club. We’ve got to win games of football and that’s what we’re striving to do.”

Despite the poor results Carrick has not sought reassurance from the hierarchy. “Certainly not. I don’t need any reassurance,” he said. “It’s pretty clear. I know the role, my responsibilities. I know we’ve got to win ­football games for everything to flow and ­everything to fall into place.”

Ten Hag was Carrick’s predecessor from April 2022 to October 2024. During his tenure the Dutchman claimed that the executive did not support him regarding some disciplinary ­matters. In early 2024 Jim ­Ratcliffe, who had recently become the largest ­single minority stakeholder, assumed control of the football department.

View image in fullscreen Erik ten Hag and Cristiano Ronaldo in 2022. ‘He let the team down, and he let me down,’ the former Manchester United manager said. Photograph: Ed Sykes/Action Images/Reuters

“They are continuing the toxic culture, they fuel it, they give power to the players,” Ten Hag told the Athletic, referring to his time in charge.

Ten Hag claimed that Cristiano Ronaldo “let the team down” ­when the Dutchman was managing United. The ­forward’s second spell at the club featured him walking out twice.

“He let the team down and he let me down, because we planned with him,” said Ten Hag. He also questioned ­Ronaldo’s commitment, saying that after United were beaten 4-0 at Brentford in the second game of his tenure, the ­Portuguese refused to complete a run in training.

“I confronted him with this,” Ten Hag said. “Many times I say: ‘Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can’t bring yourself in the box, you can’t score.”

Carrick, who became interim manager in January and was appointed permanently in May, was asked if he has encountered toxicity at United. “No, I haven’t. The players, the staff, they’ve given us everything that they could give,” he said. “I couldn’t be happier with the togetherness.”

Ten Hag led United to the FA Cup in 2024, but claimed the owners then failed to meet promises made during talks that led to him agreeing a contract extension.

He said: “They promised me ­loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned. We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn’t keep. “I said: ‘No selling Scott ­McTominay.’ And in the end they sold him. I got, of course, very embarrassed and disappointed.”

Carrick was asked if Ten Hag’s comments about the leadership raised any red flags. In answering he mentioned Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the chief executive, Omar Berrada.

“Not for me, that’s Erik’s opinion, it’s totally wrong for me to comment or get involved, it’s nothing to do with me at that stage. We’re pretty stable. There’s certain conversations we have that we’re really clear with, with Jason with Omar, the owners, and to the players. It’s really important we’re all pulling in the same direction.”

Carrick will be without nine players for Como: Leny Yoro is ­suspended and Ayden Heaven is ill, while Luke Shaw, Lisandro Martínez, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford, Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu and Manuel Ugarte are injured.

The absence of five frontline defenders (Yoro, Shaw, Heaven, Martínez and Dorgu) will force Carrick to field an unfamiliar backline that may include Matthijs de Ligt, who has not played since last November due to a back problem. An appearance for the 19-year-old left-back, Harry Amass, is also being considered.

There is a severe weather warning for lightning and rain in Como on Wednesday that may affect the 5.45pm kick-off.

Sports.title: Champions League roundup: McTominay double leads Napoli past Bodø/Glimt
Sports.content:
Scott McTominay scored his first two goals of the season to help Napoli beat Bodø/Glimt 4-3 and relieve pressure on the coach, Massimiliano Allegri. McTominay, who also hit a post, missed a month of the season after undergoing a surgical procedure in early September to treat an irregular heartbeat.

Matteo Politano’s first-minute opener was cancelled out by Bodø’s Jens Petter Hauge. McTominay restored Napoli’s lead before the break only for Andreas Helmersen to again level for the Norwegian club.

The Scotland midfielder struck again on 71 minutes and Odin Bjørtuft’s late own goal secured the result. Bodø still managed an injury-time consolation from Sondre Brunstad Fet.

Atlético Madrid held on with 10 men for a 1-1 draw with Stuttgart, foiling the German underdogs’ bid to join Paris Saint-Germain and Liverpool at the top of the table on nine points.

Julián Alvarez’s goal for Atlético had cancelled out Jamie Leweling’s opener when the midfielder Morten Hjulmand made a reckless sliding tackle from behind on Angelo Stiller, resulting in a red card that left Atlético clinging on.

Serhou Guirassy scored twice but Borussia Dortmund wasted plenty more chances in a 2-1 away win over Azerbaijan’s Sabah.

It wasn’t the sort of convincing victory the German team were hoping for, after last week’s loss to Bodø/Glimt and draw at Union Berlin which allowed Bayern Munich to take the top spot in the Bundesliga.

View image in fullscreen Serhou Guirassy scores for Borussia Dortmund against Sabah. Photograph: Alexandre Simões/Borussia Dortmund/Getty Images

Pavel Kacor’s leaping volley in the 90th minute earned Slavia Prague a 2-2 draw at Fenerbahce, extending the hosts’ long wait for a Champions League win. The Turkish side had been leading 2-0 early on before a defensive blunder by Mattéo Guendouzi let the Czech team back into the game.

PSV won 1-0 against Porto thanks to Guus Til’s 57th-minute winner as the Portuguese side slumped to a third loss. Roma cruised to a 4-0 win over Slovan Bratislava with Mario Hermoso, Nahuel Molina and Niccolò Pisilli on the scoresheet before Donyell Malen added a fourth from the penalty spot.

Sports.title: Arsenal’s David Raya hits back at ‘boring’ label as Arteta defends side’s style of play
Sports.content:
David Raya says he does not care if rival supporters call Arsenal “boring” as his manager, Mikel Arteta, insisted that critics of the team’s style were only a “very small minority”.

Arsenal made it 10 wins out of 11 in all competitions for the season when they beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 at the City Ground on Sunday. But it was a day when Noni Madueke’s late goal papered over a flat and one-paced performance. Arteta admitted his players had to be better in attacking terms and the discussion over how they are able to get the job done has tracked them to Germany where they face Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

Raya sought to cut through the external noise when he was asked whether the criticism irritated him and his teammates. “No it doesn’t,” the goalkeeper said. “People have their own opinions. We have our own opinion. At the end of the day, we have lost one game in 11 this season and if you call that boring or irritating … I don’t know what to say. We enjoy playing football. We enjoy going out there every single day to win football matches and that’s the most important thing.”

Arteta is focused on the glamour tie against Bayern, who will be without the suspended Michael Olise and might not have their manager, Vincent Kompany, in the dugout. He has been laid low by a viral infection that has also affected his legs. Arteta’s attitude to those who throw stones in Arsenal’s direction is that there will always be gripes about every club.

“If you analyse all the top teams in England and I go: ‘OK, what are they talking about?’ They all have a list [of things about them],” he said. “None of us are perfect and thank God that we are not perfect and we can still improve, even though we have won the amount of games we have done because otherwise the next day, what do you do? You just expect to be better than the opponent and that’s it. Especially in the Premier League, we know that is very far from the reality.”

Arteta sought to introduce a note of levity. “I don’t have that impression [about there being a debate over Arsenal’s style] because I heard it was incredible,” he said. “Because we scored so many goals, we have more possession, more shots, different players participating, no goals from set pieces … so the story is completely different to last year. I think we are talking about a very small minority and the other ones they know they have enjoyed a lot the way we have played and dominated games this year. We have proven that, so that’s my opinion.”

Arteta knows that Bayern will bring the game to Arsenal; perhaps it will be a relief not to face low-block opponents and it might allow his team to be more expansive.

“We know the kind of game that we’re going to play,” he said. “Both teams are very clear on that and we experienced that at the Emirates [last season, when Arsenal won 3-1]. It’s going to be a very similar one in many moments. A low block demands a different kind of game to a high block, to a team that is constantly putting the ball in the last line. But still on Sunday, I think we could have done things better and that’s in our hands. We need to recognise that openly, as well.”

Arteta is never short of intensity or motivation and he went back to last season’s Champions League final defeat by Paris Saint-Germain on penalties to illustrate how wildly the fire burns inside of him.

“I tried [to get over it] but I haven’t managed to,” he said. “I tried for many weeks during the summer but when I see the ball, the scenes, I hear the music, I want it so badly. We know that we have to go step by step but I think that fire is within the team and all of us individually. We know what we had to go through – not being champions of Europe by a penalty. So, let’s try again.”

View image in fullscreen Vincent Kompany may not be in the dugout due to a viral infection. Photograph: Marcel Engelbrecht/firo sportphoto/Getty Images

Raya remembered how Arsenal had only 28% of the ball against PSG but he feels they are better equipped to enjoy greater control against the elite. “I think so,” he said. “You have to see that in perspective, as well. It was our first Champions League final in so many years, we score in the fifth minute and you sit back a little bit knowing how good they are offensively. We didn’t want to give anything away. It is different now. You can see the way we play. You can see different type of ways of playing that we have. We are more prepared this year than last year.”

Kompany is touch and go to make the game. He was unable to attend Bayern’s training session on Tuesday while he ceded the responsibility of the pre-match press conference to his assistant, Aaron Danks.

Kompany had struggled through the 6-1 home win over RB ­Leipzig in the Bundesliga on Saturday – after which the club’s sporting director, Max Eberl, addressed the media instead of him. There have been reports in Germany that Kompany needed to lie down on his sofa at home after the Leipzig game and that the infection had affected an existing hip problem which meant he could hardly walk.

“It has affected his legs at times,” Danks said. “He’s felt some pain in his legs. I’m not sure about the reports about him lying down on the couch. I think we can all have a lie down on the couch after a game. It’s just a virus. The doctors and experts know way more than I do. The most important thing we have encouraged is that he rests; he takes the time he needs – however long that may be.

“Unfortunately, I can’t give you any more – whether that’s tomorrow or whether that’s two or three days’ time. I don’t know.We just take it day by day and see how he is. Getting Vince to rest is a challenge. You know him as a person. He’s a real leader. He works hard.”

Danks will take charge of the team against Arsenal if Kompany cannot make it, just as he did last season during the epic Champions League semi-final, first leg against PSG when Kompany was suspended. PSG won 5-4 at the Parc des Princes that night before progressing 6-5 on aggregate.

Birmingham-born Danks, who briefly took caretaker charge of Aston Villa in 2022 and has coached at various clubs including Anderlecht and Middlesbrough, said he would be in communication with Kompany “in some shape or form” if the manager was not able to come to the stadium.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
Sports.content:
MAD FOR IT

As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry, a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26.

So what has changed? Ange Postecoglou was tinned that summer despite winning the Flamin’ Bigger Vase. Thomas Frank was an appointment the soccer sensibles agreed was smart. A coach with impeccable credentials in improving players, willing to work in tandem with club suits, an ideal apex for an org chart. With lovely hair, too. Frank was sent packing in February, his popularity ratings plunging to depths unseen since Alan Sugar had the bright idea of appointing George Graham, who had paid his gardener to shape his lawn into the Arsenal crest. In football’s world of irrelevant but interesting (you sure? – Football Daily Ed) coincidences, the last time Spurs beat Coventry in the league, when Sergiy Rebrov’s goal completed a 3-0 stroll in 2001, the manager’s programme notes had been written by Gorgeous George, who the day previously had been the recipient of Sugar’s “you’re fired” flex.

Igor Tudor’s tenure resembled a slasher movie, an appointment on the nod from a sporting director, Fabio Paratici, who had already left. Classic Spurs. What could possibly go wrong? Everything, it turns out. Or close to, until Roberto De Zerbi was handed the keys and a control none of his predecessors commanded. The transfer spend has been heavy, and when Kulusevski arrived in the 87th minute on Monday, the game not yet won, he did so following an absence where Spurs signed 20 players either permanently or on loan, at a cost of £530m.



Scoring Spurs’ opening goal on Monday was James Maddison. Football’s king of the oche was absent for almost as long Kulusevski. Last season, as De Zerbi attempted to arrest the slide towards relegation, ‘Madders’ initially sat on the bench on a vibes-only basis and closed out the season with not much more than 30 minutes of play, and had little time to do Maddison things like his arcing beauty against his hometown club on Monday, which opened the scoring for Spurs.

Good feelings at last, following a sunshine break in Marbella where, according to De Zerbi, his players became less a squad than a family. “You have to play for your friend and your brother, not like 11 robot players on the pitch,” he cooed. With two of his stars back in tandem, De Zerbi’s enforcer intensity brought a first league win of the season, to help Tottenham off the bottom. “With them in the dressing room there is another atmosphere,” De Zerbi roared. Jam tomorrow? Glory, glory? Lads, it’s etc …

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Scott Murray from 8pm BST for Liverpool 2-1 Villarreal in the Bigger Cup action while Simon Burnton is on clockwatch action to bring you updates from PSG 3-3 Barcelona, Manchester City 4-1 AEK Athens, and more.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“People still call me a ‘party boy’. That stigma has been overused and has followed me since I retired from football. I’m not saying I didn’t enjoy myself as a player. You never hear that I didn’t turn up for training or wasn’t fit … now I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time. I’m a manager” – Dwight Yorke speaks to Morgan Ofori from his home in Dubai about his career ambitions, having been linked with the vacant Ghana job.

View image in fullscreen Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m straightforward. I don’t mess around, take shortcuts or do the job halfway.’ Photograph: Christopher Pike/The Guardian

double quotation mark Further to Peters and Lee [Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green. They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning.

double quotation mark On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White” – Tim Russell.

Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others).
