Sports.title: Featured Comment: Budget cap not to blame for lack of winning teams in F1 | Brief
Sports.content:
This week’s poll asks whether Formula 1 needs to rethink its budget cap as the series’ top four team have pulled further away from their rivals this year.

But reader @Skydiverian suggests it might not be realistic to expect F1 to regularly have more than four race-winning teams:

Four competitive teams has happened before but it’s still not great and the problem is as it always is, money. And I’d like to see more teams in a season have a realistic shot of winning races. It’s unfortunate that the stats are not on my side.

Pretty much since the late 80s the problem has been that the best teams could throw more money at the problem to fix it. Now, teams that are significantly behind can’t throw more money at the problem to catch-up due to the cost cap, rather than simply not having the money in the first place as was common in the 80s. (This season is interesting. It seems that Mercedes blew most of it’s cap early to get and maintain their advantage, whereas Red Bull didn’t and that’s in part why Max has had a better car the last two races. But it’s not like Williams or Aston Martin can fix their problems by spending more money to fix the deficit).

The problem is that ultimately there’s no easy fix, but spending millions to be the so-called best of the rest basically seems pointless if there is a very unlikely chance of a team outside of the top four having a realistic shot at the podium or even a win. And that’s always been a problem going back decades.

Some number crunching by looking at the history books: the 500th race was 1990 Australia, 1,100th being Vegas 2023. In those 600 races I’ve found six that were won by drivers driving for teams who finished outside the top four in the constructors championship.

That’s six of 600 races over 33 years where we had a winner driving for a team who finished outside the top 4 in that years constructors championship, 1% of all races. Seven if you count Johnny Herbert’s win at the Nurburgring which to me was a genuine surprise at the time. To me those stats aren’t good enough.

Whether that’s the fault of teams with no money, teams with too much money or teams with a cash limit so they can’t design their way out is up for debate. But my point is that I’d like to see more teams have a reasonable chance of winning. F1 has never really had that and will continue not to unless something changes (maybe by letting teams further down have a bigger budget the following season rather than just more CFD time).

I’d rather that at least 70% of drivers have a realistic chance of winning, ideally 100% of teams. It’s the reason I preferred IndyCar before Alex Palou showed up, results were unpredictable and smaller teams have a chance of getting a win or two. That’s just so rare in F1 and the current cost cap rules will continue to make unlikely.

@Skydiverian

Sports.title: Early coronation for Antonelli? Five talking points for the United States Grand Prix | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli could win the world championship this weekend in only his second year as a Formula 1 driver. Here are the talking points for the United States Grand Prix.

Will Antonelli clinch the title?

The odds are stacked heavily in favour of Mercedes’ new star clinching the title at some point, but most likely not this weekend. That said it is not beyond the realm of possibility team mate George Russell could have another poor weekend and come away point-less while Antonelli takes his ninth victory of the season, putting him over the line.

The title has been won at this track twice before, and both times it was by a Mercedes druver: Lewis Hamilton won the championship there in 2015 and 2019. But regardless of whether Antonelli does clinch the title this weekend it is clearly a matter of ‘when’ not ‘if’.

Verstappen dominating again?

The driver most likely to delay Antonelli’s championship celebrations is not his team mate but Max Verstappen. Red Bull have made a breakthrough with their RB22 and as well as winning the last two grands prix plus a sprint race, Verstappen could have taken victory in Baku as well with better luck.

He arrives at this weekend’s race looking like the driver to beat, with every indication he could dominate the final rounds of the season, setting himself up for a shot at the title next year.

McLaren’s driver headache

McLaren arrive in Austin in a curiously similar situation to last year: a clash between their drivers at the previous race in Singapore has created an obvious tension. What’s more, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri’s collision during the sprint race in Singapore was more costly than the one they had in the grand prix 12 months ago.

Norris’s radio messages during the grand prix gave the distinction impression he was looking for ways to make amends, having eventually accepted he was the one at fault for their collision. But above all the team will be anxious to avoid a repeat of the first-corner collision which wrecked their sprint race at the circuit 12 months ago. Particularly as a resurgent Red Bull are poised to relegate the reigning constructors’ champions to fourth place in the standings.

US teams’ driver decisions

Of the two teams competing in their home event this weekend, one has settled its driver plans for 2027. Haas has announced Rafael Camara as the replacement for Esteban Ocon, whose Formula 1 future is in serious doubt as few likely alternatives remain for next year.

Could Cadillac be one of them? F1’s new American team is yet to confirm its plans for next year. However its hopes IndyCar star Colton Herta would take Formula 2 by storm and make himself an obvious candidate for promotion have been dashed: he lies 19th in the standings, 181 points behind fellow rookie and championship leader Camara.

Are Colapinto’s die-hards paying attention?

Last week Franco Colapinto spoke out in criticism of the element of his fanbase which has sent vile abuse to his rival drivers, team members and FIA officials since he made his F1 debut this year. The Alpine driver told those attacking others in his name that they are not helping his cause in F1.

Will they take his words on board? We’ll get an indication the next time he is involved in any kind of incident on-track – however slight it may be.

Sports.title: On This Day: Ralf Schumacher wins Formula Nippon title despite spinning out | Brief
Sports.content:
30 years ago today Ralf Schumacher won the Formula Nippon title despite retiring two laps into a rain-lashed race.

Schumacher arrived at the final race at Fuji Speedway just two points ahead of team mate Naoki Hattori. But Schumacher spun out two laps into the rain-hit race (see 3’50 in the video below).

That left Hattori on course for the title, which looked increasingly secure as the laps ticked down. But conditions worsened, and seven laps from home he spun out too, handing Schumacher the 1996 title. Schumacher made his F1 debut the following year for Jordan (now Aston Martin).

Katsutomo Kaneishi won ahead of future Formula 1 driver Pedro de la Rosa. Another future F1 driver, Shinji Nakano, took fourth place behind Masahiko Kageyama. Just seven of the 26 starters were running at the finish.

Sports.title: Rafael Espinoza Wants Naoya Inoue Before Moving Up
Sports.content:
Rafael Espinoza has his sights set on Naoya Inoue, citing the Japanese superstar as his main reason to stay at 126 pounds. The WBO featherweight champion is also realistic, keeping the door open to move up to super featherweight if elite opportunities don’t materialize.

At 6’1″, the Mexican titlist wants unification honors at featherweight, knowing a win over Inoue punches his ticket straight into pound-for-pound conversations. He is even game to travel to Tokyo to make it happen.

“There’s also a big fight, the Inoue fight, and I think that’s the fight that would launch me into the world pound-for-pound rankings. That’s my dream,” Espinoza said to The Ring.

Landing the bout is another story. Espinoza presents an awkward, grueling test for anyone stepping up in weight. His height, wingspan, and relentless motor demand total focus. While Inoue possesses the timing and precision to exploit defensive holes, getting inside on Espinoza means walking through fire against a much bigger fighter.

Espinoza feels fully equipped to take the victory, even if he avoids bold knockout predictions.

“I have the qualities, the desire, and I have the reach, the height. I think I have power,” Espinoza said. “I’m not saying I’m going to knock him out. I’ve never liked talking that way, but I have a lot of hope that I can win that fight.”

Under the guidance of trainer Eddy Reynoso, Espinoza has spent recent camps dialing in his fundamentals. Rather than crowding opponents and absorbing needless shots, he has been drilling range control, leaning hard into straight punches from the outside.

The risk-to-reward ratio is completely tilted against Espinoza. Inoue gets credit for daring to be great no matter who he faces, but taking on a tall physical anomaly in his first outing at 126 offers minimal extra reward compared to the extreme stylistic danger.

Instead of Espinoza getting rewarded for ruling the division, Top Rank and Inoue’s team have plenty of reason to look elsewhere. Whether that means targeting a more conventionally sized titlist like Leo Angelo or Bruce Carrington, or grabbing the newly stripped WBA belt against an opponent with fewer stylistic advantages, Espinoza could find out the hard way that being the most dangerous man in the room often leaves you standing alone.

Sports.title: Jaron Ennis Signs Seven-Fight Extension With Matchroom
Sports.content:
Jaron “Boots” Ennis is locked in for the long haul after signing a massive seven-fight extension with Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom. His eyes remain squarely set on collecting every piece of hardware at 154 pounds.

The timing couldn’t be better since IBF champion Josh Kelly signed fresh terms with the promoter on the exact same day. Because both champions share a promotional home, Hearn holds the inside track to set up an in-house unification clash. Whoever walks away with those three belts would then need only Sebastian Fundora’s WBC title to crown an undisputed king.

Ennis, now 29, picked up the WBA alongside the WBO belt after stopping Xander Zayas in Brooklyn this past July. Matchroom hasn’t announced a date or next rival just yet, but the mission statement is clear.

“I’m excited for my extended partnership with Matchroom,” Ennis stated. “Together we have aligned ourselves in all the right positions to get what I want, and that’s undisputed!” A seven-fight commitment gives Hearn plenty of runway. Still, locking down every title means hammering out contracts with rival camps, and Kelly’s signature alone doesn’t automatically settle fight terms.

Fundora brings another challenge to the bargaining table. His team wants an even split for any clash with Boots. If Ennis handles Kelly first to claim the IBF strap, he enters negotiations holding three belts, giving him total leverage to demand the lion’s share. Yet Fundora would still hold the final piece of the puzzle Ennis desires.

Ennis originally teamed up with Matchroom back in April 2024. That run saw him defend his turf in Philadelphia against David Avanesyan, beat Karen Chukhadzhian, then unify at welterweight by taking down Eimantas Stanionis in Atlantic City. Since jumping up to light middleweight, he obliterated Uisma Lima inside a single round before outclassing Zayas to become a two-division unified champ.

Hearn made his intentions clear, stating the entire Matchroom team plans to honor that loyalty by delivering undisputed opportunities on boxing’s premier stages.

Now comes the real work: turning contract ink into confirmed fight dates. Locking down Kelly gets the ball rolling toward three belts, setting up a clash with Fundora to finish the undisputed sweep.

Hearn had no choice but to lock Ennis down with a massive commitment, because letting him walk into Zuffa’s open arms would have been catastrophic for Matchroom’s stable. Dana White and the Zuffa operation are hungry for legitimate, elite names with actual substance, not smoke and mirrors. Losing Boots to that machine right when Anthony Joshua is clearly nearing the final bell would have stripped Matchroom of its true crown jewel in the United States.

The reality is that Hearn’s roster of genuine, division-ruling stars is paper thin. Ben Whittaker was hyped up as a generational sensation, but the matchmaking quickly exposed the ceiling there. When a promoter has to spoon-feed a 29-year-old fighter soft touches like Richard Rivera just to keep the show on the road, everyone sees through the packaging. Whittaker needs careful stage management and manufactured protection to stay afloat.

Ennis is the exact opposite. Boots does not need protective matchmaking or promotional smoke screens to look elite because the skill set is real. He can fight on the inside, switch stances seamlessly, punch with spite, and wipe out titleholders without Hearn having to hold his hand. While British promoters naturally lean toward homegrown cash cows, Ennis possesses the pedigree to carry the Matchroom banner globally and clean out an entire division on merit alone. Locking him in for seven bouts ensures Hearn stays relevant in the US market instead of watching Zuffa build their boxing empire around Philadelphia’s best fighter.

Sports.title: David Haye Urges Fabio Wardley To Take Year Off
Sports.content:
David Haye thinks Fabio Wardley needs to step away from the ring for an entire year to rebuild his mechanics from the ground up following another brutal second-round TKO loss to Daniel Dubois.

While Haye still sees a path forward for Wardley, he doubts a standard eight-week training camp offers enough runway to fix the technical flaws Dubois repeatedly punished. His advice is simple: take an extended break to master the fundamental skills Wardley missed by turning pro without an amateur background.

“He should take a year out. But not a year out partying, holiday. No, just working on the basic fundamentals,” Haye said to talkSPORT Boxing about Wardley. “Go get a good Cuban coach, someone who just gets your legs right, gets your balance.”

Haye is assuming a lot if he thinks a year off in a Cuban school of boxing is going to rewire a 31-year-old brawler who learned his trade on the white-collar circuit. Fighters do not magically develop fluid footwork, ring IQ, and nuanced balance at this stage of life in an empty gym. Those instincts are drilled into kids through hundreds of amateur bouts between the ages of twelve and twenty.

If Wardley steps away for twelve months with millions already sitting in the bank, he will not return as Guillermo Rigondeaux. He will return as an older, heavier, rustier version of the exact same guy, minus whatever sharp edge kept him dangerous.

Taking a year off ignores human nature, especially for a fighter who just cashed massive checks. Inactivity dulls timing and slows reflexes, and when a fighter relies almost entirely on explosive athleticism and punching power, ring rust is lethal.

“In the heat of the battle, you do what you do,” Haye explained. “He hasn’t done the correct thing, enough reps.” “He could continue in this division, and we’ll have some great fights, but it’s not going to be good for his health.”

The blueprint to keep his career alive is obvious: step down levels immediately. Wardley needs active reps under the lights against beatable, mid-tier opposition. He needs guys who will test him for six to eight rounds without having the world-class power or technical precision of a Daniel Dubois or Joseph Parker to punish every fundamental mistake.

The punishment he absorbed across those three elite fights is the kind that takes chunks out of a fighter’s prime. Throwing him into gym purgatory will only make him think too much in the ring, and a hesitant brawler gets knocked out twice as fast.

Sports.title: Josh Kelly Extends Matchroom Deal, Targets 2027 Unifications
Sports.content:
Josh Kelly is staying put. The IBF light middleweight champion just signed a multi-fight contract extension with Eddie Hearn and Matchroom Boxing, setting his sights directly on major unifications for 2027.

The deal keeps Kelly locked in with Matchroom following a breakout run where he claimed his first world championship and successfully defended it. While Matchroom announced no date or opponent alongside the new paperwork, Kelly made his intentions clear immediately.

“I’m World Champion, and I am very excited about the future with Matchroom Boxing,” Kelly said. “Now I only want the biggest fights in the division. Unifications. Bring it on.”

The 32-year-old slickster took the IBF belt via majority decision over Bakhram Murtazaliev at Newcastle’s Utilita Arena in January. He then traveled to Jeddah in July, handing Caoimhin Agyarko his first career defeat over twelve rounds.

Those victories completely transformed his negotiating leverage. Kelly enters future talks holding genuine hardware rather than petitioning as a challenger.

Matchroom must now translate that ambition into reality. Kelly wants fellow champions, though Hearn stopped short of naming specific targets for the stablemate.

“We are thrilled to extend Josh Kelly’s contract with Matchroom Boxing,” Hearn stated. “He is an elite operator and one of the pound-for-pound best the UK has to offer. It is no secret that we have some huge plans ahead for Josh in 2027, where he will be aiming to add more World Titles to his collection.”

Kelly’s signature footwork carried him to the top. Meeting another belt-holder will test if that slick style holds up while mounting enough offensive output to take rounds against elite champions.

Now sitting at 19-1-1 with nine knockouts under trainer Adam Booth, Kelly gave his promoter clear instructions for 2027: line up the champions and let him work.

Hearn is rolling the dice here, because putting Kelly in the ring with Jaron Ennis looks like a recipe for a demolition. If that unification gets made, Kelly is facing an elite-level talent.

Ennis operates on an entirely different level of spite, power, and switch-hitting precision. Kelly might have the flashy reflexes to look cute for two or three rounds, but once Ennis starts cutting off the ring, targeting the body, and applying sustained heat, Kelly’s habit of pulling straight back with his hands down will catch up to him fast.

The foundation holding up Kelly’s sudden championship status looks shaky at best. Squeaking past Agyarko in Jeddah exposed all his familiar flaws. He spent long stretches coasting on the back foot, surviving on safety-first potshots, and failing to stamp any real authority on an opponent who had never operated anywhere near world level.

Before that, taking the belt off Murtazaliev raised plenty of eyebrows. Murtazaliev was relentlessly pressing the action, landing the heavier, more damaging blows while Kelly relied on flashy flurries that largely caught gloves and air. Handing Kelly a majority decision on home soil in Newcastle felt like a gift, not a definitive changing of the guard.

Locking Kelly down to a multi-fight extension right now puts Matchroom in a vulnerable spot. If the grand plan for 2027 is throwing him in against Ennis in a unification, Kelly’s market value could disappear in a defeat.

Sports.title: Gareth Davies Believes Tyson Fury Will Fight Daniel Dubois
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury could face Daniel Dubois after Anthony Joshua, according to Gareth A. Davies, who believes Fury possesses the skills to neutralize the newly crowned WBO heavyweight champion.

Davies floated the possibility following Dubois’s second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley. Although he now rates Dubois as the world’s best heavyweight, he still sees a route to victory for Fury through movement and ring intelligence.

“He’s got the skills to nullify Daniel Dubois, but he’s got to be at his very best,” Davies said to iFL TV. “He needs to be elusive, and he needs his movement, and I think that will be key in the fight. He’s certainly got the IQ to do it.”

Fury would give Dubois a different fight than Wardley did. His movement could force Dubois to keep turning and chasing him, making it harder to plant his feet and land his power shots.

Whether Fury can actually pull that off inside the ropes at this stage is a massive question mark.

Knowing the blueprint to mess with Dubois’ offense is one thing, but dragging those thirty-something legs through twelve rounds against a younger brawler constantly walking him down is another test entirely. Davies thinks a dominant win over Joshua might tempt Fury into stepping in with Dubois, though he floated it purely as speculation rather than a done deal.

“I can see the winner of Fury and Joshua, or either Fury and Joshua, fighting Daniel Dubois,” Davies said. “It’s probably because I want to see it.”

Davies also pointed to Dubois growing as a ring craftsman. He liked the composure Dubois showed while closing the show against Wardley, picking his spots without walking into incoming right-hand counters.

That added discipline makes life tough on Fury. Dubois wouldn’t have to outbox him minute by minute if relentless heat drains the gas tank and leaves Fury carrying concrete in his boots.

Gareth’s theory hinges entirely on Fury having the wheels to dictate where the action happens. If those legs are spent, keeping Dubois off his chest turns into a brutal fight.

Fury has shown zero real appetite to get anywhere near Daniel Dubois, and the reasons are obvious.

Dubois is in his physical prime, throws heavy artillery with both hands, and walks opponents down without blinking. For an aging Fury whose legs are not what they used to be, taking on a puncher like Dubois is high risk with little appeal.

Fury is looking for massive paydays against names that match his era, like Anthony Joshua, or manageable outings where he can control the terms without taking life-altering punishment. Getting cornered by Dubois, taking shots to the body, and being forced into a grueling trench battle simply does not fit Fury’s career plans at this point.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Faces WBA Appeal Rejection Over Catterall
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is convinced Teofimo Lopez will not wiggle out of facing Jack Catterall. Matchroom holds stack after stack of written promises from the WBA guaranteeing the mandatory order stands.

Teofimo’s camp wants an exception so they can chase a unification scrap with Ryan Garcia. Hearn is betting the WBA refuses to play along, forcing Teofimo to either step into the ring with Catterall or give up the welterweight crown.

“Teofimo has pushed back and said, ‘We don’t think we should have to fight Jack Catterall. We’d like to try and make another fight,’” Hearn told iFL TV. “Basically, the WBA are going to say no because we’ve had multiple dozens of assurances in writing through the resolution.”

The WBA ordered the fight on September 22, giving the sides until October 22 to negotiate. That deadline does not guarantee a ruling on Teofimo’s request that day. Failure to reach an agreement could lead to purse bids, depending on how the sanctioning body handles the pending petition.

Hearn claims Matchroom holds ironclad written guarantees from the WBA locking in the Catterall defense, leaving him convinced the sanctioning body will shut down Teofimo’s petition to steer elsewhere.

“Teofimo Lopez will have the decision to fight Jack Catterall or vacate the belt,” he said.

Hearn knows Teofimo would earn more fighting Ryan, but says that doesn’t give him a pass to skip Catterall.

“I get it. It’s not a fight that pays you as much money as Ryan Garcia, but it’s a good fight that pays you a lot of money,” Hearn said. “Do as champions should do and make the fight.”

Right now, Catterall sits on hold while Teofimo chases the bigger fight against Ryan. Enforcing the mandatory would give Catterall clarity, but it might not actually hand him the fight he wants. Teofimo can still chase the Ryan fight, but Hearn says he’ll have to give up his WBA belt to do it. He doesn’t expect the WBA to let him keep Catterall waiting.

If Teofimo vacates his WBA belt, fans will not call it a shrewd business maneuver, though. Many will call it a duck. It becomes Ryan defending his WBC title against a challenger who showed the boxing world he didn’t want to face a Catterall, who fights a lot like Shakur Stevenson.

For the Ryan Garcia bout, it knocks a massive dent in the promotional luster. More importantly, it destroys Teofimo’s bargaining power at the negotiation table. Without a belt, Teofimo loses any claim to parity. Ryan will dictate the purse split, the ring walks, the poster placement, and the rules of engagement. The moment Teofimo drops the title, the event gets downgraded.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Celebrates Shakur’s Zuffa Departure Without Addressing Cost
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn called Shakur Stevenson leaving Zuffa Boxing an outright embarrassment, but he skipped over the core financial question. How much money was Zuffa supposed to put up for the matchups Shakur demanded?

Hearn openly questioned how any promoter could lock down an elite talent, only to let him walk without staging a single fight.

“How can you sign your most high-profile fighter and then he leaves you without even fighting?” Hearn said to iFL TV about Shakur.

Optically, that hurts Zuffa. Still, it does not mean holding onto Shakur made sound business sense.

Reporter Sean Zittel reported that Shakur sought at least $15 million per outing, even for a bout against Rayo Valenzuela, with an even steeper price tag for Devin Haney. Those numbers matter when evaluating what ended this partnership.

Hearn praised Shakur for walking away, hinting he could join Haney over at DAZN.

“Of course we’re going to dine out on it, aren’t we? Because they would do the same thing,” Hearn admitted.

The real test is whether Matchroom can satisfy that reported price tag. If Shakur sticks to those demands, Hearn faces the exact math problem Zuffa chose to avoid.

Bringing up Conor Benn’s paydays misses the point. Benn commands a massive following across Britain. Shakur has not shown that kind of commercial pull in America. Pure ring skill does not automatically generate the ticket sales needed to justify a $15 million purse before covering the opponent’s guarantee or card production.

Zuffa letting him walk says plenty about where they drew the line. The promotion simply decided the cost outweighed the return. Until contract paperwork surfaces, neither party holds the full truth.

Hearn can celebrate a rival stumbling all he wants. Actually signing Shakur fight by fight takes serious cash. If that $15 million asking price stands, someone has to absorb that risk, and Hearn hasn’t explained how he plans to make the numbers work.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Claims He Can Dominate Emanuel Navarrete
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster insists he has Emanuel Navarrete completely figured out ahead of their October 24 unification bout in San Antonio. Foster plans to outclass him, take his belt, and force critics to treat him like an elite name at 130 pounds.

Foster claimed he could turn this into a one-sided blowout if he simply sticks to the outside and picks Navarrete apart.

“I believe not only that I can beat Navarrete, I believe that I can do it in a dominant fashion, a super dominant fashion,” Foster said to Bradley’s channel. “I can make it an easy night and just box his head off.”

At the same time, Foster called this matchup a nine out of ten in difficulty and admitted it represents the biggest threat of his career. Navarrete throws wild, looping bombs from angles nobody learns in the gym. Foster insists none of that will rattle him. He points to past rounds with Rey Vargas, Robson Conceicao, and Jon Fernandez as proof that he knows how to handle height, awkward attacks, and long-range pressure.

Navarrete brings chaos, not textbook mechanics. Surviving separate elements from past opponents does not guarantee Foster can absorb the non-stop pressure Navarrete brings from opening bell to the final seconds. Foster cannot afford to run and let rounds slip away on activity alone.

He claims he wants to dominate, yet talking about an easy night while hunting for a highlight reel finish creates immediate risk. If Foster gets trapped between cruising on points and trying to look spectacular, Navarrete will make him pay with relentless volume.

“I’m looking to come in to make a statement,” Foster said. “I’m coming in to put on a dominant performance, show the world who I really am.”

Trying to invent power and aggression at age 31 against Navarrete is playing with fire. If Foster wants to leave San Antonio with the belts, he has to accept who he is, ignore the crowd, use his legs, and be content with a disciplined, ugly points win. Anything else plays right into Navarrete’s hands.

Foster has his sights set on undisputed status before jumping up in weight. Talking about blowing through Navarrete is bold talk, but a flat decision win will not deliver the respect he expects. Foster made big promises, and on October 24, he has to back them up against a puncher who never stops coming forward.

Ghana News.title: BBC Three, BBC Scotland and Radio 4 Extra broadcast channels to close
Ghana News.content:
The BBC will close its BBC Three and BBC Scotland television channels in the spring, as the corporation continues to save £500m over two years.

Both services will become online-only, meaning they will continue to produce and host some content on iPlayer, without the need to fill a terrestrial TV schedule.

The BBC has also announced the closure of Radio 4 Extra, which largely airs speech programmes from the BBC's archive, including comedy, drama and documentaries.

BBC director-general Matt Brittin said: "We need to make every pound work harder for audiences as we respond to the immediate cost pressures and reinvent the BBC for a changing world. We all know that means tough choices."

Discussing the closure of linear broadcast services, Brittin said: "Much of the great content they currently carry will still be found where audiences already enjoy them on iPlayer and Sounds.

"While this follows media speculation, I recognise the confirmation of this news will be hard for audiences and colleagues."

Outlining the plans, the corporation confirmed:

BBC Scotland will remain a channel on iPlayer, with some content also broadcast on BBC One and BBC Two in Scotland

BBC Three commissions, supported by increased investment in content for younger audiences, will be available on BBC iPlayer and on other platforms including YouTube

Some programmes that air on Radio 4 Extra will be available on BBC Sounds - while its religious programme The Daily Service will be on BBC Sounds and local radio

BBC Three launched hits including Gavin & Stacey, which returned for a Christmas finale in 2024

BBC Three, aimed at young audiences and home to hits such as Fleabag, Normal People and Gavin & Stacey, moved online in 2016 but was reinstated as a TV channel in 2022.

BBC Scotland launched as a channel in 2019, broadcasting a variety of Scottish programming including news, sport, documentaries and entertainment.

However, some shows on the two networks, such as Two Doors Down on BBC Scotland and Sort Your Life Out on BBC Three, are repeats of episodes originally broadcast on other, more mainstream BBC channels.

Both networks currently broadcast TV programming only in the evenings, although BBC Scotland simulcasts BBC Radio Scotland for the rest of the day.

The BBC said that the network's nightly programme Reporting Scotland: News at Seven will not move to BBC iPlayer and will cease when the linear channel closes.

BBC Scotland's wider news offering will continue to serve audiences, including Reporting Scotland, The Sunday Show, Radio Scotland Breakfast, Debate Night and Scotcast, the corporation said.

While Radio 4 Extra airs some original programming, its schedule is mostly archive content, much of which is available on BBC Sounds.

Sir Peter Bazalgette, former chairman of ITV and production company Endemol, told BBC News: "This is a modest and pretty well-judged package.

"The essence of it is it protects the spending on content, it really cuts money in the distribution of programmes, and it really had to happen because the BBC has lost 30% of its revenue in 10 years."

But entertainment trade union Equity said Tuesday's announcement "does not signal a thriving BBC, and we are concerned about the UK's preeminent public service broadcaster's ability to meet its duties to the fullest".

Staff affected by the changes were told on Tuesday, although some media outlets had reported the proposed closure of BBC Scotland and BBC Three in recent weeks.

The BBC aims to cut between 1,800 and 2,000 jobs, almost one in 10, to save £500m over two years as it faces "significant financial pressures".

Around 550 job closures have already been announced in the news, while BBC Sport has so far announced more than 30 job cuts.

The newly appointed director of BBC News, Rachel Jupp, announced on Tuesday that the BBC is proposing a further £5.5m in savings, which would mean closing around 100 roles.

Meanwhile, the BBC has cancelled several high-profile TV series in recent weeks.The BBC has dropped

RuPaul's Drag Race UK, Blankety Blank, Celebrity Mastermind, Live at the Apollo, Football Focus, Ski Sunday, and Radio 4’s The World Tonight and You & Yours so far.

Ghana News.title: Elon Musk says Tesla-SpaceX merger being considered
Ghana News.content:
Elon Musk said he likes the idea of merging Tesla and SpaceX, two of his most notable companies, and that it is under active consideration.

"Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes," Musk said during a call with financial analysts over the quarterly business results of SpaceX on Tuesday.

While Musk noted that such a merger is not certain and would need shareholders' support, he said special committees within both companies have been formed to examine the move.

"The special committees have not reached agreement on terms of any transaction, and there's no guarantee that they will," Musk added. "But I do think there is a lot of merit to merging and a lot to be gained."

With Tesla valued at roughly $1.5 trillion and SpaceX at $2 trillion, combining the two companies would mark one of the largest mergers in history.

Over the last year, Musk has brought more of his companies under fewer banners. Before it went public earlier this year, SpaceX acquired xAI and X, the platform formerly known as Twitter, both of which Musk owned.

The recent launch of Terafab, a joint effort between Tesla and SpaceX to manufacture computer chips, was another signal that Musk sees his companies as potentially more effective when working together.

Musk said on Tuesday that a full merger between the two companies would make sense given the work each is doing on chips, artificial intelligence, software, and more.

Musk, who became the world's first paper trillionaire after SpaceX's stock market debut earlier this year, said he is not on either of the special committees considering the mega-merger.

He described himself as a "conflicted party" as Tesla and SpaceX's chief executive.

Even commenting on a possible merger between the two companies, Musk compared it to "tap dancing through a minefield".

He added that shareholders would ultimately decide on a merger. At least 50% of Tesla's shareholders would need to approve the merger, which Musk described as "quite a high hurdle to achieve".

Shareholders have supported Musk's desires before. Last year, a majority of Tesla investors approved a compensation package for Musk valued at around $1 trillion.

While Tesla is known as an electric car company, Musk has recently shifted resources to focus on robotics.

SpaceX quickly outstripped Tesla in market value when it made its stock market debut.

The company, which builds space rockets and Starlink internet satellites, is now expanding into offering cloud compute capacity for other tech companies, like Anthropic and Google.

That line of business is now SpaceX's most profitable, bringing in $7.5bn, according to the latest quarterly results.

Ghana News.title: Turkish FA bans 147 officials for breaching betting rules
Ghana News.content:
Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan has been named among 147 football club officials to receive 45-day bans from the Turkish Football Federation (TFF) for breaching betting rules.

In September, the TFF announced that it had provisionally suspended 448 people and referred them to its professional football disciplinary board over allegations they placed bets while in office.

Like players and coaches, TFF regulations, along with those of FIFA and UEFA, forbid match officials from participating in betting activities.

The TFF said the people involved had held posts at clubs in the top two divisions in Turkish football over the previous five years.

Of those, some 147 breached betting rules and will be barred from carrying out duties in football during the suspension period.

There were insufficient grounds for disciplinary action in the other 301 cases.

The Turkish football authorities have clamped down on betting in the sport over the last year.

In November 2025, a TFF investigation handed bans to 149 referees and 1,204 players.

Ghana News.title: FGMSA sues Medical and Dental Council to halt Common Registration Examination
Ghana News.content:
The Federation of Ghana Medical Students’ Associations (FGMSA) and affected graduating medical and dental students have sued the Medical and Dental Council (MDC), seeking to restrain the regulator from conducting the Common Registration Examination (CRE).

In a statement issued on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, and signed by its National Executive Council, FGMSA said the case had been filed at the High Court’s Human Rights Division in Accra.

The applicants are seeking an injunction to prevent the examination from being conducted pending the determination of the substantive legal issues before the court.

The action follows unsuccessful attempts to resolve their concerns through engagement with the relevant authorities, according to the Federation.

“FGMSA remains committed to protecting the interests of medical and dental students and will pursue the legal process to its conclusion,” the statement said.

The Common Registration Examination is a new licensing examination introduced by the MDC for graduating medical and dental students.

Its implementation has drawn opposition from some students, who have raised concerns about the examination and its potential implications for their careers.

FGMSA said it had previously engaged the MDC and other relevant authorities in an effort to resolve the concerns, but those efforts did not produce an agreement, prompting the legal action.

The application seeks to prevent the MDC from proceeding with the examination while the court considers the issues raised by the applicants.

The specific legal arguments and reliefs sought beyond the injunction were not detailed in the statement.

The timing of the hearing and whether the court will grant the injunction were also not specified.

The case is therefore pending, and the court’s decision will determine whether the examination can proceed while the substantive legal challenge remains before it.

Ghana News.title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting
Ghana News.content:
The UK audit regulator has confirmed it is leading inquiries into accounting irregularities at Manchester City.

The Financial Reporting Council confirmed in a letter to the House of Commons Business, Culture, and Sport Committee that it had taken over "regulatory consideration" of the case from the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales on 30 September.

No formal investigation has started, but the FRC is investigating the case.

This follows an independent commission finding Manchester City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, including artificially inflating the club's financial position by more than £900m. City are appealing the verdict.

The FRC has greater resources and powers to impose sanctions if it finds evidence of violations. It routinely oversees accounting standards at bigger institutions such as listed public companies, but not football clubs.

The FRC can investigate the conduct of BDO, Manchester City's auditors, to determine whether the audit complied with the rules.

It can also sanction individuals, such as directors or employees of the Etihad club, if they are members of professional accountancy bodies.

BDO is the UK's fifth-biggest accounting firm, but claims to be a market leader in football, advising more Premier League and Championship clubs than any other firm.

The independent commission that investigated Manchester City found that the club gave its auditors a "misleading impression" of the scheme used to disguise the origin of shareholder funds injected into the club, and that the auditors were "unaware" of the scheme.

Manchester City said it will appeal the commission's decision, arguing it contains "material errors of law, principle and fact and is unsafe".

Liam Byrne, chair of the business select committee, called for greater powers for the FRC to look into similar cases.

He wrote on X: "The regulator's letter exposes gaps in its ability to compel evidence from the club and pursue directors who fall outside its disciplinary rules.

"This raises serious questions about the powers available to hold companies and directors to account.

"The government has a responsibility to explain why reforms to close these gaps were abandoned - and what will now be done to strengthen accountability."

BDO declined to comment.

Ghana News.title: Doue impresses as PSG beat Barcelona in thriller
Ghana News.content:
Desire Doue, Lamine Yamal and Vitinha scored superb individual goals as Champions League holders Paris St-Germain overcame Barcelona in a breathless encounter at Parc des Princes.

After starring in PSG's victory against Manchester City last week, Doue opened the scoring in the 38th minute of a first half in which both sides missed several clear chances.

Teenage full-back Xavi Espart drew Barcelona level early in the second half with a rifled near-post effort, before PSG defender Lucas Hernandez powered in a towering header.

Lamine Yamal made it 2-2 with a genius near-post finish, but less than two minutes later Vitinha sent a volley into the bottom corner to reclaim the lead for PSG.

Fabian Ruiz put the result beyond doubt five minutes later by converting Achraf Hakimi's low cross at the back post, in a win that ends Barcelona's 11-match unbeaten run at the start of their season.

The Parisians had wasted little time in implementing their high-pressing gameplan to force Barcelona into several mistakes in the early stages.

The game was 79 seconds old when Khvicha Kvaratskhelia struck the foot of the post after Pedri was dispossessed, before Doue and Ousmane Dembele were denied by Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia following high turnovers.

It was then Barcelona's turn to launch their own rapid attacks, but Raphinha could only fire straight at Matvey Safonov in the PSG goal after running on to a neat Anthony Gordon pass.

Garcia had a busy end to the half as he twice denied former Barcelona team-mate Ferran Torres - who replaced the injured Dembele - but the goalkeeper could do nothing about Doue's opener.

After PSG intercepted a Barca ball out from defence, Doue drove to the edge of the penalty area and rifled a low shot into the bottom left corner.

Minutes before half-time Fermin Lopez was thwarted in a one-on-one situation by Safonov, but 10 minutes into the second half Espart, 19, beat the Russian goalkeeper at his near post after bursting into the box.

Barcelona were starting to look the more likely side to claim a winner, but, moments after Torres hit the post following a quick counter, Hernandez planted a header past Garcia from a corner.

Out of nothing, Lamine Yamal then turned Warren Zaire-Emery, sprinted into the box and squeezed the ball in between Safonov and the post.

Just as the momentum looked to have swung in Barca's favour, Vitinha controlled a clearance with his chest before launching a stunning volley into the bottom corner, before Ruiz put the seal on an exhilarating match.

PSG have nine points and will next face Villarreal in Spain on Tuesday, 3 November (20:00 GMT).

Barcelona remain on six points and will host Aston Villa at Camp Nou at the same time.

Ghana News.title: Four-goal Roma thrash Yaya Toure’s Slovan Bratislava
Ghana News.content:
Molina celebrates Roma's second as they comfortably beat Slovan Bratislava

Ruthless Roma stuck four past Yaya Toure's Slovan Bratislava to secure their first Champions League victory of the season.

Goals from Mario Hermoso, Nahuel Molina, Niccolo Pisilli and Donyell Malen sparked the Serie A side's European campaign into life on what is their return to the competition for the first time since 2019.

Roma suffered a shocking late collapse last week to lose 4-3 against Real Madrid as they conceded three goals in the last seven minutes.

But they bounced back here and were in front against the Slovakian side inside 21 minutes when Hermoso headed in almost on the goal-line after Daniele Ghilardi nodded down Lorenzo Pellegrini's free-kick.

Roma were dominant against the side managed by former Manchester City midfielder Toure and got a deserved second six minutes before the break.

Molina forced the ball home at the back post for his first goal for the club after Brastislava keeper Dominik Takac pushed ex-Aston Villa forward Malen's shot across goal.

Roma, who drew their opening European game of the season against Fenerbahce, took advantage of some hesitant defending early in the second half to get their third.

Matias Soule managed to win the ball in the area before Malen played the ball back for Pisilli to turn home in the 52nd minute.

Malen then got the fourth from the penalty spot just before the hour mark after Cesar Blackman fouled Wesley Franca to leave Toure's side bottom of the Champions League table.

Ghana News.title: Nigeria confirms first Ebola case amid concerns about continental spread
Ghana News.content:
Nigeria has confirmed its first Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who travelled from Uganda tested positive for the virus.

The case in the West African country comes amid an outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and some cases in Kenya, raising concerns about a spread across the continent.

According to Nigeria’s Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the woman began showing symptoms on October 7 and was admitted to a private hospital in Abuja on October 11, before being diagnosed with Ebola.

Health Minister Muhammad Pate said authorities had begun trying to trace 44 people who came into contact with the patient.

“We are doing everything possible to contain this case by tracing all the contacts the individual may have had,” he said.

New case in Kenya

Earlier on Tuesday, Kenya confirmed ⁠its ninth case of Ebola.

A 24-year-old man, who was already being held in quarantine, is the latest to test positive, Kenya’s Ministry of Health said in a statement on Tuesday.

“He was isolated at the first sign of illness, tested and started on treatment immediately upon confirmation of his positive test result,” it said, adding he “was already in quarantine when he fell ill”.

The man was a close family member of Kenya’s first Ebola patient, who had travelled from the DRC, through Uganda and before arriving in Kenya and dying at a Nairobi hospital on ⁠October 5.

“All nine cases belong to one cluster, and as of ‌today there is no evidence of transmission outside this group,” Director-General for Health Patrick Amoth said in a statement on Tuesday.

“Eight patients are stable and responding well to treatment, while 134 of 135 contacts have been traced and quarantined,” Amoth said.

Amoth said a milestone was in sight for the majority of the contacts in quarantine as they had remained well for the 21-day monitoring period and could return home from October 25.

It appealed to communities to welcome them back, saying they “pose no risk of infection”.

The ministry said no infections had occurred within quarantine facilities and that it was continuously monitoring infection-prevention measures to protect health workers.

Despite the nine infections, Kenya has not imposed restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings, with authorities saying the country remains open for business.

In the DRC, there have been more than 9,000 Ebola cases and 4,000 deaths since May.

The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control says it’s the second-largest epidemic on record.

It has been difficult to contain because there is no licensed vaccine or specific treatment for the Bundibugyo strain of the virus.

Uganda had previously reported Ebola cases but was later declared free of the virus.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: NATO to send additional patrol planes to Black Sea after drone attacks
World.content:
The alliance announces after a chain of deadly drone attacks have struck the region.

Share NATO to send additional patrol planes to Black Sea after drone attacks on social media

NATO is deploying additional patrol aircraft and intelligence personnel to the Black Sea, a spokesman for the alliance said, after a series of deadly drone attacks in the region widely blamed on Russia but denied by the Kremlin.

“Allies have or will send additional maritime patrol aircraft, radar systems, explosive exploitation teams, intelligence personnel, drones and more to the Black Sea,” said Colonel Martin O’Donnell on Tuesday.

“The most important thing we can do, however, is to increase our situational awareness in the region through increased sensors and data sharing,” he added.

NATO, along with Bulgaria and Romania, has not directly attributed the recent spate of attacks to any country. Military analysts have said Russia almost certainly carried out the attacks but Moscow has not acknowledged any responsibility.

In an attack on October 5, Romania reported two people dead after their ship caught fire and sank in Black Sea waters. Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Moscow of being responsible.

The announcement came after NATO’s main decision-making body, the North Atlantic Council, discussed security in the Black Sea at the alliance’s Brussels headquarters.

“NATO has already strengthened our posture along the eastern flank, including with counter-drone capabilities,” spokeswoman Allison Hart said earlier in a post on X.

‘Dangerous and unacceptable’ escalation

The European Union’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas on Tuesday said that “six attacks in 10 days by suspected Russian drones marks a dangerous and unacceptable escalation”, adding that the Kremlin likely sought to choke off revenue to Kyiv from grain exports.

Kallas warned that the latest strikes were adding to a “perfect storm” facing global food supplies already being battered by droughts in multiple regions and the war in the Middle East.



Last week, seven sailors were reported missing after drones struck two chemical tankers near Romania’s Black Sea coast, setting them ablaze and raising fresh security concerns along a vital shipping route used by Ukraine.

At least five other cargo vessels were hit near the coasts of Romania and neighbouring NATO member Bulgaria over the previous 10 days, with at least 23 sailors reported missing or dead.

World.title: The Gambia to pay reparations to ex-dictator’s victims from sale of US mansion
World.content:
Share The Gambia to pay reparations to ex-dictator’s victims from sale of US mansion on social media

Gambian authorities have announced that funds from the sale of the country’s former president’s mansion in the United States would be used to pay reparations to victims of his rule.

The Gambia Reparations Commission confirmed Tuesday that it received just more than $2.5m from the sale of a property in the wealthy Washington, DC suburb of Potomac, Maryland, belonging to ex-President Yahya Jammeh.

The commission, which was set up to compensate victims of abuses committed during Jammeh’s 22-year rule ending in 2017, said in a statement that “the funds were deposited directly into the Reparations Fund account at the Central Bank of The Gambia and shall only be utilized for the payment of reparations”.

“The Commission is committed to ensuring that the funds are managed responsibly, transparently and accountably, with due regard to the rights and needs of victims and survivors,” it added.

Jammeh currently lives in Equatorial Guinea, after he was forced out under pressure from The Gambia’s West African neighbours following his 2016 election loss to current President Adama Barrow.

He is accused of presiding over the murder of political opponents, disappearances, rape and torture.

A commission of inquiry estimated that between 240 and 250 victims were killed by Jammeh’s forces in the former British colony of two million people.

Proceeds from corruption

President Barrow said in a statement that his government would heed any recommendations by official auditors on how the funds would be allocated to victims.



The US Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint in 2020 alleging that the property was bought with proceeds of corruption. A court ordered its forfeiture in 2022.

The property, it asserted, was purchased through a trust set up by Jammeh’s wife.

The US Justice Department had announced in September that it would return the funds from the mansion sale to The Gambia.

World.title: ‘I don’t care how it’s done’: Trump pressures Ukraine to cut peace deal
World.content:
The US president’s remarks come amid a deepening feud with Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Amid escalating tensions with Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy, United States President Donald Trump has increased pressure on the Eastern European country to make a deal that would end the war with Russia.

Speaking at the White House on Tuesday, Trump doubled down on his efforts to blame the Ukrainian president for holding up peace efforts that would bring the years-long conflict to a close.

“Zelenskyy has to want to settle this war, and if he doesn’t, I think it’s going to be a very bad thing,” Trump said as he talked about Russia having an “unlimited” supply of people to send in the fight.

Moments later, the US president referenced a contentious Oval Office meeting he held with Zelenskyy in February 2025, shortly after returning to power.

Zelenskyy, Trump said, could have made a “better deal” then. “He’s going to have to want to make a deal, because I don’t think his people are going to stand for it any longer,” Trump told reporters.

On Tuesday, the Ukrainian president met US special envoy Steve Witkoff and European leaders in Oslo, Norway, to discuss ending Russia’s war.

In a post on social media after the meeting concluded, Zelenskyy said, without providing specifics, that his country has “some clear ideas on how to get to peace”.

“We are united with our European partners in this effort, and we want the Americans to take these ideas to the Russians,” Zelenskyy wrote. “One of the important ideas is to move to a potential trilateral meeting of the leaders to address the issues that only the leaders can do.”



The Ukrainian leader added that Witkoff would head to Russia on Wednesday, where peace discussions are expected to continue.

“Let’s see what Putin has to say,” Zelenskyy said.

When asked whether Russian President Vladimir Putin should meet Zelenskyy, Trump said there was “tremendous” hatred between the two leaders.

“It’s hard for them to be in the same room,” Trump said. “I don’t care how it’s done.”

Starlink controversy

Trump’s remarks come as the White House continues to squeeze Ukraine in order to force the country to cut a deal with Russia.

Last week, Ukrainian officials reported slowdowns with Starshield, the military-grade version of the Starlink satellite system, run by the aerospace company SpaceX.

Ukraine relies on the technology for communications and intelligence to prevent Russian attacks.

It is unclear who ordered restrictions that limit Ukraine’s access to Starshield. SpaceX CEO and Trump ally Elon Musk pointed a finger at the White House.

“Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” he wrote on October 14.

The news agency Reuters also reported that the order came from inside the White House, citing two US officials and a Western official.

But a report in The Wall Street Journal on Tuesday claimed US officials had blamed Musk himself for the slowdown, saying the SpaceX CEO ordered it last week. Trump and US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth have both denied that the government directed the restrictions, with Hegseth pushing responsibility towards SpaceX.

Building ties with Putin

Trump, meanwhile, has sought to ease the historically tense relations between Russia and the US.

In August 2025, Trump invited Putin to Alaska, the Russian leader’s first visit to US soil in a decade.

More recently, Trump has expressed openness this month to meeting with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, as part of a trilateral discussion on denuclearisation.

Trump also announced this month that he struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, marking a stunning reversal of years of US pressure on Moscow’s economy.

The US president also waived new economic restrictions that would have been imposed under the Lindsey Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, a bipartisan law he signed one month earlier, in honour of a late senator.

It would have imposed sanctions on Russian officials, banks and tankers, as well as tariffs on countries that purchase Russian oil.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended the decision on Tuesday, saying the law allowed the waiver through a provision embedded in the legislation.



“The president chose to use a national security waiver to not immediately implement those [sanctions and restrictions], because he recognises that these things have to be looked at in their totality,” Rubio said in an interview with India’s News18.

Rubio argued that Trump was engaged in a “balancing act” in deciding the extent of US-imposed economic restrictions and how they could impact the rest of the world.

“When you do that pressure, sometimes it spills over and has a negative impact on other countries,” Rubio said.

World.title: Trump commits more than $400m ahead of high-stakes midterm elections
World.content:
The president’s Republican Party seeks to maintain its hold over both chambers of Congress, despite declining poll numbers.

Share Trump commits more than $400m ahead of high-stakes midterm elections on social media

United States President Donald Trump has announced he plans to spend more than $400m to help Republican candidates win the November 3 midterm elections as his party fights to maintain its grip on Congress.

In a post on his Truth Social platform on Tuesday, Trump wrote that much of that total had already been spent on campaign outreach.

“More than 300 Million Dollars has already been spent on Advertising, Direct and Indirect Voter Contact, Rallies, Rally Arenas, Telerallies, Get Out the Vote Programs, Election Integrity, and more,” Trump said.

“It is my Great Honor to do so on behalf of the Republican Party, which has done so much to bring our Country back from the Edge of Oblivion.”

He added that the November vote was “the Most Important Midterm Elections in our Country’s History”.

The president offered no detailed breakdown of the spending, including how much would reach individual races.

But the promised influx of spending comes as Trump’s Republican Party faces headwinds ahead of the election, including pushback over the economy and the protracted US-Israeli war against Iran.

In the lead-up to the vote, Trump’s approval ratings have tumbled to record lows. A poll this week from the news agency Reuters and the research firm Ipsos found that only 31 percent of Americans approved of Trump’s job performance so far.

Some Republicans have sought to distance themselves from the president as a result. Others have pushed for greater support, particularly for close races with Democrats.

Questions have swirled over whether Trump and his allies would tap into the war chest amassed by MAGA Inc, the super PAC named for his “Make America Great Again” movement.



As a super PAC — or political action committee — MAGA Inc can raise unlimited sums from donors to support or oppose federal candidates. But its spending is legally required to remain independent of their campaigns.

Last month, the Campaign Legal Center (CLC), a campaign finance watchdog, accused Trump of violating those rules by claiming control over MAGA Inc’s expenditures.

The group cited the president’s public statements, including an exchange with reporters in the Oval Office on September 4, when Trump was asked when the money would start flowing to Republican candidates.
