Courts are not beyond criticism, however. Their decisions must remain open to rigorous analysis by lawyers, scholars, the media, enlightened citizens and by history. Reasoned criticism forms part of constitutional democracy and can strengthen judicial authority. What must be protected is the distinction between criticism of judicial reasoning and destruction of confidence in adjudication. If every politically significant judgment is immediately interpreted as evidence of partisan allegiance merely because it disadvantages one side, the possibility of neutral constitutional authority becomes endangered.

Sadly, this tendency has increasingly entered public consciousness in Nigeria. That is where a boundary must be established in the criticism of the Constitution and the Judiciary, as is often demonstrated by the misguided enthusiasm and exuberance of the proponents of restructuring in Nigeria. We concede that the Court must recognise that public confidence cannot simply be demanded. It must be earned through consistency, transparent reasoning, fidelity to precedent where appropriate and clear explanation where departure becomes necessary. Finality is a formidable power, and the obligation to explain must therefore be correspondingly greater. But that recognition is central to the selection and appointment of judges of the Apex Court.

Judicial independence has institutional and ethical dimensions. Judges must be protected from intimidation and improper interference while remaining detached from partisan, sectional, confessional and personal considerations. This independence is not a personal privilege. It protects citizens and the state itself. Political fortunes are temporary, but constitutional institutions must aspire to permanence.

The national interest must therefore be distinguished from the interests of any government, party, religion, region or influential personality. Against the fact that governments change, presidents leave office, legislatures get reconstituted and parties rise and fall, the deeper national interest lies in preserving the framework within which such changes can occur peacefully without imperilling the Republic. The permanence of the Judiciary is therefore the solid pillar upon which the Federation rests.

This brings us to a distinction that should remain constantly in view. The Supreme Court must be profoundly conscious of the national interest, but it must never become a court of national expediency. By this I mean a situation where the Court arrives at a decision that may appear convenient at a particular moment. However, the overriding national interest is concerned with what principles will preserve constitutional government over time. The long-term stability of Nigeria depends not upon whether one side is accommodated today, but upon whether all sides believe that the same constitutional rules will remain available to them tomorrow and in perpetuity.

This is why fidelity to law is itself a form of statecraft and the foundation of the national interest. The Supreme Court does not govern Nigeria, but it helps determine the constitutional conditions under which Nigeria can continue to be governed peacefully. Likewise, it does not manufacture national unity, but provides a mechanism through which disputes threatening that unity may be resolved under law. Although it is not a forum for discourse on governance, its judgments necessarily form part of public-policy development.

In that sense, the Court is one of the custodians of the Republic. Its ultimate duty is neither to please government nor opposition, neither to satisfy popular sentiment nor to resist it for its own sake. Its duty is to uphold the Constitution with courage, wisdom, independence and restraint. Justice, in this larger sense, is not separate from the national interest. It is one of its highest expressions. These are the principles that I have learned in listening to The Honourable Justice Sidi Dauda Bage Muhammad I.

World.title: Igbo rebuff of today’s Nigerian Army (I), by Ochereome Nnanna
World.content:
Ochereome Nnanna

For some years now, youths of the Igbo ethnic group, especially in the five states of the South East geopolitical zone, have been shunning enrolment into the military. In 2025, a Brigadier General, Chima Ekeator, led a team round the geopolitical zone canvassing for Igbo youths to take up their quotas. For instance, he said Kaduna State indigenes, like youths of most other states, oversubscribed their state quota, while Enugu State failed to raise up to 100 recruits to fill its 200 slots. This year, the Brigadier General in charge of the Nigerian Army’s Ohafia Division, A. M. Dikko, lamented that he failed to fill his slot as only a few showed up for recruitment.

The question is: why have Igbo youths lost interest in the same Army they once bestrode like the proverbial colossus? The answer is simple: no sense of belonging. Before Nigeria’s independence and the Biafra War, Igbo and Eastern youths dominated the officer corps of the Nigerian military and security services. The Igbo were at the forefront of the fight for Nigeria’s independence, and they looked forward, alongside their compatriots, to defending its sovereignty. For some of those graduating from colleges, the military offered a prestigious career opportunity.

Pioneers like the billionaire’s son, Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu (who joined the officer corps after obtaining a Master’s degree at Oxford), Okoh Ebitu Ukiwe, Godwin Ndubuisi Kanu, Allison Madueke, Alexander Madiebo, Obi Rapu and so many others joined the Army and Navy in the late 1950s. Madiebo, in his book, Nigerian Revolution and Biafra War, documents how, by 1963, Igbo officers dominated the Nigerian Army. Indeed, the very first full General and first military Head of State of Nigeria was an Igbo man – Johnson Thomas Aguiyi-Ironsi. For whatever it is worth, I need to recall that the first military coup was led by an Igbo man, Major Chukwuma Kaduna Nzeogwu, and Ironsi, as Head of State, led the forces to quell the coup. This says it all: Ndi Igbo once occupied the alpha position in the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

Let me also note that the Igbo did not join the lower ranks with the same enthusiasm. This “other ranks” cadre was dominated mainly by Hausa and Northern elements, which were later mobilised to attack their Igbo officers when the first coup occasioned the killing of Northern political leaders. After the Biafra War, many Igbo youths desired to rejoin the Nigerian armed forces, more especially as Gen. Yakubu Gowon proclaimed his fraudulent “No Victor, No Vanquished”, giving the impression that the nation had put the war behind it. What actually happened was that the British-manipulated Federal Military Government sought to hoodwink the ex-Biafrans while the war was continued through hostile government policies. Many Igbo youths who struggled to join the Army, Police, Air Force and other uniformed forces were either stiff-armed or given a ceiling above which they would not be allowed to rise.

They endured decades of marginalisation, early retirement and exclusion from occupying certain ranks and command positions. They kept struggling until just about a decade ago, when Muhammadu Buhari came back to power as an elected president. The only time, since the War, when an Igbo, Lt.-General Azubuike Ihejirika, was appointed Chief of Army Staff, was during the regime of President Goodluck Jonathan. Ihejirika was the last Nigerian Army Chief who fought Boko Haram terrorists like the Nigerian Army we all knew and respected. He was on the verge of defeating the jihadists when, suddenly, Northern politicians and Islamic clerics began accusing him and President Jonathan of “fighting the North” and “killing Northerners”.

The Sultan of Sokoto, Nasir el-Rufai, Muhammadu Buhari and Borno elders were all on this chorus. Indeed, Amnesty International (AI), curiously, joined them, showing more concern for the dirty blows being administered on the terrorists than for the fate of Boko Haram victims in North East communities and refugee camps. President Jonathan, who was fervently seeking Northern support for his second term, panicked and retired Gen. Ihejirika. He handed over his government’s security architecture fully back to the North, thus setting the stage for Buhari’s victory at the 2015 presidential election.

Apart from appointing Ihejirika the first Igbo Chief of Army Staff, President Jonathan, who owed his 2011 election into the presidency mainly to the sacrifice of the Igbo nation in his favour, also “committed” another unpardonable taboo. He used the Nigerian Army to give Ikemba Odumegwu Ojukwu a full military burial with a 21-gun salute on 2nd March, 2012, at Nnewi. This five-star rite was also accorded Nigeria’s leading fighter for independence and first President, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, in November 1996. The Sokoto Caliphate and Arewa cabals see Nigeria as the private estate of their ancestors, and the Army as their ultimate instrument of power over Nigeria. Whatever the votes cannot achieve, the Army will achieve for them. We other Nigerians also claim that Nigeria and the Armed Forces belong to us all, as the Constitution says. But in the end, both Nigeria and its Armed Forces dance to the tune of the Sokoto Caliphate and its Arewa cabals.

Indeed, the notion that the Nigerian Army owes more of its allegiance to the Islamic Sokoto Caliphate and Arewa cabals than to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria is encapsulated in its motto, boldly inscribed in Arabic: “Victory is from Allah alone.” When taken to task, the Army likes to interpret it as “Victory is from God alone” to water down the Islamic overtone. Yet, they vehemently refuse to write it in the Nigerian lingua franca that we all understand, as sanctioned by the Constitution: English. The Army is thus portrayed as a tool of Islam, which is an affront to non-Muslims, particularly Ndi Igbo.

We conclude in part two.

World.title: Building myths around the NCC Device Checker, by Okoh Aihe
World.content:
Okoh Aihe

The NCC Device Checker came on stream on October 7, 2026. Although it was expressly stated that all SIM-enabled devices already connected before the date were automatically verified, with no action needed from the user, I still took my devices through the process of verification by dialing *315#. Here is the result returned for both phones: “This device is NCC Type Approved and verified for use on Nigerian mobile networks.” I needed to be very sure that the backend had been properly sorted before the telecommunications regulator, the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), could introduce such a very technical process into the regulatory space. It is commonplace for us to see certain things promoted with so much fanfare and bravura, only to find the readiness of such products absolutely wanting. On this particular issue, for me, the NCC may have scored high.

“The Device Checker,” according to the regulator, “is an NCC Type Approved service for checking whether a SIM-enabled device model is NCC Type Approved and whether the device is for use on Nigerian mobile networks.” Through the process, the regulator is taking Type Approval a notch higher. “Type Approval is a requirement under Nigerian law that every communications device meets approved technical standards before it is sold or used in the country. It ensures that all device models brought into the country are fit for use in Nigeria. It is prohibited to use, sell or import non-Type Approved communications devices,” the NCC explained. Type Approval is as old as the Communications Act but has been given more impetus now by the regulator in order to clip some subtle features which conspire to degrade the signal quality received by subscribers from the networks. Unfortunately, the fault or failure to receive or connect equipment can easily be classified as network failure. Type Approval is one regulation with which the regulator planned to attack multi-pronged issues.

“The integrity of the telecommunications industry depends not only on network infrastructure but also on the quality, safety and compliance of the devices that access and are used on these networks. For this reason, Type Approval is not merely a regulatory requirement. It is a vital mechanism for protecting consumers, safeguarding network performance and preserving confidence in Nigeria’s digital economy,” explained Engr. Edoyemi Ogoh, who is Director, Technical Standards and Network Integrity at NCC. “The initiative,” he continued, “supports the Commission’s broader efforts to strengthen the integrity of devices in Nigeria’s telecommunications sector. It will improve compliance with applicable standards, enhance network performance, facilitate the identification of non-compliant devices, and strengthen consumer confidence in devices sold and used within the country.” The NCC Device Checker has been long in the making, like the meat of the antelope, which takes long to cook in order to achieve maximum delicacy. The regulator said it has consulted with stakeholders across the value chain, which include the Nigeria Customs Service, Original Equipment Manufacturers, importers and relevant market associations, adding that “this collaborative approach reflects our belief that effective regulation is best achieved through partnership, consultation and shared responsibility, consistent with firm belief in collaboration.”

In my very simple observation, the regulator is waging a full-fledged war against the grey market through which millions of devices pour into the Nigerian market, phone theft, which is prevalent in this part of the world – a stolen phone can now easily be knocked off the networks – and ensuring the fidelity of products. Phone buyers are investing in genuine products that can deliver proper service by following the International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) number at the back of the phone pack or even doing the needful to confirm second-hand phones. As one industry source told this writer, this would also mean the Customs Service making more money through revenue generation, because, at the moment, it was possible for cars or buses to be imported into Nigeria with lots of phones in them which are not properly cleared or even have their sources determined, except that their destination is Nigeria. The Device Checker has drawn a line against such practices. Understandably, not everybody is excited about the NCC Device Checker. The Association of Mobile Phones and Allied Products Traders of Nigeria has raised some concerns about the introduction of the Device Checker, asking the NCC to provide a window of sensitisation in order to align all stakeholders with its plans. Even as they support the fight against counterfeit devices, the association is frowning at sundry fees that may be introduced, which could bring more hardship on its members and phone and device buyers.

But what is this thing about counterfeit devices? I will tell a personal story. I have an iPad which plays a central role in all my operations. Recently, the charger got bad, and I decided to buy one from a shopping mall nearby before heading out to Banex Plaza to buy an original version the following day. I plugged the iPad with the stop-gap charger and stepped out of the room for some minutes. By the time I returned, the room was charged and very hot. My mind went to the iPad, which was as hot as fire itself. Just a few minutes’ delay, and it would have exploded into a ball of fire. I was lucky because the damage was not extensive. But it still cost about N400,000 to bring it back to life! The nation’s telecommunications sector is growing in leaps and bounds; it therefore demands the attention of the regulator to ensure that such growth is not impaired by fake equipment or allow such equipment to endanger the lives of users. The regulator is waging a war against what the people may ignorantly accept as good and normal, and, in the process, save their lives.

Even with all the good attributes of the Device Checker, which could include restoring efficiency to the mobile networks, hyperbolically, and causing subscribers to smile each time a connection is made – oh, thinking of nirvana – I was also very fascinated with what the Device Checker is not, according to the NCC. This is very important in a country where the trust deficit is nearly as important as the country’s legal tender and the politicians are skilled in making falsehood the figment of reality. “The Commission recognizes that consumers have legitimate expectations regarding the privacy and security of their personal information. The Type Approval Compliance framework is not designed for surveillance and does not provide the Commission with access to the content of communications, photographs, messages, contacts, financial information or any other personal information stored on users’ devices. The framework is limited to device identification information required to support regulatory compliance and facilitate the identification of devices that may not meet applicable Type Approval requirements. Consumer privacy remains fully protected in accordance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements,” NCC assured.

Such assurances are not misplaced. However, I want to observe that there seems to be a certain urgency in the way the regulator wants to get things done. For long, service quality and network integrity have remained major issues in the regulatory space. The case of the regulator, therefore, can be likened to that of a man fighting fire desperately. I implore relevant stakeholders to give the regulator the needed help in order to create an industry that may bring benefits to all.

World.title: Kashim Shettima’s response in kind to Atiku Abubakar, by Rotimi Fasan
World.content:
It’s exactly a week ago today that the All Progressives Congress inaugurated its expanded Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) at the presidential villa in Abuja. It was an occasion for some chest-thumping as well as an opportunity for the APC to set out its agenda for the 2027 campaigns. As is to be expected, the inauguration of the APC’s PCC presented Nigerians, including opposition politicians and their supporters, yet another opportunity to scrutinise the APC-led Bola Tinubu administration. That scrutiny has appropriately come with criticisms of the government’s performance or the person of the president. The APC leadership had itself set the ball rolling by responding in kind to recent attacks on the party beginning with the ADC’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar’s ill-advised decision, to address President Bola Tinubu by his first name at formal public events.

It was a gesture that many Nigerians advised the former vice president to desist from. Not only is it a breach of protocol, it is also culturally distasteful. But since it appeared to be getting him the needed attention, no matter how negative, from a section of the public, Atiku chose to double down on it and recruited his surrogates into the Tinubu-baiting game. The likes of Paul Ibe and Phrank Shaibu thought they were being dutiful by joining their principal to go the street-fighter route forgetting that they did not own the patent for retailing insults to political opponents. It was therefore not surprising to see Vice President Kashim Shettima use the occasion of the inauguration of his party’s PCC to launch a number of broadsides at both Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi of the NDC.

In his words, ‘We have the capacity to respond to all sorts of innuendoes and outright lies that our political opponents are taking on’. This is precisely what Nigerians who cautioned Alhaji Atiku Abubakar and his co-travellers feared would happen. They were starting a fire they would not be able to put out. One that would downgrade the quality of the campaign and deflect attention from the type of issues the candidates should be addressing. Shettima’s verbal shots are not new. Some of them are old arrows seasoned with new baits. Apparently referencing Atiku Abubakar’s displeasure to similar verbal shots in the past, he started by asking those who come to equity to do so with clean hands. He then went on to tell his audience that President Bola Tinubu remained the President and Commander-in-Chief of Nigeria no matter what Atiku chose to call him.

Whether Bola or Adekunle, it made no difference he said. Atiku’s repeated contestation for the presidency, he argued, only made him a Raila Odinga, a former Prime Minister in Kenya, who repeatedly contested but failed to be president and not an Abraham Lincoln who eventually succeeded after several failed attempts at contesting to be president in America. Speaking rather tongue in cheek, he said he would not ‘follow suit with Lawal and call him Kachalla’ by which he recalled Babachir Lawal’s reference to Atiku as Kachalla, which is a word for a leader of bandits in the north. In Shettima’s attack on Atiku, Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress suffered what one might call a collateral damage. Shettima called Obi ‘the master of bogus statistics and incoherent economic prescriptions’ from Bangladesh. Policies that worked in Bangladesh, he said quite correctly, would not automatically work in Nigeria with a demographic, economic and institutional structures that are vastly different.

I have called the damage Obi suffered from Shettima’s attack as collateral only because, unlike the attack on Atiku, it came unprovoked. At least not by anything Obi had said or done to the APC or its leadership in the immediate context of the point at issue. Obi is, however, as guilty as Atiku when it comes to such matters. The only difference is that as the master of performative morality and mob incitement, Peter Obi leaves the dirty work of rage baits and cussing to his Obidient followers. Some of them, like the shawl-wearing Edo-pretend, who contributes nothing aimed at intellectual or policy direction for her principal, cusses worse than an infidel. She is always invoking Ogun to ‘kpai’ her political opponents. What type of vote-canvassing is that?

Yet what rankles in all of this has been the response of supporters of Atiku Abubakar. Their latest criticism of Shettima’s attack of their principal is utterly hypocritical. It harks back to what Atiku himself had said in the past when Shettima took the verbal war to him. Atiku had said he would not respond to Shettima because he was older and more accomplished than him. Shettima’s utterances he said breached northern codes of respect for elders. Which again should tell Nigerians about the ADC’s presidential candidate’s style of politics which operates by appealing to religious and ethnic sentiments. He is a politician who wants Bola Tinubu’s job for himself and is bent on handing Shettima’s job to Rotimi Ameachi (in 2023 it was Ifeanyin Okowa), where does age much less regional or ethnic consideration come into the debate?

If Atiku ‘Tarkaed’ Shettima and Shettima ‘Dabohed’ him, should that offend God? You push me, I push you. Why should Alhaji Abubakar’s response be about northern solidarity? Why is he struggling to address the point raised by Shettima on its merit? Does it mean Tinubu is good target because he is from the south? Which Nigerian or foreign culture preaches outright the disrespect of elders? Nigerians should ask Atiku and his followers why they think it is appropriate for them to address the president by his first name at formal events but chafe at the ‘duba-gari’ tag that Shettima has foisted on him? Afterall, duba-gari is not a curse. It is the Hausa equivalent of ‘wole-wole’, the Yoruba word for a sanitary inspector.

As Phrank Shaibu asked Seun Okinbaloye if Bola is not the president’s name to justify their action of calling him by his first name, so can any Nigerian ask if Atiku did not train as a sanitary inspector? He did attend the Kano School of Hygiene! Should things like this be the talking point of the 2027 campaigns? Of course, no! But it’s the path Atiku chose to walk with his surrogates and it can’t be right for them and then be wrong for Shettima because he is of the APC. Taunts and puns are a critical part of political rhetoric. They could be a source of entertainment as well as education when rightly deployed. Thus, they have their place in politics and Nigeria has had past masters of the art like S.L.A. Akintola and K.O. Mbadiwe among others. At a time of grave economic and social disjunction, however, they should not constitute the main subject of national debate.

World.title: Superhighway: Ebonyi Community demands compliance with Umahi’s directive on borrow pits
World.content:
David Umahi, Minister of Works

By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

The people of Ndiebor Ishieke Autonomous Community in Ebonyi Local Government Area of Ebonyi State have called for strict compliance with the directive of the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, on borrow-pit operations along the ongoing Calabar–Ebonyi–Enugu-Benue–Nasarawa–Abuja Superhighway project.

The community urged the relevant authorities and the project contractor to ensure that further excavation activities complied with the minister’s directive, particularly regarding landowners’ consent, consultation with host communities and the protection of farmlands and economic crops.

The stakeholders, who commended Umahi for his intervention over concerns about alleged damage to agricultural lands in the area, said effective enforcement of the directive was necessary to safeguard rural livelihoods, prevent further encroachment and avert avoidable disputes between affected residents and the project authorities.

The community in a joint statement signed by the traditional ruler of Ndiebor Ishieke Autonomous Community, Eze Hyacinth Awoke Nwiboko; the President of the community.

They acknowledged the interventions and contributions of Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, and Senator Peter Nwebonyi, representing Ebonyi North Senatorial District, towards addressing the concerns associated with the project.

They, however, maintained that the minister’s directive must translate into concrete measures to protect affected landowners and ensure that construction activities were conducted in accordance with the relevant safeguards.

According to the statement, the community supports the superhighway project because of its potential to improve transportation, facilitate the movement of agricultural produce and other goods, and stimulate economic development across the benefiting states.

The stakeholders nevertheless cautioned that the pursuit of infrastructure development should not undermine the property rights, economic security and environmental safety of host communities.

“Our community supports the superhighway project and recognises its potential to boost transportation, trade and economic development.

However, we maintain that infrastructure development must respect the land rights, agricultural livelihoods and environmental safety of host communities,” the statement said.

The community expressed concern over reports of damage to farmlands and economic crops, noting that agriculture remained a major source of livelihood for many households in the area.

It identified yam, cassava, rice, millet and beniseed among the crops cultivated by residents, warning that the destruction of productive farmland could worsen the economic difficulties of affected farming families.

The stakeholders consequently called for a transparent assessment of the alleged losses and appropriate compensation for verified damage to crops, farmland and other legitimate property interests arising from the excavation activities.

They also urged the relevant authorities to establish effective communication channels involving traditional institutions, community representatives, landowners, project supervisors and the contractor before further borrow-pit operations were undertaken.

The community leaders said prior consultation and timely communication would help prevent misunderstandings, promote mutual trust and ensure that legitimate grievances were addressed before they escalated into disputes.

They further called for the reclamation of abandoned or exhausted borrow pits and the implementation of adequate environmental safeguards to protect residents, agricultural land and the surrounding ecosystem from hazards associated with excavation activities.

The signatories stressed that transparent procedures for assessing affected properties and determining compensation were essential to securing the cooperation of host communities and sustaining public confidence in the project.

On the broader development concerns, the community commended Governor Nwifuru for his administration’s development efforts in Ebonyi State and acknowledged Senator Nwebonyi’s representation of the district, including his reported legislative contributions towards attracting the superhighway project.

They appealed to both public officials to sustain their engagement with the relevant federal authorities to ensure that the concerns of affected residents received appropriate attention.

The statement added that the successful implementation of the project required a balance between the Federal Government’s infrastructure objectives and the legitimate interests of communities whose lands were affected by construction activities.

Reaffirming their commitment to peaceful engagement, the traditional ruler and other signatories pledged the community’s cooperation with the Federal Government, the Ebonyi State Government, the Ministry of Works and the contractor in finding a lasting resolution to the concerns.

“Our position is clear: we support the superhighway project, but development must not come at the expense of our land rights, livelihoods and environmental safety,” the statement added.

The stakeholders expressed hope that compliance with Umahi’s directive would lead to practical measures to protect affected landowners, address outstanding compensation claims and ensure that construction activities proceeded without unnecessary conflict with host communities.

World.title: Ebonyi arrest 30 suspected sex workers
World.content:
….seals unapproved guest house

By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

The Ebonyi State Ministry of Capital City and Urban Planning has arrested 30 suspected sex workers over alleged security concerns and the discovery of suspected hard drugs at the premises in a guest house in Abakaliki.

The team also sealed the Guest House in Abakaliki following an inspection of unapproved building used as guest House.

The Commissioner for Capital City and Urban Planning, Hon. Richard Ugo Idike, in collaboration with the Commissioner for Internal Security, Hon. Prince Etta Uka Ude, alongside security operatives and members of the ministry’s taskforce carried out the operation.

Addressing journalists during the inspection, Hon. Idike expressed concern over the alleged security threats associated with activities at the guest house. He noted that the presence of individuals reportedly from different states had raised concerns about security and public safety in the area.

The Commissioner disclosed that the team discovered substances suspected to be hard drugs, including wrappers allegedly containing substances locally referred to as Colos and Indian hemp, among others.

The suspected substances were reportedly recovered during the operation, while security operatives took charge of the matter.

Idike reiterated the state government’s commitment to ensuring that buildings within Abakaliki are used for lawful purposes and comply with approved development plans.

He called on property developers and building owners to obtain the necessary building approvals from the Ministry of Capital City and Urban Planning before commencing construction, stressing that the government would not tolerate the use of unapproved buildings for activities that could threaten public safety.

The Commissioner subsequently directed that Guest House be sealed indefinitely pending further clarification and compliance with the ministry’s requirements. He also directed the owner of the facility to visit the ministry to explain the circumstances surrounding the building and resolve the outstanding issues

The Commissioner for Internal Security, Hon. Prince Etta Uka Ude, in his remarks said the primary concern of his ministry was to ensure adequate security and protect residents of Ebonyi State.

He stated that the state government would not tolerate the use of any premises as a haven for criminal activities.

Ude added that the Ebonyi State Government, under the leadership of governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru, remained committed to maintaining peace, law and order across the state.

He urged security agencies to intensify surveillance and monitoring of establishments suspected of engaging in illegal activities, particularly within Abakaliki, to prevent criminal elements from exploiting business premises to undermine public safety.

The Commissioner stressed the importance of collaboration between government agencies, security operatives and members of the public in identifying and addressing security threats.

At the time of filing this report, the over 30 arrested individuals had reportedly been taken into police custody for further investigation, while the owner of the Guest House had yet to be arrested.

The sealing of the facility underscores the state government’s enforcement efforts concerning building regulations, public safety and security within the capital city.

World.title: 2027: Ebonyi Stakeholders’ Summit endorses Nwifuru for Second Term
World.content:
Gov Nwifuru

…Adopts zoning arrangement, calls for peaceful election

By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

The Ebonyi State Leaders and Stakeholders’ Political Summit has endorsed Governor Francis Nwifuru for a second term in office ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

The endorsement was made through a unanimous voice vote at the summit held on Tuesday at the Ecumenical Centre, Abakaliki, following a motion moved by the senator representing Ebonyi North, Onyekachi Nwebonyi.

The summit, which brought together political leaders and stakeholders from the three senatorial zones and 13 local government areas of the state, was held under the theme, “Orderly and Peaceful Political Transition in Ebonyi State: The Way Forward.”

Among those who attended were the first civilian governor of the state, Senator Sam Egwu; former Senate President Anyim Pius Anyim; former governor Martin Elechi; former governor and Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi; and Nwifuru, who attended as Special Guest of Honour.

The stakeholders deliberated on the future of the state, with particular emphasis on political stability, zoning, equity, continuity in governance and the need for a peaceful transition ahead of the 2027 general elections.

In a communiqué issued at the end of the summit, the participants reaffirmed their commitment to peace, unity and political stability, describing them as essential to the continued development of Ebonyi.

The communiqué, which was read by Mrs Chioma Nweze, was signed by Umahi, Anyim, Egwu and other leaders present on behalf of the summit.

They called on political leaders, public office holders, traditional rulers, religious leaders, civil society organisations and citizens to protect the state’s unity, irrespective of political affiliation and other differences.

The summit urged political parties, aspirants and their supporters to conduct their activities with restraint and mutual respect, while rejecting inflammatory rhetoric, intimidation, political violence and other actions capable of disrupting public order.

On the contentious issue of zoning, the summit expressed support for the continuation of the governorship rotation arrangement among the three senatorial zones, saying the practice had helped promote inclusion and political stability since the beginning of the Fourth Republic in 1999.

The communiqué noted that the state’s first three elected governors — Egwu from Ebonyi North, Elechi from Ebonyi Central and Umahi from Ebonyi South — each served two four-year terms.

It said the arrangement had encouraged continuity, mutual accommodation and respect for established political understandings among the zones.

The summit consequently resolved that Ebonyi North should complete the governorship slot in the 2027 electoral cycle, in line with the zoning principle recognised by the participants.

It further proposed that the governorship should move to Ebonyi Central in 2031 and remain there for eight years before moving to Ebonyi South in 2039 for another eight years.

The proposed rotation schedule provides for Ebonyi North from 2023 to 2031, Ebonyi Central from 2031 to 2039 and Ebonyi South from 2039 to 2047.

The stakeholders also called for the equitable distribution of public amenities and development projects among the zones, stressing the need to sustain fairness, justice and peaceful coexistence.

On governance, the summit commended Nwifuru’s administration for its development initiatives under the People’s Charter of Needs.

It identified infrastructure and rural development, education, healthcare, agriculture, food security, human capital development, women’s empowerment and youth development as important areas requiring sustained attention.

The summit urged political leaders and other stakeholders to continue promoting dialogue across party lines and discourage actions capable of creating unnecessary tension during the transition period.

It also called on political parties, aspirants, security agencies, electoral authorities and the media to work towards peaceful, credible and orderly elections in 2027.

The participants urged politicians to pursue their ambitions through lawful and democratic means, respect the rights of other citizens, avoid hate speech and misinformation, and recognise the role of relevant institutions in electoral matters.

The communiqué expressed appreciation to the leaders and representatives of the 13 local government areas, political parties and community organisations who participated in the deliberations.

It reaffirmed the summit’s aspiration for an Ebonyi State that remains peaceful, united, inclusive and development-oriented, while urging leaders and citizens to translate the resolutions into practical commitments that would advance the welfare of the people.

“Participants called on all political actors and their supporters to conduct political activities with restraint, mutual respect and a commitment to peaceful engagement. They further urged stakeholders to reject inflammatory rhetoric, intimidation, political violence and any conduct capable of undermining public order.

“The summit recognised that continuity, mutual accommodation and respect for established political understandings have contributed to the State’s stability. It therefore encouraged political leaders and stakeholders to sustain a culture of dialogue, fairness and responsible political engagement in addressing questions relating to succession and the future leadership of the State.

“The summit acknowledged the long-standing practice of senatorial rotation in the distribution of the governorship of Ebonyi State and the role this arrangement has played in promoting a sense of inclusion among the three senatorial zones. In the interest of equity, fairness, mutual trust and the preservation of peaceful coexistence, the summit expressed support for the continuation of the established zoning understanding in the consideration of the 2027 governorship succession.

“Accordingly, the summit resolved that Ebonyi North Senatorial Zone should be allowed to complete the governorship in the 2027 electoral cycle, in keeping with the rotation principle recognised by the participants and the objective of equitable political inclusion.

“The summit called on political parties, aspirants, supporters, security agencies, electoral authorities and the media to contribute to a peaceful, credible and orderly electoral process.

“Political parties and aspirants were urged to pursue their ambitions through lawful and democratic means, respect the rights of fellow citizens, avoid hate speech and misinformation, and accept the legitimate role of relevant institutions in the conduct and resolution of electoral matters” the communique stated.

World.title: Obasanjo ​‌⁠⁠​‍⁠⁠‍‌​​‍‍⁠‍⁠‌​Mourns Fasoranti, Uduaghan
World.content:
Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has expressed sadness over the deaths of Chief Reuben Fasoranti, former Afenifere leader, and Dr Emmanuel Uduaghan, former Delta governor.

Obasanjo described Fasoranti as one of the last surviving titans of a generation that laid the foundation for modern Nigeria through selfless service, sacrifice and unwavering integrity.

He said this in a statement on Tuesday in Abeokuta by his Special Assistant on Media, Kehinde Akinyemi.

According to Obasanjo, Fasoranti’s life exemplified purposeful leadership, integrity and an unwavering commitment to the progress of the Yoruba nation and Nigeria.

The former president described the late elder statesman’s death as the end of an extraordinary era, recalling his contributions to education and nation-building.

Obasanjo said Fasoranti had served as a school principal in several historic institutions, moulding minds, instilling discipline and building character before venturing into politics.

He also recalled Fasoranti’s tenure as Commissioner for Finance in the old Ondo State under the Unity Party of Nigeria (UPN) administration.

According to him, the late Afenifere leader’s record in office remains a reference point for fiscal discipline, transparency and accountability.

Obasanjo said Fasoranti provided unifying leadership when he assumed the leadership of Afenifere amid internal divisions and national uncertainty.

He added that the late elder statesman consistently opposed military dictatorship and advocated true federalism, justice and equity despite threats to his life.

“When the mantle of leading Afenifere fell upon him during a period of fragmentation and national uncertainty, Baba did not falter.

“He stepped up as a unifying anchor. He led with a calm and resolute authority that derived its strength not from loud proclamations, but from the immense moral weight of his convictions.

“On a personal note, I will always remember Baba’s warmth and his open-door policy. Even when we found ourselves on different sides of political debates, our mutual respect never waned,”he said.

On Uduaghan, Obasanjo described his death as a painful loss to Nigeria, saying the country had lost a gentleman, dedicated medical professional, and an accomplished statesman.

He recalled working with Uduaghan during his presidency when the latter served under former Delta governor, James Ibori, as Commissioner for Health and later Secretary to the State Government.

Obasanjo said Uduaghan distinguished himself as a brilliant administrator and a calm voice of reason during periods of political turbulence and heightened agitation in the Niger Delta.

He added that their interactions on healthcare policies and federal-state relations demonstrated Uduaghan’s administrative competence and commitment to Delta State’s peace and development.

Obasanjo said these qualities prepared Uduaghan for the responsibilities of leadership when he became governor of Delta State in 2007. (NAN)

World.title: Tinubu Mourns Fasoranti, Pays Glowing Tribute to Late Afeniifere Leader
World.content:
.Says Nigeria’ll sorely miss his voice of wisdom, moral authority, fatherly counsel

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has paid glowing tribute to the late Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, who died on Tuesday at the age of 100.

The President, in a tribute signed by him described the patriarch and elder statesman as an icon, beacon of principle and one of the last great titans of Chief Obafemi Awolowo’s progressive family.

According to him, Nigeria will sorely miss Pa Fasoranti’s voice of wisdom, moral authority and fatherly counsel.

Tinubu, in the 13-paragraph release stated, inter alia: “I received with profound sadness the news of the passing of Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, our father, patriarch, elder statesman, and foremost Afenifere leader, who died at the glorious age of 100.

“On behalf of the Federal Government and the people of Nigeria, I commiserate with the Fasoranti family, the good people of Akure Kingdom, the government and people of Ondo State and South-West Nigeria, and the entire Afenifere family.

“Pa Fasoranti was an icon, a beacon of principle, and one of the last great titans of Chief Obafemi Awolowo’s progressive family.

“His life, spanning a century, was a lesson in integrity, discipline, selflessness, and unwavering commitment to the Yoruba people and the unity and progress of Nigeria.

“From his days as an educationist and principal, to his stewardship as Commissioner for Finance in the old Western Region, and later as the leader of Afenifere, Baba never wavered in his belief in true federalism, social justice, and a Nigeria that works for all.

“Baba made immense contributions to this country and, at the risk of his life, fought for the democracy we enjoy today.

“Pa Fasoranti distinguished himself in every respect: in his disciplined, Spartan way of life, his belief in principles, and his commitment to noble causes.

“Our nation will sorely miss his voice of wisdom, moral authority, and fatherly counsel, especially now, when we need his guidance most.

“I recall Baba’s centenary on May 11 this year, when we celebrated not just longevity, but a legacy of honour. He lived a fulfilled life and left indelible footprints in the sands of time.

“I also recall his prayers and counsel when I came to his residence in Akure in 2022 to inform him of my decision to contest the presidency. Pa Fasoranti told me I would be President in his lifetime, and God answered his prayer.

“I had hoped Papa would also be around with us for my second term to witness the full dawn of economic growth and prosperity in the land.

“But we must thank God for Pa Fasoranti’s long life of service, grace and fulfilment.

“May his gentle soul rest in perfect peace. May God comfort all who mourn him and grant his family the fortitude to bear this great loss.”

World.title: Presidency: Draft Of National Policing Bill Now Ready
World.content:
.Submitted along with 29 consequential amendment bills for legislative drafting review

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

The Presidency on Tuesday disclosed that the draft of the 2026 National Policing Bill is ready.

Chief of Staff to the President and Chairman of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill, Hon Femi Gbajabiamila, stated in a release that the group has completed the drafting stage of its assignment and has formally submitted the draft National Policing Bill (2026), together with 29 consequential amendment bills, to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting review and validation.

According to him, the submission took place on Monday, to the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, in line with the Working Group’s work plan while the Ministry’s review will ensure that the bills conform to legislative drafting standards and conventions, and that they do not conflict with existing laws.

The Ministry of Justice, he further said, is expected to return the validated draft bills to the Working Group on or before Friday, 30th October 2026 and the Working Group will then give the validated bills final consideration before presenting them to Mr President, thereby concluding its mandate.

Gbajabiamila further said: The proposed National Policing Bill seeks to establish the constitutional and legislative framework for a dual policing structure, comprising a Federal Police Service and State Police Services.

“The Working Group remains committed to a rigorous and transparent process that will deliver a comprehensive legislative proposal for consideration by the President and subsequent transmission to the National Assembly.

“The work on preparing the National Policing Bill is proceeding alongside the ongoing consideration of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 by the States Houses of Assembly, which must be completed before the Bill is transmitted to the National Assembly.”

The Presidency had last Thursday hinted that the National Policing Bill will be transmitted to the National Assembly within two weeks.

Gbajabiamila had told newsmen after the steering committee meeting at the State House in Abuja that “The National Policing Bill is more or less ready for transmission to the National Assembly. We will probably have one more meeting after this to cross the t’s and dot the i’s and make sure every area is covered. So, we are 90% ready.

“The governors have one or two observations, and we should be ready in about a week or so.”

He described the bill as ‘the most consequential Bill of the administration so far’ adding that it has undergone strenuous exercises in the last few weeks since the working group’s steering committee began deliberations on August 3, 2026.

Also commenting on the possibility of the states dragging their feet on the passage of the Sixth Constitution Alteration Bill (State Police), especially against the backdrop of the information that only about six states had passed the amendment out of the 36 states and the FCT, Gbajabiamila affirmed that there was a “national consensus” among Nigerians on the need for the amendments.

“I see no reason why anyone will want to have a rethink on it,” he said.

Members of the committee present at the Thursday’s meeting held at the conference hall of the Chief of Staff Office at the State House, Abuja, were Chairman of the Governors’ Forum and Governor of Kwara State, AbdulRazak AbdulRahman; Governors Dapo Abiodun, Ogun State; Uba Sani, Kaduna State; Inspector General of Police, Tunji Disu, and the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice represented by the Solicitor General and Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Justice, Mrs Beatrice Jedy-Agba.

Others included Chairman, Policy Advisory Committee, Justice Abdullahi Liman (rtd); Head, Nigeria Police Reform Secretariat, Professor Olu Ogunsakin; Special Adviser to the President on National Assembly Matters (House of Representatives), Dr Lanre Smart; Senior Special Assistant to the President on Planning and Research who also doubles as the Secretary of the Committee, Nnadubem Moghalu; representative of the President of the Nigerian Bar Association; and AIG Abraham Nabhon Thomas, representing the National Security Adviser, among others.

President Bola Tinubu had on July 7, 2026,

inaugurated the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill to prepare the legal framework for the implementation of state police across the country.

The Working Group’s inauguration followed the National Assembly’s passage of the Constitution Alteration (State Police) Bill, 2026, in which the President proposes a dual policing structure comprising the Federal Police Service and 36 State Police Services.

Tinubu had pisited that while the constitutional amendment creates the framework for state police, the National Policing Bill would provide the legal structure for its implementation.

“The Constitution Amendment Bill establishes the framework for dual policing, but it does not operationalise it. That work is left to the National Policing Bill.”

According to him, the proposed legislation would address issues necessary for a smooth operationalisation of the State Police system.

“The proposed National Policing Bill will include provisions on minimum policing standards, state readiness certification, federal-state coordination, accountability, human rights safeguards and fiscal conditions.”

The President said that the committee will produce an implementation-ready draft bill immediately after the constitutional amendment process.

“The Working Group has been constituted to produce a technically robust, implementation-ready draft National Policing Bill for transmission to the National Assembly,” Tinubu said.

He said the committee was necessary to avoid delays after the State Police bill passed.

“We must not wait until the constitutional process is concluded before beginning this important assignment,” he said.

World.title: Breaking: Afenifere ​‌⁠⁠​‍⁠⁠‍‌​​‌‍‍​‌‌​Leader, Pa Fasoranti, Dies at 100, Aiyedatiwa Mourns
World.content:
Gov. Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State has expressed sadness over the death of the leader of the pan-Yoruba socio-poitical organisation, Afenifere, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, at the age of 100.

Aiyedatiwa, in a condolence message he personally signed on Tuesday in Akure, said the death of the centenarian was a great loss to Ondo State, Yorubaland and Nigeria.

The governor described Fasoranti as a patriarch and beacon of wisdom, integrity and selfless service, whose life was dedicated to the development of the society.

According to him, the late elder statesman demonstrated uncommon commitment to the progress and development of Ondo State, Yorubaland and Nigeria throughout his lifetime.

“With a heavy heart but with total submission to the will of God, I announce the passing of our revered elder statesman, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, who departed this world at the glorious age of 100.

“Pa Fasoranti was a patriarch, a beacon of wisdom, integrity and selfless service whose century-long life was marked by uncommon commitment to the development of our dear State, Yorubaland and Nigeria at large,” he said.

Aiyedatiwa said the deceased would be remembered for his fatherly guidance, wise counsel and principled positions on issues bordering on justice and good governance.

He noted that Fasoranti lived a fulfilled life and left behind enduring legacies worthy of emulation by the present and future generations.

“His counsel, fatherly guidance and principled stand on issues of justice and good governance will be sorely missed.

“He lived a fulfilled life and left indelible footprints of honour and legacy for generations to come,” the governor said.

Aiyedatiwa, on behalf of the government and people of Ondo State, commiserated with the Fasoranti family, the people of Akure Kingdom and the entire state over the loss.

He prayed for the peaceful repose of the deceased’s soul. (NAN)

World.title: Breaking: Nigeria Confirms Ebola Case in FCT, Identifies 44 Contacts, Activates Emergency Response
World.content:
The Federal Government has confirmed one imported case of Bundibugyo ebolavirus in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) and has activated public health response measures to prevent further spread.

The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Pate, disclosed this at a media conference in Abuja on Tuesday, following laboratory confirmation of the infection on Oct. 20.

Pate said the patient, a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda, was currently in isolation and receiving medical care.

He described the case as “a contained case,” while assuring Nigerians that the government was working with relevant authorities and partners to prevent further transmission.

Pate said the woman had been admitted to a private hospital in the FCT, where she received care for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed.

He said contact tracing had commenced, with 44 close contacts identified so far, while public health teams were identifying and monitoring people who might have been exposed, including healthcare workers, patients, caregivers and travel contacts.

“Surveillance has also been intensified, and the private hospital where the patient was treated is receiving immediate support to strengthen infection prevention and control measures,” he said.

The minister urged public and private healthcare facilities nationwide to remain on high alert, maintain a high index of suspicion, promptly identify and isolate suspected cases.

He also urged the public to observe strict infection prevention and control measures, and immediately report suspected cases to public health authorities.

He said Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of an infected person who is sick or has died from the disease, as well as contact with contaminated materials.

Pate advised Nigerians to practise regular hand hygiene, avoid contact with the body fluids of anyone suspected to have Ebola and watch for symptoms.

The symptoms, he said, included fever, severe weakness, headache, vomiting and diarrhoea, particularly following possible exposure.

He said people who might have been exposed should report immediately, even if they felt well, while anyone who developed symptoms should avoid close contact with others and call public health authorities for guidance before visiting a healthcare facility.

The minister also urged people contacted during the tracing exercise, including relevant airline passengers, to provide the required information and comply with public health advice.

He cautioned against rumours, misinformation and stigmatisation, advising Nigerians to rely on verified information from official health authorities.

Pate recalled that Nigeria had successfully contained Ebola in 2014 and had the experience and public health systems required to respond to the current case.

He, however, emphasised that containing the infection required cooperation from the public, early detection and prompt reporting of suspected cases.

“The Government of Nigeria through the Presidential Taskforce on EVD and NCDC will continue to provide updates.

“NCDC free call centre is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. For information or to report a suspected case, please call NCDC toll-free number 6232,” Pate added.(NAN)

World.title: Zitra Investments Vows to Close Financial Inclusion Gap, Expands Access to Credit
World.content:
Marking its sixth anniversary, the management of Zitra has expressed its determination to close the financial inclusion gap and expand access to credit for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria.

The Chief Executive Officer of Zitra, Mr Babatunde Obadero, said at a press conference recently held in Lagos that SMEs remain the heartbeat of commerce in the country, and that the company is poised to help them access credit.

He said: “I dare say over 300,000 loans worth N30 billion have been disbursed in the last six years, with 200,000 customers on our digital platforms. The journey has just started, and there is still a lot of ground to cover.

“In six years, we have secured our banking licence, a Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) asset management licence, and built a payment company called ZitraPay. All of these entities give us a platform to provide the services our customers need.

“We have built an ecosystem that delivers financial services just the way our customers need them. We are proud to say our growth has only just begun. We have a combined balance sheet of over N50 billion, which is the beginning of our journey to greater things ahead.”

Looking ahead, he said the company’s goal is to lead retail digital financial services in Nigeria, adding that it aims to expand its footprint geographically and improve access to its digital channels.

Co-founder of Zitra, Mr Femi Okuyelu, recalled that the company started with five staff and now has over 120 staff across different locations in the country.

“In terms of growth, we have seen the business evolve, and we have been able to solve some problems in the nation’s economy.

“Today in Nigeria, financial inclusion is about 79 per cent, which leaves 21 million adults financially excluded. That may look small, but it is more than the combined populations of Finland, Denmark and Estonia. And we have contributed our quota to that financial inclusion story,” he said.

On why credit penetration is still low, Okuyelu said: “Only 10 per cent of the adult population has access to credit. Most people borrow from family and friends, cooperatives and churches. Why can’t they access formal credit? Number one, they don’t have collateral. Number two, they operate in the informal sector, which is not organised. And number three, they have no credit history or records.”

He said Zitra’s response has been to create a social business model that onboards informal customers, helps them organise their businesses, monitors their cash flow and lends against it.

“What we have created will make it easier for them to access credit. We monitor their cash flow and lend against it, because in this environment, lending against collateral is difficult,” he said.

On his part, Director, Chief Olaotan Olamuyiwa, recalled that the idea for Zitra was conceived during COVID-19, when the founders decided to start their own firm after working in different organisations.

He said the journey has been built on relationships and one major investor who believed in the vision.

Speaking on how small businesses struggle with funding, he noted that many SMEs have their own money trapped with clients.

“You see people who want N5 million to stock up, but they have sold products to other businesses, and those businesses owe them in excess of N20 million. They cannot afford N5 million to finance a transaction because their cash is tied up,” he said.

He said products like invoice discounting address that gap, adding: “If you have N20 million in invoices due in 60 to 90 days, you can come to us and say, fund this N5 million project, and I will pay when my debtor pays.”

World.title: TETFund Urges Academics to Turn Research into Practical Innovations
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) has urged Nigerian academics and researchers to move beyond publishing scholarly papers to developing practical innovations that address societal challenges and create economic opportunities.

The Executive Secretary, Sonny Echono, made the call in Abuja at the closing ceremony of the 35th cohort of the Research for Impact Initiative (R4i).

Echono said the initiative, implemented in partnership with Innov8 Hub, is part of the fund’s strategy to institutionalise research and development in public tertiary institutions and strengthen the relationship between academic research, industry and government.

“We must empower our scholars to create local solutions for our societal problems. This is why a commitment to education is a commitment to our nation’s future, ensuring that our people are not just consumers of foreign technology, but innovators who can drive sustainable growth,” he said.

He stressed that Nigeria needed to strengthen its capacity to develop home-grown technologies rather than depend on innovations from other countries.

He noted that technological advancement had become a major driver of economic transformation, adding that countries seeking sustainable development must invest in quality education, research and innovation.

“At TETFund, we are refocusing and reinvigorating our intervention activities to drive the institutionalisation of Research and Development in public tertiary institutions, enhance research capacity, and support research-industry linkage, among others,” he said.

He said R4i is designed to reposition public tertiary institutions as drivers of a knowledge-based economy through innovative practices and solution-driven research.

Echono commended Innov8 Hub for providing technical expertise and mentorship to participating academics, and urged the graduates to apply the knowledge acquired to develop solutions for their institutions and communities.

He disclosed that some innovations from previous editions of the programme were showcased at the maiden TETFund National Research Fair and Exhibition in November 2024.

The second edition will hold from November 23 to 27, 2026 at the Abuja Trade and Convention Centre, Airport Road, giving researchers the opportunity to showcase their innovations, connect with industry players and explore partnerships for commercialising research outputs.

The Deputy General Manager of Innov8 Hub, Dr. Deji Ige, said the initiative was designed to establish a culture in which research and development drive innovation, enterprise creation and national development.

“Innovation thrives in a culture where research and development are the primary languages of interaction. If we can learn, understand and revive this culture, the outcomes will include inventions, solutions, technological advancement, enterprise development, job creation, wealth generation, meaningful impact and societal development,” he said.

Ige described the programme as a shift towards stronger collaboration among government, academia, industry and society, adding that research without practical impact could limit the ability of tertiary institutions to contribute to technological advancement.

“Impact-driven research and development is what keeps it afloat and enables it to navigate safely. Without impact flowing from research and development, academia becomes an immobile vessel, bereft of progress, possibilities and the power to navigate,” he said.

World.title: ADC Unveils Kele As Running Mate, Intensifies Push for Plateau Govt House
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Plateau State has unveiled Hon. Chungdung Bitrus Pwajok Kele as the running mate to its governorship candidate, Brig.-Gen. John Sunday Sura (rtd), ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

The event, which took place in Jos, attracted party officials, stakeholders, supporters and political associates from across the state.

Speaking at the unveiling, Sura described Kele as an experienced politician and grassroots mobiliser whose emergence would strengthen the party’s efforts as it prepares for the forthcoming election.

He said the ADC ticket was aimed at providing what he described as an alternative platform for governance in Plateau State, adding that the party would focus on issues of security, rural development and inclusive leadership.

According to him, the unveiling marked the beginning of a series of political activities designed to expand the party’s presence across the state’s 17 local government areas.

He disclosed that the ADC would subsequently launch its governorship campaign and embark on consultations and mobilisation efforts in various constituencies across the state.

“We want Plateau people to know that ADC is on the ground. This is the beginning of our activities ahead of the campaign proper,” he said.

Sura also expressed confidence in the party’s chances in the election, stating that voters would assess the performance of the incumbent administration alongside the programmes being presented by opposition parties.

He said his campaign would focus on issues affecting citizens, including infrastructure, transportation, economic development and public welfare.

Responding to questions on the incumbency factor, the ADC governorship candidate maintained that the party remained focused on its objectives and would continue to engage voters.

On his running mate, Sura described Kele as a politician with extensive grassroots experience, noting that she had previously served as councillor representing Gyel ‘A’ Ward in Jos South Local Government Area and had contested for several elective offices.

He added that her political network and experience in mobilising women and young people would be of great advantage in the state governance.

ADC officials at the event expressed optimism that the Sura-Kele ticket would enhance the party’s reach across different demographic groups as political activities gradually gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general election.

World.title: ‘What did she do’? Fans speculate why Tracy Hlophe MUST apologise
Kearsney College mourns former top student’s tragic death
World.content:
Kearsney College is mourning the death of one of their star past pupils. Images via FB

Kearsney College is mourning the death of one of their Old Boys, Ndabenhle Shazi, who died in a car accident last week.

The star actor and performer passed just two days before his 33rd birthday.

The KwaZulu-Natal all-boys private school is South Africa’s Top 5 expensive schools.



KEARSNEY COLLEGE MOURNS ACTOR AND ARTIST ALUMNUS

On their social media platforms, Kearsney College shared the tragic news of the passing of their former top student, Ndabenhle Shazi.

They shared: “With deep sadness, we announce the tragic death of a shining Kearsney star and one of our dear brothers. Shazi, also known to family and older friends as Boyo, died in a car accident on the afternoon of Monday, 14 October 2026, near Ermelo. He was laid to rest at the family’s homestead on Saturday.

Affectionately known as “Shazi”, the 2012 matriculant was a distinguished drama student and musical artist who was involved in the school choir and theatre productions that were performed around the world.

This included an international tour to Asia in 2010 and to the World Choir Olympics in Cincinnati, USA, 2012, where the Kearsney College choir won 3 gold medals.

“Shazi made us laugh, cheer, sing and smile over many years. His laugh and personality brought joy to so many. With a heart of gold, he loved his Kearsney brothers and, being based in KZN, often popped in to visit staff members he respected and cared for.

“Shazi, you will always be a Kearsney legend and loved by many around the world. Rest in Peace, ” added the post.



CELEBRATED MUSIC AND DRAMA STUDENT

During his tenure at Kearsney College, Shazi served as chairman of the dance and drama club, head of choreography, and soloist in the school choir. He was also co-head of the Pembroke Inter-House Plays.

During his matric year, he received his colours and honours in music and dramatic arts.

After matriculating, he pursued his love of the performing arts through his entertainment company, SM ENT, where he continued to produce music and DJ under his artist name, Shazi Mayne.

He also graduated with a BCom in Supply Chain Management from the University of Pretoria.

World.title: Wednesday’s coastal tides: What beachgoers and anglers should know
World.content:
Beachgoers, surfers and anglers can check Wednesday’s high and low tide times before planning activities along South Africa’s coastline. Image: Unsplash

If you’re heading to the coast on Tuesday, check the tide times before planning your activities.

Water levels change throughout the day, while wind, waves, swell and the shape of the seabed also affect conditions along the shore and at sea.

When to expect the next spring tide

Spring tides are important to watch out for because they bring higher high tides and lower low tides than usual.



The next spring tide is expected around the full moon on Monday, 26 October 2026.

These changes can affect swimming, surfing and fishing. High tides may cover rocks and reefs, while low tides expose more of the shoreline.

Check the tide times and the latest weather and marine warnings before you head to the coast.

World.title: Tso uses Max Verstappen analogy to explain Kaizer Chiefs’ struggles
World.content:
Former Orlando Pirates midfielder Benedict Vilakazi believes Fernando Da Cruz’s time as Kaizer Chiefs coach could be short-lived, arguing that the club’s struggles go beyond the technical team.

Vilakazi, popularly known as Tso, believes Amakhosi lack the quality of players needed to compete for major trophies and fears the club could once again turn to a foreign coach if Da Cruz is dismissed.

Speaking to iDiski Times, the former midfielder predicted that Chiefs would look overseas for another coach rather than appoint a local tactician.



“He will leave and again, they will still go overseas to get a new coach,” he said.

Vilakazi also questioned why Chiefs did not consider local coaches such as Rulani Mokwena and Pitso Mosimane when they were available, pointing to their achievements at Mamelodi Sundowns.

“I don’t think Kaizer Chiefs will consider a local coach. When Rulani Mokwena and Pitso Mosimane were unattached, that was a perfect opportunity for them to say, ‘If we want to bring back glory days, here are people who showed at Sundowns that they are winners’. It didn’t happen,” he said.



However, Vilakazi believes changing coaches alone will not solve Amakhosi’s problems, insisting that the club must improve the quality of players at its disposal.

He argued that even an elite coach would struggle to deliver results without the right squad, using a car analogy to illustrate his point.

“Even if they bring in the best coach like Jose Mourinho, you still driving the same car. You can’t beat a Maserati driving a Toyota Tazz. You can put Max Verstappen in a Tazz and I’ll drive a Mercedes and I’ll be faster than him; that’s how it is,” he said.



Kaizer Chiefs told to get quality players

Vilakazi added that the quality of the squad ultimately determines what a coach can achieve, regardless of their reputation or experience.

“So whoever you put in the team, with the same material, he won’t get results for Kaizer Chiefs,” he concluded.

World.title: Friend testifies about final moments before AKA and Tibz were shot dead
World.content:
Rapper Kierna ‘AKA’ Forbes’ friend and celebrity chef Tebello ‘Tibz’ Motsoane repeatedly said he could not breathe after gunshots were fired outside Wish restaurant on Florida Road in Durban, the Durban High Court heard on Tuesday.

Motsoane and AKA were gunned down on February 10, 2023.

Lindokuhle Mkhwanazi, Lindani Ndimande, Siyanda Myeza, Mziwethemba Gwabeni, Lindokuhle Ndimande, Malusi Ndimande and Siyabonga Ndimande face charges 11 charges including conspiracy to commit murder, murder, unlawful possession of a firearm, unlawful possession of ammunition, five counts of attempted murder, and money laundering.





WITNESS RECOUNTS DAY AKA WAS MURDERED

State witness Lusaso Ngcobo, a Durban musician and event organiser, testified on Tuesday and requested that his face not be shown.

Ngcobo told the court that he had known AKA for more than a decade through the music industry and that they were close friends. He also knew Motsoane through the industry.

He testified that on 10 February 2023, he went to the Bryd and Groom hair salon on Florida Road at around 18:30, as he usually did on Fridays. About 15 minutes later, AKA arrived with his entourage. The rapper, who was visiting the establishment for the first time, also had his hair cut.



Ngcobo said they spent time catching up before heading to Wish restaurant for dinner, where they discussed AKA’s plans, including the release of his new album Mass Country which was released posthumously on 24 February 2023.

Motsoane later joined them during the approximately two hours they spent at the restaurant.

Ngcobo testified that the group eventually left Wish through a passage leading outside. He was among those at the front, while AKA and Motsoane were behind him.



Once they reached the pavement, the group said their goodbyes. Ngcobo said he turned towards the passage to return inside after saying goodbye.

He testified that AKA was standing to his right and speaking to Motsoane, and AKA was about an arm’s length away just before the shooting. They planned to meet again later after the performance at Yugo nightclub in Durban.

Ngcobo recalled hearing a loud bang that initially sounded like fireworks.



“Right at that moment I heard a loud bang like fireworks. My first reaction was to duck because I wasn’t sure what was happening. I then saw everyone running and I realised it was unsafe and that maybe the sound couldn’t have been fireworks but a firearm instead,” he testified.

Ngcobo said he ran back towards the restaurant corridor with others. During the commotion, he saw Motsoane trip and fall.

He testified that he went to check on Motsoane before noticing AKA lying on the ground.



“I went to check on Tibz if he was okay and I recall seeing Kiernan lying on the floor I was walking out. I proceeded to check if he was okay because I could see some blood and I wasn’t sure if it was on him or on the floor. I asked him if he was okay, he said I can’t breathe. He kept saying I can’t breathe,” Ngcobo told the court.

“I proceeded to ask him if he was hurt and I could not make sense of the words he was saying. We tried to see where the blood was coming from as we were searching his body we realised he had a wound by his chest underneath his arm,” he added.

They called for assistance and attempted to stop the bleeding using towels while waiting for help to arrive.
