World.title: Tallinn Old Town doubles as England for highly anticipated Indian film
World.content:
Tallinn Old Town recently transformed into early 20th-century England for the historical Indian film "The India House," bringing major Indian stars to the Estonian capital.

Directed by Ram Vamsi Krishna, the film follows Indian students in London who fought British colonial rule in the pre-independence era in the early 1900s.

The film takes its name from the North London student residence that became a key hub for Indian nationalist political activism between 1905 and 1910.

During filming around Tallinn's Old Town this fall, the picturesque Müürivahe tänav, for example, became Oxford Street, complete with British flags, while a major protest scene involving 150 actors was filmed by Cinema Sõprus.

Nafta Films founder and producer Esko Rips said that it was unusual for such a large crew to travel abroad for a shoot, with 47 Indian crew members in Estonia alongside Nafta Films' local team of around 70.

He said working across cultural and professional differences meant both teams had to adapt their communication and working styles. "We try to find common ground," Rips added.

'Tallinn feels like home'

Tollywood star Nikhil Siddhartha has more than 25 films to his name, including the 2022 Telugu blockbuster "Karthikeya 2," one of India's highest-grossing films.

Shooting for "The India House" marked Siddhartha's first-ever visit to Estonia, but he admitted it didn't feel that way.

"It just feels so welcoming," he said. "I don't feel like I've come to a different country; it feels like home."

Siddhartha also praised Tallinn's well-preserved Old Town and Estonia's collective efforts in supporting culture.

"Estonia is rich in culture," he said, "and I'm very happy to come visit it and shoot here."

Filming for Indian film "The India House" in front of Tallinn's Cinema Sõprus. October 2026. Source: press photo

Estonian slackliner Jaan Roose also joined the production as a stunt performer, handling falls, jumps and other action sequences. He said protective padding hidden beneath his costume helped cushion the impacts.

"I have to run on cobblestones, jump, fall and take a hit from a barrel," he said. "I'm doing anything that requires knowing how to fall."

The Indian production team considered filming in several European countries before choosing Estonia, Siddhartha said, thanking Rips personally for helping make the arrangements.

"The way they welcomed us, the way they described filming locations — we were blown away," the film star emphasized, adding that the film will also be shown in several Estonian movie theaters once released.

Film Estonia incentive's future uncertain

Rips said Estonia's 40 percent film production incentive helped secure the foreign film project. The "India House" team had visited other countries, including the U.K. itself, but filming there would have been more expensive.

After driving about 7,500 kilometers, scouting locations across Estonia a year ago, the filmmakers fell for Tallinn, choosing it over alternatives including Bulgaria and Lithuania.

The Estonian producer warned, however, that the Film Estonia incentive is poised to lose funding under the next government, set to be elected next March. Securing one production is only part of the challenge.

"I don't understand why our industry is being jerked around like this," Rips said. "Attracting a project here and working on it is one thing; attracting new projects is another, and we need them to keep the industry going."

World.title: Keidi Jaakson: How we talk about immigration matters
World.content:
In mid-October, Rainis Sinikas, head of the border and migration supervision department at the Police and Border Guard Board's (PPA) North Prefecture, told ERR that the situation with irregular migrants in Estonia is "difficult and could turn into a crisis situation," that administrative courts and local governments are overloaded and that the entire cooperation network is under great strain. A few days earlier, PPA chief Egert Belitšev warned that migration pressure could rise sharply as people try to leave Belarus ahead of winter, describing organized routes that cost each person up to €10,000. Interior Minister Igor Taro has called the situation "part of Russia's overall aggression tactics" and declared that Estonia must send a clear message that it cannot be used as a transit corridor. So far this year, the PPA has detained 542 people from 48 countries, both within Estonia and at its borders, and returned 120 of them to Latvia.

There are real operational and security challenges behind these numbers. According to Egert Belitšev, Russia and Belarus facilitate routes organized by criminal networks, with people paying thousands of euros to reach the EU. Processing people who arrive without documents, establishing their identities and routes and pursuing those responsible for facilitating irregular crossings is demanding work. ERR has reported that tighter border controls in Poland and Lithuania have redirected part of these flows towards Estonia. The pressure on local services is also documented: Rae Municipality, where the main detention center is located, is considering legal action against the state and the Social Insurance Board has acknowledged that it was unprepared for the increase. But public concern about immigration is not simply a reflection of how many people arrive across the border. It is also shaped by how much attention, and what kind of attention, the issue itself receives.

James Dennison and Andrew Geddes of the European University Institute's Migration Policy Center recently published "What Europeans Think About Immigration and Why It Matters," drawing on 25 years of survey data across Europe. Their research suggests that public attitudes towards immigration are more stable and more nuanced than commonly assumed and that, where they change, they tend to actually become more favorable over time. What changes more readily is what the researchers call salience: how much attention immigration receives as a political issue. This can be shaped by institutional communication, political rhetoric and media coverage. Speaking at the book's launch at the Center for European Policy Studies in Brussels, Dennison argued that people who consider immigration an important political issue are disproportionately likely to hold restrictive views. Raising the issue's profile can therefore benefit one part of the political spectrum. He also warned that political parties often confuse the growing prominence of immigration with a shift in what people actually believe about it, responding to heightened attention as though it necessarily reflected more restrictive public attitudes.

The language used to describe the current situation to the Estonian public should be proportionate to its scale. Repeated references to crisis and hybrid attacks can make the situation appear more acute and exceptional than the numbers alone suggest. Estonia has detained 542 people so far this year, while Latvia, which directly borders Belarus, recorded over 8,400 irregular crossing attempts by July 21. Across the EU, Frontex recorded approximately 74,000 irregular border-crossing detections in the first eight months of the year, down 35 percent compared with 2025. These figures measure different things and cannot be compared directly, but they provide context for assessing the language used. In an ERR report published on October 19, Taro himself said that Estonia had not yet exhausted its capacity to handle migrants and that the situation could only be described as a crisis once existing resources were no longer sufficient, with several hundred detention places across the country still vacant. By the interior minister's own measure, then, the situation has not reached the point of crisis, which makes the persistent language of potential crisis harder to account for.

Dennison and Geddes's research raises questions about how the current framing of immigration in Estonia may shape public perceptions. Detentions are routinely reported as separate events, often with considerable operational detail. PPA statements repeatedly warn that institutions are overloaded and that the situation could turn into a crisis. The interior minister has urged people to report suspicious individuals. Such communication may increase the prominence of immigration in public debate and encourage people to view it primarily through the lens of security, even if it does not change their underlying attitudes.

In the Spring 2024 Eurobarometer, 29 percent of Estonian respondents agreed that immigrants contribute positively to the country, tied with Cyprus for one of the lowest figure in the EU. The 2018 European Social Survey found that just over half of Estonians thought the state should allow few or no people of a different race or ethnic group to move to Estonia, though the same data shows that attitudes have been slowly becoming more favorable over time. Against this backdrop, repeatedly framing immigration as a potential crisis risks reinforcing the perception that it is primarily a threat.

The deliberate instrumentalization of migration by Russia and Belarus is a genuine security concern, yet recognizing that threat does not require treating everyone travelling along these routes as a threat in themselves. The largest groups among those detained this year come from Somalia, Sudan, Ethiopia, Eritrea and Bangladesh, several of which are affected by armed conflict or severe human rights abuses. EU law provides no visa for the purpose of seeking asylum, so in most cases protection can only be claimed once a person is already on European territory. Arrivals along these routes are unlikely to stop and Estonia needs the capacity to process them effectively.

And Estonia has demonstrated that it can mobilize considerable institutional capacity when the political and public context supports it. In 2022, more than 43,000 Ukrainian refugees arrived, amounting to over 3 percent of the population. The legal framework was different, the circumstances were different and the public solidarity was grounded in a shared sense of threat from Russia. But the experience shows what Estonia can organize when political priorities and public solidarity align. The question is whether the capacity can be rebuilt for people whose reasons for seeking protection may be less immediately legible to the Estonian public.

The debate also raises questions about who attracts suspicion and on what grounds. An operation in Nõmme on October 11 began when residents reported two dark-skinned men who appeared unfamiliar with the area. In August, ERR reported that police had already received unfounded reports about people based solely on their skin colour and PPA representative Indrek Aru acknowledged that in one case the person who had been reported "had all the necessary documents, was completely law-abiding and even spoke Estonian." In its account of the October incident, however, the PPA said that reports were generally prompted by behavior rather than race, while acknowledging that people from a different ethnic background stand out more in a suburb like Nõmme where residents tend to recognize one another. Sinikas also pointed to muddy clothing as one reason groups of migrants might attract attention in autumn.

The gender equality and equal treatment commissioner's 2024 report on racial discrimination documented experiences of racism among people of color in Estonia, including verbal abuse and physical threats, much of it unreported. The difficulty lies in how authorities distinguish legitimate reports based on specific behavior from suspicion based primarily on someone's appearance, particularly when the police themselves acknowledge that skin color can influence who attracts attention. That distinction deserves more public discussion than it currently receives.

World.title: Estonia could learn from Israel's crisis preparedness
World.content:
Estonia can learn from Israel's decades of experience with war, particularly when it comes to building shelters, warning the public about attacks and preparing people for crises, Israeli civil defense expert Yoram Laredo says.

Israelis have been hardened by various wars.

"Unfortunately, since the establishment of the state in 1948, there has been a war every 10 years. So, sadly, we have experienced different types of warfare," said Israeli civil defense expert Yoram Laredo on ERR's "Välisilm" foreign affairs program.

When it comes to shelters, for example, Israel is often held up as a model. However, the system in which everyone knows where to go has taken decades to develop. The turning point came with the 1991 Gulf War.

"That was a lesson we learned from the Gulf War. At the time, Iraq fired ballistic missiles at Israel for the first time. Following that tragic event, we introduced a rule requiring every newly constructed building and apartment to have a shelter. Today, 70 percent of Israeli citizens have a shelter in their homes. It takes time," Laredo said.

But what could be done more quickly, including in Estonia?

"My recommendation is to bring in engineers and inspect every underground parking garage. If they can be shown to withstand ballistic missile strikes, they can be designated as shelters for large numbers of people. These are things that can be done using existing resources," Laredo said.

The most important thing is to be prepared for a crisis.

"You need to prepare your citizens for what is coming and keep them informed. The information available must be shared because that is the first step toward resilience. People break down psychologically when something happens that they did not expect. If the government communicates with people and warns them that there will be power outages, communications disruptions and supply chain problems, and explains how these will be handled, citizens will be able to cope," Laredo said.

Estonia can also learn from Israel's approach to warning people about attacks.

"Israel has a highly sophisticated system that detects all objects flying toward the country, whether from nearby or far away, regardless of their shape or type. The most important element is the siren system. There are thousands of sirens on rooftops. In addition, mobile apps, the internet, radio and television all work in sync. Someone might be watching television, using their phone or standing outside — the system warns them that a missile is on its way. The best thing to do then is take shelter. After the first casualties, everyone knows what to do and people become very disciplined. Unfortunately, that is how it works," Laredo said.

However, when several generations have grown up without experiencing war, it is difficult to make people understand what they need to be prepared for.

"It is comparable to how we anticipate an earthquake in Israel. Our region experiences a devastating earthquake every 100 years. There has been no such earthquake in the history of modern Israel. The last one occurred 100 years ago, before the State of Israel was established. How do you convince the population that an earthquake could strike at any moment?" the expert said.

Israel learned a harsh lesson three years ago when one of the world's best intelligence services allowed the October 7 tragedy to happen because of overconfidence.

"You have to constantly reassess your strategic assumptions and paradigms. If you fail to do that and rely solely on technological superiority without questioning your interpretation of intelligence, things like this happen. That is Israel's most important lesson: Strategic assumptions and interpretations of intelligence must be constantly reassessed rather than rigidly adhered to," Laredo said.

Following October 7, the small state of Israel also had to evacuate large numbers of people.

"The State of Israel evacuated 125,000 people, including 60,000 from the north. Communities along the northern border were evacuated because, at the time, we did not know whether Hezbollah would open a second front there. Communities around Gaza were also evacuated. Those 125,000 people lived in hotels for almost two years. And that really costs a lot of money," Laredo said.

It is also essential to maintain a constant state of crisis preparedness.

"Preparing for a crisis is like a muscle that needs to be exercised constantly. If you do not exercise that muscle, you become exhausted and when a crisis strikes, you eventually break down psychologically. That is what we have learned. Unfortunately, we constantly face real incidents and wars, so we are practicing all the time," Laredo said.

World.title: DNO’s oil sales in northern Iraq double in Q3 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Norway-based oil and gas operator DNO reported that its crude oil sales in Iraqi Kurdistan nearly doubled on an annual basis, reaching an average of 28,058 barrels per day in the third quarter of 2026.

The increase in oil sales comes after the corporation proactively halted its regional activities in response to the military escalations between the United States, Israel, and Iran in late February 2026, which resulted in a total collapse in revenues in the second quarter of 2026.

During the third quarter of 2026, gross operating production from the Tawke and Peshkabir oilfields rose significantly to 73,219 barrels per day, a substantial increase from just 363 barrels per day in the second quarter of the year.

All payments for DNO’s share of the oil during the third quarter were made in advance and deposited into the company’s foreign bank accounts before delivery began, aiming to mitigate previous regional payment risks.

Compared to oil sales of 14,449 barrels per day during the third quarter of 2025, the company’s supplies in the third quarter of 2026 represent an increase of about 94 percent.

World.title: Iraq offers mediation between Iran, Gulf States
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein stated on Sunday that Baghdad is attempting to arrange a meeting between Iran and the Gulf States as part of diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions and advance regional stability.

Hussein’s remarks took place during his speech at the conclusion of the 52nd session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), where he confirmed that Iraq was maintaining contacts with both sides to facilitate dialogue, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

There are ongoing discussions between Iraq, the Gulf countries, and Iran aimed at bringing their viewpoints closer together, according to Hussein.

“We are trying to organize a meeting in Baghdad between Iran and the Gulf States,” Hussein said, without specifying a date or the degree of representation expected.

The proposal comes amid regional tensions that severely impacted maritime shipping and security in the Arabian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz.

The goal of the diplomatic framework is to bring together Iran and the six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) members—Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Oman—to address common security issues.

Hussein stressed that the region cannot purchase security from elsewhere and that internal collaboration is the only way to establish stability.

Although Hussein and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met in Baghdad on the sidelines of the summit to reaffirm a commitment to communication, the date of the joint meeting has not yet been disclosed.

World.title: Iraq holds funeral for 47 security personnel executed by ISIS years ago
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi authorities held a mass funeral on Tuesday in the northern city of Mosul for 47 victims, including security personnel and civilians, who were executed by the terrorist group of ISIS ten years ago.

Teams from Iraq’s Martyrs Foundation recently unearthed the remains from a mass burial south of Mosul. The Department of Forensic Medicine used DNA testing to positively identify the victims.

During ISIS’s brutal rule between 2014 and 2017, people from places south of Mosul, such as Hammam al-Alil, al-Shura, and al-Qayyarah, were kidnaped and executed. The victims included soldiers, police officers, religious figures, and local civilians.

Under the direction of Nineveh Governor Abdul Qader al-Dakhil, security personnel carried coffins covered in the Iraqi flag during an official ceremony. A public funeral procession headed toward the Qayyarah district for final burial after the central ceremony in Mosul.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports to China hit 1.18 million bpd in September
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil supplies to China during September totaled 4.84 million tons, or about 1.18 million barrels per day, a 19 percent decline compared to the previous year and a 248 percent increase compared to August.

The General Administration of Customs of the People’s Republic of China revealed that the country’s imports of crude oil from Russia, its largest supplier, reached 9.94 million tons (approximately 2.42 million barrels per day) in September, according to Reuters.

China oil imports from Russia in September are 20 percent more than the volumes it received during the same period in 2025, though it marks an 11 percent decline compared to the previous month.

During the first nine months of 2026, Brazil was the second-largest crude oil supplier to China, with imports reaching 44.29 million tons (approximately 324.65 million barrels) from Brazil, compared to 43.12 million tons (around 316.07 million barrels) from Saudi Arabia.

Brazil’s oil supplies to China increased by 18 percent on an annual basis to 5.15 million tons in September alone, or almost 1.25 million barrels per day.

China’s crude oil imports from Saudi Arabia stood at 2.70 million tons, or about 660,000 barrels per day, marking a 62 percent decline compared to the previous year.

Chinese independent refiners increased recently their imports of Iraqi and Qatari crude to compensate for a sharp decline in Iranian oil supplies.

As their stockpiles near depletion, private refineries in China are paying considerable premiums to acquire alternatives, according to Reuters.

Experts see that the step represents a desperate search for alternatives due to logistical obstacles, rather than a true rebound in Chinese domestic crude demand.

World.title: Two oilfield operators in northern Iraq merge in $600 million deal
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Gulf Keystone Petroleum and ShaMaran Petroleum have reached a merger agreement, becoming one of the top private oil producers in Iraqi Kurdistan.

According to a statement from the corporation, the all-share acquisition is worth $601 million, Reuters reported.

As of October 19, shareholders of ShaMaran, who are listed on Euronext, will receive 0.075 shares of Gulf Keystone for each share of ShaMaran they own, reflecting a premium of 23 percent.

Each company’s stockholders will own roughly half of the merged business when the merger is complete.

According to the announcement, Gulf Keystone intends to cease its London listing and transfer its principal listing to Euronext Oslo Bors’ main list.

Following the completion of the deal, the listing of ShaMaran shares will end.

The proposed combination has received unanimous approval from the boards of Gulf Keystone and ShaMaran. December will see special meetings to complete approval.

With combined estimated reserves of 323 million barrels and daily production of 53,000 barrels of oil, the merged business is expected to profit from greater size and diversity.

As part of its ambitions to increase its oil production capacity, Iraq has given many contracts to businesses from the United States, China, France, and other countries.

As Baghdad looks to boost natural gas supply and oil output, British Petroleum (BP) and its US and Turkish partners took over operations at four oilfields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk this week.

World.title: Iraq Stock Exchange records 2.5 billion IQD in weekly trading turnover
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraq Stock Exchange (ISX) reported weekly trading turnover exceeding 2.5 billion Iraqi dinars ($1.68 million) for the previous trading week, according to an official market report published on Tuesday, October 20, 2026.

Across the five trading sessions, shares of 57 joint-stock companies were actively traded out of 103 listed entities. Equities of 36 firms saw zero transactions due to pricing bid-ask disparities between buy and sell orders, while 11 companies remained suspended from trading for failing to meet mandatory corporate financial disclosure and regulatory reporting deadlines.

Trading volume expanded by 6.8% compared to the prior week, reaching 1.852 billion traded shares. However, total trading value contracted by 67% to 2.560 billion dinars, executed across 3,676 transactions. The main price benchmark, the ISX60 index, closed at 943.57 points, shedding 1.54% from its previous session close.

Foreign investment activity posted net inflows into domestic equities. Non-Iraqi investors bought 158 million shares valued at 331 million dinars over 55 contracts, while foreign selling remained muted, tallying 5 million shares worth 10 million dinars across 38 transactions.

The exchange convenes trading across five weekly sessions from Sunday through Thursday, listing 103 joint-stock enterprises spanning banking, telecommunications, industry, agriculture, insurance, financial investment, tourism, and services.

World.title: US dollar edges down across Baghdad, Basra, and Erbil Exchanges
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged down across exchange shops in Baghdad, Basra, and Erbil on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, slightly paring back gains recorded earlier in the week.

In Baghdad, foreign exchange counters registered a dip of 500 dinars per $100 compared to Monday’s trading, setting the retail selling rate at 169,000 dinars against buying bids of 168,000 dinars.

In Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, trading displayed a similar softening, with selling desks quoting 168,200 dinars per $100 and buying transactions settling at 168,000 dinars.

In the southern commercial port hub of Basra, rates slipped by 250 dinars per $100 compared to yesterday’s levels. Exchange bureaus posted retail selling rates at 168,500 dinars against purchase bids of 168,000 dinars per $100.

Parallel market activity continues to reflect a sustained premium above the Central Bank of Iraq’s official statutory peg of 152,000 dinars per $100, driven by commercial merchant demand for physical liquidity outside the central electronic clearance platform.

World.title: Rubio lands in India for ‘trade diplomacy’
World.content:
Mumbai – US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in India on Tuesday, his second official visit to the country this year, as he pursues an Asian tour blending diplomacy and trade.

Rubio visited Uzbekistan, where he called for stronger partnerships with Central Asian countries, before landing in Mumbai for talks with Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar and meetings with business leaders.

He visited New Delhi and Kolkata in May, when he also toured the Taj Mahal and met Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Modi is not scheduled to meet Rubio this time.

The top US diplomat will visit Jamnagar, in the western state of Gujarat, a port and stronghold of billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance conglomerate and its flagship refinery, the world’s largest.

He is also due to lay a wreath in memory of the 2008 Mumbai attacks that killed 166 people.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Tuesday he had also spoken to Rubio and raised issues with the US military satellite system that Ukraine uses, as well as missile delays.

Zelensky, expected in Oslo for talks with US envoys, said he told Rubio that “Starlink/Starshield needs to be restored” and that ballistic missile interceptors “are needed to protect lives”.

– ‘Energy supplies’ –

Rubio’s visit comes as India and the United States struggle to finalise a trade deal, a persistent source of friction between the two countries.

Speaking in Samarkand, Rubio said Washington and New Delhi were “very close” to an agreement.

However, a deal during his visit appears unlikely.

US President Donald Trump’s tariff war launched in April last year has added to friction over India’s imports of Russian oil and warming ties between Washington and Pakistan, India’s arch-rival.

Asked about temporary US sanctions waivers for Russian oil, of which India is a major importer, Rubio said Washington had to juggle multiple factors “including our bilateral relationships with other countries and what they realistically are capable of being able to do in terms of their own energy supplies”.

“You also can’t unravel the economy of other countries because of one central issue,” he said.

The two countries reached an interim trade agreement in February aimed at reducing US tariffs on Indian goods.

But days later, the US Supreme Court struck down Trump’s sweeping tariffs, fuelling uncertainty over when the agreement would take effect.

The two sides have been negotiating ever since.

Indian Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said this month the talks had reached “a plateau, beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult”.

Jaishankar met with his United Arab Emirates counterpart in Mumbai earlier on Tuesday. The UAE is a key supplier of Indian energy, especially liquefied natural gas (LNG).

“The situation in the Gulf remains a matter of deep concern,” Jaishankar told UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, in public comments broadcast before their meeting started.

He said India continues to support “free, safe and unimpeded flow of trade, energy and fertiliser”.

World.title: Delhi high court cites national security, junks CIC order to IAF on PMs’ foreign trips
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

has set aside a Central Information Commission order directing the

to disclose flight records pertaining to foreign visits undertaken by PM Narendra Modi and former PM Manmohan Singh, stating such disclosure could compromise national security and the PMâs safety.

Allowing a petition by the Central Public Information Officer of Directorate of Personal Services, Air Headquarters, Justice Amit Mahajan held the IAF was justified in denying access to the records under section 8 of RTI that exempts disclosure of information that could jeopardise national security or pose a risk to a personâs life and physical safety.

The high court said CIC erred in directing disclosure of Special Flight Returns (SFR-II) after redaction of the names and particulars of security personnel, observing removing such details would not necessarily eliminate the potential security risks.

The RTI plea was filed by retired Commodore Lokesh K Batra in 2018, seeking information about foreign visits by Indian PMs on IAF aircraft from April 1, 2013, until the date of his application.

In response, the IAF provided certain information about Modiâs foreign travels, and stated there had been no travel by ex-PM Singh on IAF aircraft during the period from April 1, 2013 to May 25, 2014. However, it refused to disclose copies of the SFR, Part-I and Part-II, citing national security concerns and the confidential nature of the records.





Batra approached CIC, which directed the IAF on July 8, 2020, to provide certified copies of available and relevant SFR-II records to the applicant.

The IAF challenged the CIC order, contending the records contained sensitive information that could potentially enable the identification of security personnel, reveal the composition of PMâs entourage and allow inferences to be drawn about patterns of security deployment.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and US ambassador to India Sergio Gor stand for the national anthem, as they attend a Freedom 250 reception at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai.

World.title: Police lens on Lawrence Bishnoi’s aide Randeep Malik in Tiger Shroff shooting case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Security agencies probing the attack on actor Tiger Shroff are investigating the role of

âs top-tier US-based operative Randeep Malik, notwithstanding gangster Anil Pandit claiming responsibility for it on social media.

Malik is considered very close to both Lawrence and his brother Anmol, who are also likely to be questioned in their respective jails in Gujarat and Delhi soon, sources have said.

Pandit and Shroff âs shooter Rehan both reported to Malik and were considered âhis menâ till a few months ago, a source said. Rehan had been earlier tasked by Malik and Pandit with a shooting incident in Sonipat as well.

âRehan was shown the same âAmerican dreamâ that Malik had shown Pandit in the past,â a source said.

As Pandit had been sent to California through the âDunkeyâ route months after the Siddhu Moose Wala murder, he was cited as a success story to young recruits.

Pandit used to handle âDabba callsâ for Malik till last year. In underworld parlance, âDabba callsâ refer to Voice over IP (VoIP) calls routed through speakers using multiple connected phones at different locations so that the real callerâs identity and physical location remain concealed.

World.title: Allahabad HC cites long trial, lets off offenders, SC slams ‘misplaced sympathy’
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A âgraciousâ trial court and a âvery indulgentâ Allahabad HC paved the way for two offenders in a grievous hurt case to go scotfree without spending a day in jail on the grounds that they suffered because of a 22-year-long trial, but the courts did not consider the victim, who is still getting treatment, Supreme Court has said.

Now, SC has directed the accused in the 2003 case to surrender and asked the HC to conduct a fresh hearing.

A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said it was a case of misplaced sympathy. The trial court had awarded fiveyear jail terms to the two, but the HC released them on probation. World.content:

Tuesday said US was in discussions with

on creating capacity to refine Venezuelan crude, calling India a refining superpower and underlining that Washington understood Indiaâs need to diversify its oil imports and saw Venezuela as a potential source of supply.

NEW DELHI: Govt has granted a one-year extension to Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) director-general G V G Yugandhar, with some key ongoing investigations â including Air India AI 171 crash â awaiting their final reports. The reason: Having a new DG at a time like this could delay the final report into the June 12, 2025, Ahmedabad crash. Accordingly the aviation ministry had recommended an extension for Yugandhar, who retired as Indian Air Force group captain earlier this year, and the same was approved about a month back.The key probes that are currently underway have AI 171 Air India right at the top followed by Air Indiaâs turbulent Phuket-Delhi flight of Aug 4, 2026, and some other crucial cases. AI 171 report is learnt to be in its final stage and will be shared with stakeholders as per rules once ready.People in the know say while the aviation ministry âkeeps the aircraft accident investigating agency at an armâs length and does not interfere in its working in any way,â it is taking steps to strengthen the AAIB. The bureau's lab has been recently upgraded and it now has the capability to download cockpit voice recorder and digital flight data recorder (black box) to know the conversation in the flight deck and the flight parameters till before an event being investigated.It is learnt that the aviation ministry is working on having regional offices of AAIB to ensure investigators reach the site of accident/incident at the earliest. Additionally, this is to augment the bureauâs infra at a time when Indiaâs aviation is seeing a boom right from the number of flight training schools to aircraft in fleet of Indian operators with the figure currently being close to 900.Aurobindo Handa, who was with IAF director (engineering) till Oct 2018 and then joined AAIB as DG on deputation where he remained for 3.5 years, said: âSome steps have been taken to strengthen AAIB but a lot more has to be done. The plan is to have regional offices wherever DGCA has the same. The same must be staffed by non DGCA people to avoid 'conflict of interest'. The investigatorâs execution has to be like a clockwork mechanism as its scientific reports pinpointing cause/s of accident/incident are crucial for air safety to prevent the same thing from happening again. And to achieve the outcomes, immaculate staffing is the most important function.âAAIB was formed in 2012 following an ICAO objection that the regulator (DGCA) canât be the investigator. World.title: Two Andaman, one Chhattisgarh site added to Unesco World Heritage tentative list
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Three sites from India have been added to the tentative list of United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization's World Heritage Convention, the Permanent Delegation of India to UNESCO announced on Tuesday.

The three sites are the Karst-mud-volcano Complex of Baratang and Andaman Subduction Volcanoes in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and the Sirpur Cultural and Archaeological Landscape in Chhattisgarh.

In a press release dated October 20, the Permanent Delegation of India to Unesco, based in Paris, announced the additions to India's Tentative List under the UNESCO World Heritage Convention.

Inclusion on the tentative list is a prerequisite for any property to be considered for nomination to the World Heritage List.

The delegation also acknowledged the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) for its work in the process.

The additions mark a step towards the possible future nomination of the three sites for Unesco World Heritage status.

India has 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including 37 cultural sites, seven natural sites and one mixed site, following the inscription of the ancient Buddhist site of Sarnath in July 2026.

India ranks sixth globally and second in the Asia-Pacific region.





The five countries with the highest numbers are Italy with 62 sites, China with 61, France with 56, Germany with 55 and Spain with 50.

Indiaâs first four sites were inscribed in 1983: the Ajanta Caves and Ellora Caves in Maharashtra, and Agra Fort and the Taj Mahal in Uttar Pradesh. These were all cultural sites recognised for their historical, architectural and artistic significance.

World.title: Shinde calls INDIA bloc ‘ten-headed Ravana’, accuses Uddhav of ‘vote theft’
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister

on Tuesday accused

of stealing the people's mandate after the 2019 assembly elections and called the INDIA bloc a âten-mouthed Ravanaâ whose effigy should be burnt.

Addressing his party's Dussehra rally in Mumbai, Shinde attacked the opposition over its allegations of vote theft, accused it of undermining constitutional institutions and said the government would support farmers facing crop losses due to water scarcity.

Without naming Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray, Shinde alleged that the actual âvote theftâ took place after the 2019 Maharashtra assembly elections, when the undivided Shiv Sena joined hands with the NCP and Congress to form a government.

âYou did not even contest the election. You made a backdoor entry and became chief minister. You stabbed the mandate and grabbed the post. It was a huge dacoity against the people's mandate,â he said.

Shinde questioned the opposition's allegations of irregularities in electoral rolls, saying it had earlier raised concerns over an increase in voter numbers and was now questioning the deletion of names.

âThis is double standards and a daily show of new drama. The INDIA bloc is a ten-mouthed Ravana, and we need to burn its effigy,â he said, accusing the opposition of seeking to undermine the Constitution drafted by Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar.





He also questioned why the opposition had not alleged vote theft when the INDIA bloc won elections in Telangana, Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh. âWhen you lose, you call it vote chori and start alleging foul play. The INDIA bloc won elections in Telangana, Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh. Why was there no vote chori then?â he asked.

Shinde accused the Congress of looting the country for 70 years and alleged that it was now demanding ballot papers after previously winning elections through booth capturing.

He also hit out at opposition leaders for their remarks on regime changes in Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka, accusing them of encouraging anarchy in India.

âThis is Hindustan, a new India. This is an India that enters Pakistan,â he said, adding that people would teach a lesson to those he described as anti-national.

Questioning the opposition's criticism of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah, Shinde said Modi had made India the world's fourth-largest economy and received the highest civilian awards from 36 countries.

He also claimed there was no corruption case against the prime minister.

âWhy use such foul and low language against our PM?â he asked.

Shinde further accused opposition leaders of speaking in Pakistan's favour and alleged that their statements were being used to create headlines there. Referring to Captain Smit Machchhar, who saved a plane during an attack, he said the pilot had acknowledged drawing inspiration from Modi.

Shinde claimed that Modi, the US president and the Israeli prime minister had congratulated the pilot, while some opposition leaders had not.

âWhatever they say here becomes a headline in Pakistan. This is a huge conspiracy...Why do you speak in favour of Pakistan? This is unfortunate. This is sedition and not any kind of love for India,â he alleged.

The deputy chief minister also criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for organising a rally against the Supreme Court, alleging that it amounted to an insult to the judiciary and an attack on a constitutional institution.

âOn the one hand, they hold the Constitution in their hands, and on the other, their actions amount to an attack on it. They are moving towards dividing the country,â he said.

Taking a swipe at the opposition's demand for the election of the chief election commissioner, Shinde sarcastically asked whether it would also seek elections for the chief justice of India and municipal corporation chiefs.

He alleged that opposition parties were promoting a âfake narrativeâ of vote theft through rallies in Mumbai while farmers were struggling with crop losses.

Turning to the agrarian crisis, Shinde said Maharashtra was facing drought-like conditions as standing crops dried up due to a weak monsoon. He announced that he had dispatched an initial 100 tonnes of foodgrains to distressed farmers as an advance Diwali gift, with more consignments to follow.

âToday, I have dispatched the first tranche of 100 tonnes of foodgrains to farmers as an advance Diwali gift. There will be more such rounds of assistance given to farmers,â he said.

Shinde said excessive rainfall had washed away land last year, causing serious losses to crops and cattle. This year, the monsoon had failed to provide adequate relief to farmers, he added.

âUnfortunately, this year, the monsoon turned its back on farmers. We reached out to distressed farmers who are shedding tears and offered them consolation. This is not the time to politicise the farmers' plight but to extend support to them,â he said.

World.title: Rising Crimes And Farmer’s Plight Dominate Conversations at 60th Shiv Sena (UBT) Dussera Rally
World.content:
The Shiv Sena held its 60th Dussehra rally on Tuesday (October 20, 2026), with the Uddhav Thackeray (UBT) faction organising it in Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park in Dadar, while the Eknath-Shinde-led faction held the rally at NESCO in Goregaon. Party supporters from various districts of Maharashtra participated, with senior party supporters still chanting “Thackeray is Mumbai, Thackeray is Maharashtra.”

Rising Crimes Remains a Major Concern

Speaking to The Hindu, several participants of the rally raised concerns about rising criminal activities in the State. “It’s happening in Mumbai, it’s happening in Thane. It was Purnekar last month. It was Tiger Shroff yesterday. Tomorrow it will be the common man like you and I,” a party supporter from Jalgaon taluka, who requested anonymity, said.

Participants also raised concerns about farmers’ plights, unemployment, and rising inflation, stating that the State government and officials had fallen short of supporting the poorest of the poor sections of society and had not delivered on the promises they had made.

Supporters Look Beyond Party Lines

Amid rising political dissent against the State and union governments, rally participants said that the party (Shiv Sena-UBT) will continue to support those who stand with the people. “We stand by the cockroaches (Cockroach Janata Party) and officials like Tukaram Mundhe, IAS. The government has let the rich get richer, and the poor remain poor,” said Anil Nagnath Vyavahare, 65, who was attending the rally.

Participants also noted that the officials in authority and those in power have still not delivered justice to the students who faced paper leaks in the MPSC, UPSC, and NEET examinations. They said that if the government continues to support gangster activities and tries to manipulate the Indian Constitution and its judiciary, it will soon lose its power, and in the next election, the people will choose those who understand them and stand for their betterment.

World.title: Delhi High Court imposes ₹1 cost on Niva Bupa over ₹5 crore suit against influencer
World.content:
The Delhi High Court has imposed a token cost of ₹1 on Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited for invoking its Intellectual Property Division to pursue a ₹5 crore suit against social media influencer Vishal Rattewal over allegedly disparaging posts, holding that the dispute did not involve trademark infringement.

Justice Anup J. Bhambhani, in an order passed on September 21, observed that merely using an insurance company’s name or trademark to identify it in social media posts did not, in the circumstances of the case, amount to trademark infringement.

Niva Bupa had approached the court seeking the removal of allegedly disparaging posts published in late August this year by Mr. Rattewal on Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and X.

It submitted that Mr. Rattewal, a social media influencer and content creator with a substantial following, had deliberately used its distinctive name, trademarks, logo and other brand identifiers, including ‘NIVA BUPA’, prominently in the titles, thumbnails, captions, visual presentation and content of his publications. The company alleged that he had simultaneously associated the brand with allegations of “fraud, dishonesty, deception, and unfair trade practices”.

It sought an apology, ₹5 crore in damages and litigation costs, alleging that the content had harmed its reputation and infringed its registered trademark.

The dispute stemmed from a consumer complaint filed by Mr. Neeraj Kumar against the insurer before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Charkhi Dadri, Haryana. In an order passed on October 9, 2024, the commission ruled in Mr. Kumar’s favour and made certain observations concerning medical insurance companies.

Niva Bupa alleged that Mr. Rattewal subsequently published offensive and disparaging content about the company in connection with the consumer proceedings.

In this backdrop, Niva Bupa contended that, by publishing allegedly offensive content on his social media accounts, Mr. Rattewal has infringed its registered trade mark by harming its reputation in India.

The court, however, held that Mr. Rattewal was neither engaged in the insurance business nor connected with it. Using Niva Bupa’s name or trademark to identify the company in the alleged posts did not amount to use “in the course of trade” or constitute infringement under the Trade Marks Act, it said.

“In the opinion of this court, this suit is not maintainable before the Intellectual Property Division of this court, since it is not a matter relating to infringement of any intellectual property right of either of the plaintiffs,” the court held.

After the court dictated its order returning the plaint, Niva Bupa sought permission to withdraw the suit and pursue its claims through an ordinary civil action. The court allowed the request, granting them liberty to file a fresh suit on the same cause of action, subject to payment of ₹1 as costs to Mr. Rattewal.

World.title: Left parties should sell books from party offices, not at Durga Puja pandals, says West Bengal CM
World.content:
Amidst the ongoing controversy surrounding attacks on book stalls of Left parties at Durga Puja pandals, West Bengal Chief Minister on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) said that Left parties should sell books from their party offices in the State instead of setting up book stalls at Durga Puja pandals.

Also Read: Left parties allege attack on bookstalls; Calcutta High Court stays previous order allowing stalls

“Those who do not believe in Durga Pujas or any other Pujas, it is better that they should not be allowed to sell books during Durga Puja. Keep the books inside your party offices, make a library and sell books from there. There are 4,000 to 5,000 party offices like palaces in the State and all of them are open,” Mr. Adhikari said.

The Chief Minister tried to emphasise that since Left parties do not believe in Hindu festivals and rituals they should not have book stalls at Durga Puja pandals.

While Mr. Adikari said that no one should take law in their hands, he said all the action by the administration was as per directions of Calcutta High Court. The remarks by the Chief Minister come at a time after a section of leaders of his own party condemned attacks on the book stalls set up by the Left parties at Durga Puja pandals.

On Monday (October 19), Jishnu Basu, a prominent RSS leader from West Bengal, said that there is no valour in vandalising book stalls and those indulging in such acts are cowards. West Bengal Finance Minister Swapan Dasgupta had also said that he cannot support what was happening in connection with the Left parties’ book stalls. West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya denied involvement of any party worker in the vandalism of book stalls and said that action will be taken against if any from the party is responsible in the vandalism.

Book stalls set up by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) and SUCI (Communist) have been attacked in various parts of the state including in the city. On October 17, supporters of Left parties formed a human chain to prevent a bulldozer to raze down a temporary book stall in Kolkata’s Jadavapur area.

The CPI(M) had moved the Calcutta High Court, alleging that authorities of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation and police attempted to remove a temporary bookstall set up by the party in Jadavpur during the Durga Puja festivities. The Calcutta High Court on Tuesday refused to interfere in a case by the CPI(M) over attempts by the police to remove a temporary book stall set up by the party in Jadavpur during the Durga Puja festivities. The court had said that a division bench of the High Court had already dealt with the matter in connection with a temporary book stall at Bongaon. While a single-judge bench of the Calcutta High Court had allowed the stall at Bongaon, a division bench led by Chief Justice R.V. Ghuge had stayed the order.

Senior leaders of the Left parties had held a press conference alleging a clampdown on the book stalls across the State. West Bengal CPI(M) State Secretary Md. Salim said that the books are just an excuse the party in power has decided a crackdown on anything related to education and culture.

World.title: Two arrested for possessing a country-made gun in Namakkal
World.content:
Two, including a marine engineer, were arrested for possessing a country-made gun in Namakkal on Tuesday (October 20, 2026).

Acting on a tip-off, the Rasipuram police engaged in vehicle checks at Onankaradu on Tuesday (October 20). While checking a two-wheeler, they found a country-made gun and 12 rubber bullets in a bag. The police nabbed the two who travelled on the two-wheeler and identified them as B. Natarajan (46), a resident of Malaiyalapatti in Perumbalur district, a marine engineer, and his friend Marimuthu (45). The police registered a case and arrested the duo and remanded them in prison.

World.title: Dasara gift for Singareni officers, Dy CM fulfils long-pending demand
World.content:
In a major Dasara gift to Singareni officers, the Telangana government has fulfilled a long-pending demand by approving a revision of pay scales for executive cadre employees of the Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) on the lines of Coal India. The decision, announced following the intervention of Deputy Chief Minister and Energy Minister Bhatti Vikramarka, is expected to benefit nearly 1,800 officers from Executive Cadres E-1 to E-7.

Singareni management issued orders on Monday evening (October 19, 2026) implementing the revised pay structure after securing the approval of the company’s Board. The orders were issued by Director (Personnel) Gautam Potru.

According to the notification, the revised basic pay scales will take retrospective effect from January 1, 2017. However, the financial benefits arising from the revision will be applicable from September 25, 2026, the date on which the Singareni Board approved the proposal. Officers will begin receiving revised salaries from the October pay cycle.

Under the revised structure, the basic pay for E-1 cadre officers has been increased from ₹40,000 to ₹60,000, while E-2 officers will receive ₹70,000 instead of ₹50,000. The pay for E-3 has been revised from ₹60,000 to ₹80,000 and for E-4 from ₹70,000 to ₹90,000. E-5 officers will now draw a basic pay of ₹1 lakh against the earlier ₹80,000. The pay scales of E-6 and E-7 cadres have been revised to ₹1.2 lakh from ₹90,000 and ₹1 lakh respectively.

The decision follows demands raised by Singareni officers after Coal India approved a revised pay structure for its executives to address disparities and align salaries with those of Maharatna public sector enterprises. Seeking parity, Singareni officers approached the state government and requested implementation of a similar structure in SCCL.

Responding to the request, Mr Bhatti Vikramarka directed the Singareni management in July to expedite the examination of the proposal and ensure that officers received favourable news before Dasara. A committee was subsequently constituted to study the issue and submit recommendations. Based on the committee’s report and Board approval, the revised pay scales were cleared.

Leaders of the Singareni Officers’ Association welcomed the decision and thanked Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and Deputy Chief Minister Bhatti Vikramarka for honouring their commitment. Officers said the move would boost morale and motivate them to contribute more effectively to coal production, energy security and Telangana’s industrial growth.

The pay revision comes close on the heels of the state government’s recent announcement of a ₹596-crore Dasara bonus for nearly 39,000 Singareni workers and employees. The government had also announced a bonus of ₹5,500 each for contract workers. With the latest salary revision for officers, the government has extended festival benefits across all major sections of the Singareni workforce, marking a significant morale booster for the coal major and its employees.

World.title: Rubio pushes for India to buy more U.S., Venezuelan oil
World.content:
Calling India a “refining superpower”, United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he had discussed possible Indian oil purchases from the U.S. during talks with External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar on Tuesday (October 20, 2026). He will also discuss a plan for more Venezuelan oil to be refined at the Mukesh Ambani-owned Reliance Energy plant in Jamnagar, he added.

Mr. Rubio added that India and the U.S. are “very, very close” to wrapping up negotiations on a much-delayed free trade agreement (FTA).

Energy ties, trade, and connectivity were on the agenda as Mr. Jaishankar hosted Mr. Rubio and United Arab Emirates Foreign Minister Abdullah Bin Zayed in Mumbai. The External Affairs Minister met with each of his counterparts separately, and then held a meeting with both of them together, indicating that trilateral cooperation on the issues was also discussed.

Trilateral cooperation

Mr. Jaishankar called the trilateral meeting a “useful exchange of perspectives on energy, connectivity and contemporary developments”.

“The U.S., India, and UAE have real opportunities to advance cooperation on energy, trade, technology, and regional connectivity,” said U.S. Ambassador to India Sergio Gor, sharing a photograph of the three Foreign Ministers together in Mumbai.

However, the readouts made no mention of plans for the “I2U2” that the three countries formed with Israel in 2021 or the India-Middle East Economic Corridor (IMEC) that was announced in 2023.

‘Very, very close to FTA’

Mr. Rubio’s visit comes at a time of tension in India-U.S. ties due to several issues, including the U.S.’s recent moves to stop H-1B visas, threatened sanctions (that have since been held off) over India’s import of Russian oil, and delayed FTA negotiations.

“We’re very, very close. I would say we’re about as close as you can be without having executed the [free trade] agreement. I think there’s a small number of items left to wrap up, so I think that will happen shortly,” Mr. Rubio said, adding that the State Department was closely involved with the negotiations between trade officials.

The India-U.S.-UAE trilateral meeting, which was not earlier announced by the MEA, comes at a time when the UAE is also facing many challenges in energy exports and trade due to the U.S. war in Iran and Tehran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Mr. Jaishankar met Mr. Abdullah in Mumbai just four days after he had travelled to Abu Dhabi where the two Foreign Ministers had also spent time together.

‘Strong strategic partner’

This is Mr. Rubio’s second visit to India in five months after his last visit to Delhi for the Quad Foreign Ministers meeting in May this year. This time around, Mr. Rubio’s focus is on the economic side of the bilateral relationship, officials said.

There have been questions raised about Mr. Rubio’s planned two-day visit to Jamnagar, as well as criticism that he had “summoned” Mr. Jaishankar to Mumbai rather than travelling to meet him in Delhi. Speaking to journalists at the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel in Mumbai, where he and Mr. Jaishankar offered tributes to those who were killed in the 26/11 terror attacks, Mr. Rubio fielded questions over the purpose of his visit, and why he had returned to India so soon.

“First of all, I will point out that the Foreign Minister of India [Mr. Jaishankar] has been to the United States four times this year,” Mr. Rubio explained, adding that as the most populous country and largest democracy that is a trade and defence partner, a “strong strategic partner” and a Quad member, India is an important country to interact with.

Reviving Reliance’s Venezuelan link

He explained that his visit to Jamnagar, where he will see the Reliance energy refinery and the Vantara animal facility, was in order to discuss more Venezuelan oil being brought to the refinery. “We’ve talked to them [Reliance Energy] about it in the past. We’re going to go see what the holdup is and what opportunities exist. We’ll see how the conversation goes. This is a company that has had a presence in Venezuela in the past and whose refining capabilities are substantial,” he added.

When asked about India’s purchase of Russian oil that makes up about 45% to 50% of its intake, Mr. Rubio said that he was “happy” to see India has made “substantial progress” on diversifying its oil purchases, adding that the U.S. and Venezuela can be the source of more energy inputs to India. Last month, oil from Russia, the U.S., and Venezuela made up two-thirds of India’s oil imports.

(with inputs from Vinaya Deshpande in Mumbai)

World.title: Iran security chief rejects moving enriched uranium out of country
World.content:
Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) told the visiting Pakistani army chief Asim Munir that Tehran would not allow nuclear material to leave the country, according to state TV.

"Not even a tiny bit of enriched nuclear material will leave Iran; such materials constitute a major asset and national wealth for the Iranian people, intended for use within the country," said Mr. Rezaei, Iran's secretary of the Supreme National Security Council.

"There will be no negotiations until America takes steps to build trust — a process that must begin with the fulfilment of Iran's conditions," he added.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian also rejected the idea of negotiations under U.S. threats during his meeting with Munir, who is in Tehran as part of a renewed push to mediate a peace deal between the Islamic republic and the United States.

"The Americans must first remove the threats and sanctions; only then can we engage in dialogue," he said.

"Today, our nation does not trust America. It believes that if we enter the negotiations, they [the Americans] will attack us again."

Iran's chief negotiator and parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf made similar remarks to Munir.

"We have nothing new to say; America cannot gain Iran's trust unless it fulfils the seven conditions," said Mr. Ghalibaf, noting that "threats and military manoeuvres cannot influence Iran's strategic decisions".

Iran has demanded, among other things, a ceasefire across West Asia, the unfreezing of its assets abroad and the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector.

The West Asia war was sparked in late February by the United States and Israel when they launched a wave of surprise attacks on Iran, while Washington and Tehran were in the midst of negotiations on Iran's nuclear programme.

The warring parties agreed a memorandum of understanding in June that was expected to create a framework for a permanent resolution to the conflict, but the deal did not last long.

Negotiations have effectively been at an impasse since then, and recent indirect talks between the U.S. and Iran on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly failed to produce a breakthrough.

Tehran had previously maintained it would not hand over its nuclear materials — enriched to 60%, close to the atomic bomb threshold of 90% — to any country but had hinted at the possibility of diluting them within Iran's borders.

Washington and its allies have imposed waves of sanctions on Iran, accusing it of seeking to build nuclear weapons, a charge Tehran has long denied.

World.title: Zelensky, U.S. envoys hold Oslo talks as Ukraine claims U.S. missile holdup
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky held talks in Oslo with top U.S. envoys on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) in a bid to get strained relations with Washington "on a more constructive path", Norway said.

"Ukraine is working for peace. I thank our partners for their support!" Mr. Zelensky said in a social media post after his arrival in the Norwegian capital.

Mr. Zelensky handed U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff an award in the Norwegian government's official residence, before posing with Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Finnish President Alexander Stubb, according to footage accompanying the Ukrainian leader's post.

Mr. Witkoff's fellow U.S. envoy Jared Kushner — U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law — was also taking part in the negotiations but was doing so remotely because of illness, according to the NTB agency.

Relations between Kyiv and Washington have soured since Mr. Trump partially lifted sanctions to strike a diesel-supply deal with Russia's Vladimir Putin and slammed Mr. Zelensky as a warmonger for Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries.

Mr. Zelensky has accused the United States of deliberately withholding vital intelligence and delaying military aid, saying on Monday (October 19) that Ukraine received no early warning of powerful Russian missile strikes that targeted energy facilities in the capital region.

U.S.-led diplomatic efforts to end Europe's deadliest conflict since World War II have stalled in recent months, as Washington has shifted focus towards the war with Iran.

The Norway talks were set to continue into the evening, Store told reporters, with he and Mr. Zelensky set to give a press conference around 7:15 p.m. (1715 GMT)

"The aim is to put diplomatic efforts on a more constructive path," he said.

'Needed to protect lives'

Ahead of the meeting, Mr. Zelensky said on Tuesday (October 20) he held "substantive" and "constructive" talks with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in which he insisted that the U.S. military satellite system Ukraine uses, Starshield, "needs to be restored" and that ballistic missile interceptors "are needed to protect lives".

Mr. Zelensky told U.S. senators on Monday (October 20) that "the Pentagon is delaying the delivery of missiles" already paid for by European countries, and that the shipment was waiting for U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's signature.

He said several European countries were ready to transfer Patriot interceptor missiles from their own stockpiles but were still awaiting U.S. approval.

The United States has denied making any changes to intelligence sharing with Ukraine, and Mr. Rubio said on Tuesday (October 20) that Washington was not deliberately withholding supplies.

"There's nothing being deliberately denied to Ukraine," Mr. Rubio said while on a trip to India.

"It's simply, it's a balance between our obligations to other partners and frankly our own... requirements for our own facilities as well."

Mr. Trump has also denied ordering a reduction in speeds on the US government-owned and—controlled Starshield network after Elon Musk, whose company SpaceX developed it, said the order could only have come from the White House.

Strained relations

The U.S. leader has accused his counterpart of not trying to resolve the conflict with Russia. "Mr. Zelensky doesn't know what he's talking about," President Trump said on Monday (October 19).

"To be honest, I think it's time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine."

Mr. Trump said he was ready to meet Mr. Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in China next month to discuss denuclearisation, adding that talks could also cover the Ukraine war — fuelling fears in Kyiv that it was being sidelined.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed earlier that "the topic of such a hypothetical has indeed been mentioned" when asked about a Wall Street Journal report on Sunday (October 18) that U.S. President Trump, Russia’s President Putin and China’s President Xi could meet.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga said that such a meeting would "only encourage Putin to continue this war".

News outlet Axios reported that Mr. Witkoff would travel from Oslo to Russia to meet Putin.

"We hope that it will be possible to arrange a meeting in the very near future, allowing the American negotiators... Mr. Witkoff to brief President Putin on their contacts with both the Ukrainians and the Europeans," Mr. Peskov told reporters on Tuesday (October 20).

World.title: Judicial commission points finger at police’s ‘epic failure’, says Mir Raza was murdered
World.content:
KARACHI: A judicial commission formed to investigate the circumstances and possible negligence in businessman Mir Raza Ali’s murder case has pointed out the police’s “epic failure” in their investigation.

The Sindh cabinet decided to make the report public during a meeting chaired by Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah earlier in the day. The judicial commission, which began its proceedings on Aug 28, held regular hearings to record statements of several individuals linked to the case.

“ This case demonstrates an epic failure by the police in their investigation ,” declared the 62-page report submitted by Sindh High Court’s (SHC) Justice Omar Sial, who had been heading the judicial panel.

“The police breached all required procedures, both knowingly and unknowingly, necessary to withstand judicial scrutiny and a successful prosecution,” the report stated.

While acknowledging that the initial police response when they were informed of the presence of a body was prompt, the report noted that subsequent events “left a lot to be desired”.

“It was a murder,” the report declared.

It explained that the bullet trajectory, the unusual location of the wound if it had been a self-inflicted injury, the “absence of blood, the state of the body, the principles of medical jurisprudence, acid burns and the anaesthesia detected in the blood all clearly excluded suicide as the cause of death”.

The commission determined that releasing the police findings before a proper investigation was “premature and fell short of professional standards”.

“Even if the death had been a suicide, the police should have established who was responsible for driving a young man to that point, including whether coercion, blackmail, or instigation was involved. They made no such effort.”

It said the police investigation “failed in its most basic duty: to establish the truth” .

It further observed that “incessant public criticism of the police created problems” as the police “went into a shell, completely broke down communication channels, and took a position based on ego rather than on cogent, solid reasons”.

The report pointed out specific issues with the police conduct: “Lack of leadership, seriousness, and supervision, and, in some cases, negligence by the senior officers. The handling of this case has been like a rudderless ship, not aware of its destination.

“Ranging from negligent to criminally negligent, inexplicable, casual, and unprofessional investigation.”

According to the commission, an active cover-up in the initial stages of the investigation cannot be conclusively ruled out . It noted that senior police officers swept clear investigative lapses under the carpet, without acknowledging them, addressing them, or even attempting to do so.

“Too many cooks spoil the broth. The proverb is applicable to this case as far as the police are concerned,” the judicial commission observed.

“Dozens of police officers – authorised and unauthorised – were involved in collecting evidence in this case, approaching and interrogating crucial persons, and in most cases not documenting it in any manner,” it said, adding that therefore, no officer was willing to take responsibility for the lapses .

The inquiry said there was a need to mitigate public speculation by an “honest and timely briefing on the investigation”, but this was not done, and the family or the public were not updated through official disclosures.

“The police did not follow the commission’s recommendation to appoint a focal person for this reason. As a result, public speculation further embarrassed the government and the police.”

Regarding the controversy over the reconstitution of a medical board formed for the exhumation of Ali’s body, the report said: “The overnight bureaucratic manoeuvring was a highly irregular, inexplicable, legally flawed overreach dictated entirely from the upper echelons of the Sindh Health Secretariat, more specifically by the secretary and special secretary, Health.”

It added that the Health Services director general, “being aware that he was not legally competent to form a medical board for exhumation, looked the other way”.

“The two gentlemen who directed the change in the board could not give a cogent reason for the abrupt change, making it extremely controversial, fueling public speculation, and embarrassing the Sindh government.”

Referring to an Aug 9 meeting held at CM House, which “drew considerable speculation and controversy”, the report said that “no ulterior motive can be inferred from this meeting”. The meeting was attended by Medico-Legal Officer (MLO) Dr Osama Sheikh, who conducted Ali’s first autopsy, the Karachi police chief and other senior officials.

Observations on officials

Listing its observations for certain police officials involved in the case, the judicial panel identified “criminal negligence” on the part of Station House Officer (SHO) Adeel Afzal of Ferozabad police station.

“Initiate a comprehensive inquiry into him, leading to dismissal from service. He should be suspended in the interim. He must also be questioned to determine whether he has facilitated the destruction of key evidence,” the report read.

It also found criminal negligence by Sub-inspector Shabbir Leghari, the first investigating officer (IO) in the case, and called for disciplinary proceedings against him and his suspension.

The report also determined criminal negligence of Inspector Ghaus, but did not recommend any action against him.

Regarding DIG Farukh Lanjar and Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Samiullah Soomro, the commission noted a “lack of leadership and supervision”.

The judicial panel also called out “extreme immaturity” and “childish behaviour” of MLO Sheikh , who conducted the first medico-legal examination, whose findings were later proven incorrect after a second autopsy.

“Overconfidence. Unprofessional conduct not befitting a medical professional. Must not be assigned medico-legal duties unless he has undergone at least two years of rigorous academic and practical training.”

The report said he was “possibly influenced” and called for the angle to be “conclusively determined”.

Suicide vs murder

The report also said a voice note provided by Alishaz Mushtaq to police was “one of the most suspicious parts of this case”. It said that Mushtaq and ASP Nida Junaid, “played a very important role in supporting the police narrative that the death was due to suicide”.

It said that the person Mushtaq named as his source did not corroborate the information he provided, raising suspicion regarding his conduct.

It further said that the WhatsApp messages Ali sent to Sarim Bin Tahir asking for Rs30m, which was “full of uncharacteristic grammatical errors and truncated spellings and read as acute panic”, suggested the deceased was being “blackmailed or threatened”.

It also noted that while CCTV footage showed Ali with a pistol on the night he was killed, this was “unusual”.

“All his close friends and associates told the Commission that Raza did not possess or use pistols. They said he would probably not even know how to handle one. Witnesses also vouched for his peace-loving, calm, and gentle demeanour. Why he took the pistol remained a mystery. The pistol, however, has not been found to date,” it said.

It further said: “The known financial distress was also not of such a nature that would lead a person to suicide. Ali’s behaviour, until the ride-hailing service dropped him off, did not suggest he was ready to take an extreme step for this reason.”

Recommendations

Suggesting the next steps, the judicial commission said accommodating the family’s request for a joint investigation team (JIT) was the “most viable path to mitigate ongoing reputational damage to the Government of Sindh”.

It recommended that a JIT be constituted under the leadership of Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Irfan Baloch to “balance the need for public accountability with preserving Sindh Police morale and reputation”.

The report said the team should “integrate senior representatives from the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Intelligence Bureau (IB), Pakistan Rangers (Sindh), and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) to ensure an impartial, comprehensive, and credible resolution.

“This extreme step is necessary to restore public trust and end speculation,” it stressed.

The commission contended that any subsequent police actions will inevitably face heavy public speculation, determining that the police department “bears responsibility for this profound trust deficit between itself and society”.

“Even an accurate conclusion or the apprehension of the true culprit is unlikely to be accepted by the public,” it added.

The report pointed out that the case could now “only be resolved through a rigorous, intelligence-based investigation as a “significant portion of physical evidence has been compromised” .

It called for the police to “transparently acknowledge and apologise for past operational lapses”, as well as immediately initiate formal inquiries against the responsible officers in light of the report.

While stating that it did not have investigative powers and that it was difficult to conclude conclusively that an active cover-up occurred, the commission noted that “certain inexplicable actions are difficult to justify and raise the possibility that one may have occurred”.

Therefore, it suggested that a high-level committee, preferably led by the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA), be constituted to initiate criminal action against any police officials it finds culpable.

The committee would inquire into “whether any of the police officials involved in this probe in the first 10 days” were in breach of sections 201 (causing disappearance of evidence of offence), 166(2) (public servant disobeying law, with intent to cause injury) and 218 (public servant framing incorrect record or writing with intent to save person from punishment) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC).

The judicial commission also called for initiating police reforms, particularly to address and modernise the investigation protocol.

It suggested forming a committee of “seasoned professionals” to “specifically address first response, crime scene handling, medico-legal dynamics, collection, safekeeping, and analysis of evidence, and recording the entirety of the investigation in written or digital form”.

While it proposed a three-month timeframe for the exercise, the commission said the Sindh government will make the final decision.

Another suggestion was to consider an increase in the investigation budget, with a protocol in place to monitor the fund’s use. The panel further suggested steps regarding training of investigators and enhancing the capacity of Crime Scene Units.

Panel formed to ensure implementation

The judicial panel’s primary mandate was to determine the facts and circumstances of the case; assess whether police and medico-legal investigations were impartial; identify professional negligence, misconduct, evidence manipulation, or cover-ups; review digital/forensic evidence; and recommend further investigation, forensic analysis, or legal/departmental action.
